docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Gurobi is a commercial linear, mixed-integer, and quadratic programming solver used widely on large energy-system optimisation models. FlexTool writes each solve's model to an MPS file and runs Gurobi's command-line solver gurobi_cl on it in a separate process (found on PATH, or in ~/gurobi/bin), passing every parameter as a Name=value argument. FlexTool never inspects a licence: the licence-discovery path is Gurobi's own.

Official site: https://www.gurobi.com/

docs.title: License options
docs.text:
• Commercial. Named-user, floating, and machine licences via the Gurobi sales channel.
  • Academic. Free for students, faculty, and staff at recognised degree-granting institutions. Renewable annually from an academic IP.
  • Free trial. Time-limited evaluation licence available from the Gurobi website with vendor sign-off.
  • WLS (Web Licence Service). Cloud-friendly token-based licensing for containers, CI, and shared infrastructure.

Licence acquisition page: https://www.gurobi.com/solutions/licensing/

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the Python wrapper:

pip install gurobipy

gurobipy lets FlexTool detect Gurobi at start ("Solvers:" line); the solve itself runs gurobi_cl, which comes with the Gurobi installation.

After installing the wrapper, set up a licence file. The simplest single-machine path:

  1. Sign in at https://www.gurobi.com/ and request a licence appropriate for your situation (commercial, academic, or trial).
  2. Use Gurobi's grbgetkey tool, or the equivalent web flow, to download a gurobi.lic file.
  3. Place gurobi.lic at either of:
  4. $HOME/gurobi.lic (user-scoped, the simplest), or
  5. /opt/gurobi/gurobi.lic (system-wide), or
  6. any path of your choice, then set the GRB_LICENSE_FILE environment variable to that path.

WLS and Compute Server users set up the licence the way gurobi_cl reads it (a gurobi.lic with the WLS credentials, or GRB_LICENSE_FILE). Server, cloud and licence parameters (ComputeServer, CS..., Cloud..., WLS..., TokenServer, ...) are taken from solver_config/gurobi.opt only: the input database's solver_arguments may not set them (see What the database may set).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After installing gurobipy, run:

python -c "from polar_high.solvers import available_solvers; print(available_solvers)"

Expected: 'gurobi' appears in the printed list:

['gurobi', 'cplex', 'xpress', 'copt', 'highs']

gurobi in the list confirms only that the wrapper is importable — licence discovery still happens at solve time. To check that the licence is also working, point FlexTool at any small Gurobi-targeted scenario and run it; or, outside FlexTool:

python -c "import gurobipy as gp; gp.Model().optimize()"

A clean exit (no GurobiError) means the licence is found.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text:
FlexTool runs Gurobi as the gurobi_cl command-line program. When it fails, FlexTool stops the run with a FlexToolUserError whose message includes gurobi_cl's own output (its stdout and stderr), so Gurobi's text is in the FlexTool log.

  • No licence, or the licence check failed. gurobi_cl exits with an error and prints, for example, "No Gurobi license found". FlexTool shows: "Solver 'gurobi' subprocess failed a license check. Details: 'gurobi' CLI for solve '' exited with returncode=... --- stdout --- ..." (see License options). Fix by placing the gurobi.lic file in your home folder (or /opt/gurobi/) or by setting GRB_LICENSE_FILE in the environment FlexTool runs in.
  • Licence expired. The same message, with Gurobi's text "License has expired". Renew the licence through the Gurobi web portal.
  • gurobi_cl not found. "Solver 'gurobi' CLI binary is not installed on this system." Install Gurobi and put gurobi_cl on the PATH.
  • Unknown Gurobi parameter. A misspelt name in solver_arguments or gurobi.opt (e.g. MIPGapp) is ignored by Gurobi, which prints Unknown parameter: 'MIPGapp' (ignored) and solves on. FlexTool repeats it as a warning naming where the parameter was set (the option file, or the solver_arguments of which solve). Fix the name. With console logging off (LogToConsole 0) Gurobi prints no such line, and there is no warning.
  • File parameters. Parameters that name a file or folder (LogFile, SolFiles, NodefileDir, InputFile, the .prm / .json file lists of tuning, concurrent and multi-objective runs) take a full path in gurobi.opt; in the database's solver_arguments they take only a plain file name, written in the solve's work folder, and a path is refused. See What the database may set. ResultFile is ignored everywhere (with a warning): FlexTool names its own result file and reads the solution from it.
  • Time limit reached. A MIP stopped at its time limit with a solution is kept with a warning that gives the gap reached; an LP, or a MIP without a solution, stops the run. See Time limit.

docs.title: How to set it in FlexTool
docs.text:
On the solve entity for the solve you want Gurobi to handle:

solve_advanced.solver         = "gurobi"
solve_advanced.solver_mip_gap = 0.005
solve_advanced.solver_arguments:
  Method     = 2
  Presolve   = 2
  MIPFocus   = 1

flextool <input_db_url> --solver-time-limit 60 --solver-mip-gap 0.001

--solver-time-limit 60 reaches Gurobi as TimeLimit=60 and --solver-mip-gap 0.001 as MIPGap=0.001, over the solve's solver_mip_gap (0.005) and any MIPGap in solver_arguments or gurobi.opt. Without the flags, solver_mip_gap gives MIPGap=0.005, and a MIPGap (or mipgap: names match without regard to case) in solver_arguments wins over it. The thread count comes from Threads in gurobi.opt (--threads and --highs-threads do not change it). The run prints what Gurobi receives, for example:

Solver args (gurobi): Threads=1, MIPGap=0.001, LogToConsole=1, Method=2, Presolve=2, MIPFocus=1, TimeLimit=60

Verified install on: [empty]

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
HiGHS is the high-performance, open-source linear programming, mixed-integer programming, and quadratic programming solver developed at the University of Edinburgh. It is the default solver in FlexTool and the only one that ships with the FlexTool installation — no separate setup, no licence, no environment variables. Every FlexTool scenario that does not explicitly set the solver parameter runs on HiGHS.

Internally FlexTool runs HiGHS via one of two paths:

  • Warm-active path — the default for cascade runs. Builds and solves each sub-solve in-process with highspy.Highs; the built model is re-solved for the next sub-solve only when that sub-solve is identical (same data, same labels, same solver settings). Rolls of a rolling solve are always built anew.
  • Subprocess path — for cold solves, --save-memory, and single-solve invocations. FlexTool writes the LP to a temporary MPS via the polar-high polars→MPS writer, then runs python -m flextool.cli.cmd_solve_mps in a clean child process so HiGHS' simplex/IPM working set lives outside the FlexTool address space. The retired in-process cold-HiGHS path is no longer reachable from the orchestrator — set FLEXTOOL_SAVE_MEMORY=1 explicitly to silence the soft-promote warning on the cold path.

Official site: https://highs.dev/

docs.title: License options
docs.text: • Free and open source under the MIT licence. No commercial vs academic split, no node lock, no annual renewal — install and use without paperwork.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Already installed. HiGHS is pulled in automatically when you install FlexTool because highspy is a hard dependency. If for any reason it is missing from your environment, install it directly:

pip install highspy

There are no licence files to place, no environment variables to set, and no binaries to fetch separately from the vendor.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run:

python -c "from polar_high.solvers import available_solvers; print(available_solvers)"

Expected output (the list ordering may vary depending on which other wrappers are installed, but 'highs' must appear):

['gurobi', 'cplex', 'xpress', 'copt', 'highs']

If 'highs' is missing, your FlexTool install is broken — reinstall FlexTool or run pip install highspy to repair.

docs.title: How HiGHS is called
docs.text: Without --save-memory, FlexTool calls HiGHS in-process (the fastest path). With --save-memory, the model is written to an MPS file and solved by HiGHS in a separate process. Commercial solvers are always given an MPS file.

docs.title: HiGHS-specific options worth knowing
docs.text:
HiGHS exposes a long list of options; FlexTool surfaces them through the generic solver_arguments Map plus the convenience knobs. The most commonly useful HiGHS option names are:

HiGHS option name Type Notes presolve string "on" (default), "off", or "choose". parallel string "on", "off", or "choose" (default). time_limit float Wall-clock seconds. Equivalent to the --solver-time-limit CLI flag. mip_rel_gap float Relative MIP optimality gap. Equivalent to FlexTool's solver_mip_gap. threads int Thread cap. Equivalent to the --highs-threads CLI flag. solver string "simplex", "ipm", or "choose". (Note: this is HiGHS's own solver option — not FlexTool's.)

docs.title: The former highs_* parameters
docs.text:
Three older FlexTool parameters (highs_presolve, highs_method, highs_parallel) predated the generic mechanism and have been removed. Author the equivalent HiGHS option directly inside the solver_arguments Map instead:

Removed FlexTool parameter HiGHS option key in solver_arguments Type highs_presolve presolve string highs_method solver string highs_parallel parallel string

For example, to turn presolve off:

solver_arguments:
  presolve = "off"

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text:
HiGHS is unusual in that license, install, and environment errors are essentially absent. The two failure modes you can realistically see are:

  • Model infeasibility. FlexTool reports INFEASIBLE status from HiGHS; see the FlexTool log for the path to the matrix file (when a file-based dispatch was used) or use keep_solver=True inside the engine for in-process debugging.
  • Numerical issues. The LP-scaling guard already in FlexTool catches the most common cases; if you see HiGHS warn about ill-conditioning, the scenario probably has cost or capacity coefficients spanning more than ~12 orders of magnitude.

If you suspect a HiGHS internal issue, pass --solver-log-level verbose to capture HiGHS's own diagnostics in the FlexTool log.

docs.title: How to set it in FlexTool
docs.text:
HiGHS is the default. No parameter is needed. To make the choice explicit (or to set HiGHS-specific options), author on the relevant solve entity:

solve_advanced.solver = "highs"
solve_advanced.solver_arguments:
  presolve = "on"
  parallel = "on"

Run-wide options such as the wall-clock cap are passed as CLI flags:

flextool <input_db_url> --solver-time-limit 600

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
FICO Xpress is a commercial linear, mixed-integer, and nonlinear programming solver. FlexTool writes each solve's model to an MPS file and runs the Xpress optimizer console (found on PATH or in ~/xpressmp/bin) on it in a separate process, giving every control as a setControl <NAME> <value> command. FlexTool never imports xpress directly.

FlexTool's Xpress driver solves linear problems only: it runs lpoptimize, which for a problem with integer variables would return the LP relaxation. A solve with integer variables (integer investments, unit online variables) therefore stops with a message; use another solver for it.

Official site: https://www.fico.com/en/products/fico-xpress-optimization

docs.title: License options
docs.text:
• Commercial. FICO sells perpetual and term licences directly and through partners.
  • Academic. Free academic licences for teaching and research; apply through the FICO Xpress academic partnership.
  • Community Edition. Free, no-registration size-limited build with a hard cap (historically 5000 variables / 5000 rows for LPs and MIPs; exact cap and small-print may change by release — confirm against the current FICO documentation). Useful for tutorials and small validation models, too small for typical FlexTool dispatch scenarios.

Licence and download portal: FICO's Xpress product page above.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the Python wrapper:

pip install xpress

The PyPI xpress wheel from FICO embeds the solver runtime, so no additional download is needed for the Community Edition.

For licensed users:

  1. Obtain xpauth.xpr from your FICO licence portal.
  2. Place it at one of the default locations searched by Xpress, or set the environment variable XPAUTH_PATH to point at it. Refer to the vendor's installation guide for the precise discovery order on your platform ([FIXME: confirm URL]).
  3. Floating-licence users point XPAUTH_PATH at the licence server's xpauth.xpr shim.

Unlike Gurobi/COPT, xpress.problem() does not currently accept a pre-constructed environment object, so the polar-high env= pass-through is accepted but unused for Xpress. Licence discovery is entirely vendor-side.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After installing the wrapper, run:

python -c "from polar_high.solvers import available_solvers; print(available_solvers)"

Expected: 'xpress' appears in the list.

['gurobi', 'cplex', 'xpress', 'copt', 'highs']

To verify the licence works (this also prints the Xpress banner with the licence type):

python -c "import xpress; xpress.problem()"

Community Edition users see a banner stating the size cap. If the call raises an exception mentioning license, oem, or no token, see "Common errors" below.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text:
The error messages below are what FlexTool surfaces as FlexToolUserError. Xpress does not expose a stable numeric error code on its Python exceptions, so polar-high classifies licence errors by message text rather than code; the keyword set is license, licence, oem, expired, no token.

  • No xpauth.xpr found. Xpress raises with a message containing "license" or "no token". FlexTool shows: "Solver 'xpress' is installed but its license check failed. Details: ...". Fix by placing xpauth.xpr or setting XPAUTH_PATH.
  • Community-Edition size cap exceeded. Xpress raises with a message containing "oem" or "exceeds the size of an OEM problem". FlexTool surfaces this as the licence-error family. The fix is either to shrink the model or to upgrade to a full licence — Community Edition is unsuitable for production FlexTool scenarios.
  • Unknown Xpress control. A setControl the console does not know is reported in the solver output; FlexTool does not check Xpress' names. The control names are in the Xpress Optimizer reference manual.
  • Time limit reached. An LP stopped at its time limit stops the run. See Time limit.

docs.title: How to set it in FlexTool
docs.text:
On the solve entity:

solve_advanced.solver         = "xpress"
solve_advanced.solver_mip_gap = 0.005
solve_advanced.solver_arguments:
  defaultalg = 4
  presolve   = 1

flextool <input_db_url> --solver-time-limit 60

--solver-time-limit and --solver-mip-gap reach Xpress as MAXTIME 60 (whole seconds, rounded up) and MIPRELSTOP, over the solve's solver_mip_gap, its solver_arguments and xpress.opt (precedence in Solver selection). Parameter names match without regard to case. The thread count comes from THREADS in xpress.opt; --threads and --highs-threads do not change it. The run prints what Xpress receives in a Solver args (xpress): line before each solve.

Verified install on: [empty]

docs.title: Model formulation
docs.text: Every constraint, variable and objective term of the FlexTool LP, taken from the EQ. / VAR. / OBJ. headers in the model code. Each entry names the source file and line it was generated from. Names in braces expand: maxOnline_{linear,integer} is maxOnline_linear and maxOnline_integer, {sfx} is _linear / _integer, and a part in square brackets is optional (co2_max_total[_path]). Capacities are in MW (MWh for storage) and costs in CUR, the default units of FlexTool (see Model parameters).

docs.title: Capacity symbols used in the headers
docs.text:
For a unit, connection or storage node e in period d:

  • capacity[e,d] = existing[e,d] × virtual_unitsize[e] when virtual_unitsize is set, else existing[e,d] (MW, or MWh for storage). With virtual_unitsize, existing is the number of units.
  • unitsize[e] = virtual_unitsize[e], else existing (the largest period value), else 1000.
  • existing_count[e,d] = capacity[e,d] / unitsize[e]: equal to existing when virtual_unitsize is set; otherwise 1 (less in a period whose existing is below the largest, 0 without existing capacity).
  • invest_*, retire_*, cumulative_*, invest_forced and the capacity a construction lead time carries are MW (MWh) in every case. v_invest and v_divest are continuous, in units of unitsize.

docs.title: Core model
docs.text: FlexTool LP model: builds the FlexTool LP from FlexData d into a polar_high Problem m.

docs.title: VAR. v_flow
docs.text:
v_flow[p,source,sink,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ (p,source,sink,d,t) ∈ pss_dt

Flow on a process arc in units of unitsize: MW = v_flow · unitsize[p]. Input arcs of indirect units without invest/divest variables carry a per-element upper bound (their capacity is a constant); maxFlow caps every other arc.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:903 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_flow (coarse processes)
docs.text:
Names: v_flow

v_flow[p,s,k,d,b] ≥ 0   ∀ p ∈ processCoarse, (p,s,k) arcs, (d,b) the coarse steps of p (b = first fine step)

The flow of a coarse process: one rate per coarse step, the same on its fine steps. b.v_flow is indexed on every fine step (_coarse_flows.alias): a fine row of a coarse process reads its step's column.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:910 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_ramp_up / v_ramp_down
docs.text:
Names: v_ramp_up, v_ramp_down

v_ramp_up[p,s,k,d,t] ≥ 0, v_ramp_down[p,s,k,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ (p,s,k,d,t) ∈ R
  R = the rows of ramp_change_eq (_ramp_cost_rows): (p,s,k) ∈ process_source_sink_ramp_cost with a ramp
  predecessor at (d,t) (dt_ramp_link or dt_ramp_carry; for a coarse process t = b, its coarse step)

The increase and the decrease of v_flow from the ramp predecessor, in units of unitsize (as v_flow). Priced equally by the ramp cost, so at most one of them is > 0 at an optimum (up + down = |Δv_flow|). Declared only when some arc has a ramp cost.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:921 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: VAR. vq_state_up / vq_state_down
docs.text:
Names: vq_state_up, vq_state_down

vq_state_up[n,d,t], vq_state_down[n,d,t] ≥ 0
  ∀ n ∈ nodeBalance ∪ nodeBalancePeriod, (d,t) ∈ dt

Balance slack in MW (shortfall / surplus); enters the balance times step_duration and is penalised in the objective. Nodes with penalty_method = off have none, so their balance is a hard equality.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:936 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_state
docs.text:
v_state[n,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ (n,d,t) ∈ nodeState_dt

Storage state in units of the node's state unitsize: MWh = v_state · state_unitsize[n]. Its upper bound depends on invest/divest and is the maxState row.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:947 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_state_inter / v_state_rp_start
docs.text:
Names: v_state_inter, v_state_rp_start

v_state_inter[n,d,b] ≥ 0        ∀ n ∈ nodeState_rp, (d,b) ∈ rp_base_period
v_state_rp_start[n,d,t] ≥ 0     ∀ n ∈ nodeState_rp, (d,t) ∈ rp_block_first

Representative-period storage, in state units: the state at the end of base period b of period d, and the free starting state of each representative block. Every period has its own base periods (two periods may share base-period names). Upper bounds are the rows rp_inter_period_max_state and maxState_rp_start.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:956 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_invest_p / v_divest_p / v_invest_n / v_divest_n
docs.text:
Names: v_invest_p, v_divest_p, v_invest_n, v_divest_n

v_invest_p[p,d] ≥ 0 ∀ (p,d) ∈ pd_invest_set;  v_divest_p[p,d] ≥ 0 ∀ (p,d) ∈ pd_divest_set
v_invest_n[n,d] ≥ 0 ∀ (n,d) ∈ nd_invest_set;  v_divest_n[n,d] ≥ 0 ∀ (n,d) ∈ nd_divest_set

Capacity built / retired in period d, as a count of unitsize (process) or state unitsize (storage node). Only pre-existing capacity can be retired: pd/nd_divest_set hold the periods where the entity has some (before its end of life). Upper bounds are the maxInvest_var_bound / maxDivest_var_bound rows.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:974 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_flow_back
docs.text:
v_flow_back[p,source,sink,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ (p,source,sink) ∈ twoway1var_arcs, (d,t) ∈ dt

Reverse flow (sink → source) of method_2way_1var_off and DC power-flow arcs, in units of unitsize; the signed flow is v_flow − v_flow_back. One variable serves both the balance and dc_flow_eq. A coarse process has one per coarse step, as v_flow.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:994 (_declare_variables)

docs.title: EQ. rp_inter_period_balance
docs.text:
v_state_inter[n,d,b] − v_state_inter[n,d′,b′] = drift[n,d,b]
  drift[n,d,b] = Σ_{(d,b,r) ∈ rp_base__rep, (d,r) ∈ rp_block_first, d ∈ periods of dt}
                   rp_weight[d,b,r] · (v_state[n,d,last_step[d,r]] − v_state_rp_start[n,d,r])
  ∀ n ∈ nodeState_rp, (d,b,b′) ∈ rp_base_chain, d′ = d                         (within a period)
  ∀ n ∈ bind_within_solve_blended_weights ∪ bind_forward_only_blended_weights,
    (d,d′) ∈ rp_period_previous, b = first base period of d, b′ = last of d′    (period to period)

Chains the storage state across the base periods of each period: a base period is represented by weighted representative blocks r, and the boundary state moves by the weighted net change of those blocks. The across-solve variants continue from the last base period of the previous period in solve order, as bind_within_solve / bind_forward_only continue v_state across periods. All terms are in state units.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:1210 (_eq_rp_storage_chain)

docs.title: EQ. rp_inter_period_cyclic
docs.text:
v_state_inter[n,d,b_first(d)] − v_state_inter[n,d′,b_last(d′)] = drift[n,d,b_first(d)]
  n ∈ bind_within_period_blended_weights: every rp period d, d′ = d
  n ∈ bind_within_solve_blended_weights: (d,d′) ∈ d_first × d_last, d_first = the rp periods without a
    predecessor in rp_period_previous, d_last = the rp periods that are no period's predecessor

Closes the chain: the last boundary state connects back to the first. bind_within_period_blended_weights closes every period on itself, bind_within_solve_blended_weights closes once per path of the solve: deterministic, one pair (first period, last period). In a stochastic solve the rp periods form a tree (rp_period_previous): a fan after the trunk period (the shared period before the split) has one d_first and one d_last per forecast branch, so every branch's last period ends at the level the trunk period starts from; a fan in the first period has N roots and N leaves, and the N × N pairs are the loop of each path plus an equal chain start of all the roots. bind_forward_only_blended_weights has no closure.

Energy conservation per node and time step, in MWh. Storage nodes add the state change; the previous step t⁻ depends on storage_binding_method. nodeStateBlock nodes are balanced per timeset block (nodeBalanceBlock_eq), nodeCoarse nodes per coarse step (nodeBalanceCoarse_eq). The section term exists for min_load_efficiency units only. The start-up term (core._startup_draw) is the start-up energy of the units with a start-up input node n (startup_input_method startup_and_input / startup_only), MWh per start-up event; a coarse process starts at the first fine step of its coarse step. The flow, start-up and slack terms are b.node_balance_flow_terms. Self-discharge: the content decays continuously at ln(1 + loss) per hour; flows within a step are spread evenly over the step. Exact for any step length while the loss is constant within the step; a coarse step / block with a time-varying loss uses h_b = Σ Δt·λ_t, exact for the idle decay only (#152). The decay is applied to a weighted average of the start and the end state (model/_self_discharge.py); the model folds it into the state change as (S⁻·(1 − β) − S·(1 + α))·state_unitsize.

docs.title: EQ. maxFlow
docs.text:
v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve_up[p,r,k,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve_down[p,r,s,d,t] · φ[p,s,k,d,t]
  − M·Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_p[p,d′]
  + M·Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active} v_divest_p[p,d′]
  ≤ M · existing_count[p,d]
  ∀ (p,s,k,d,t) ∈ pss_dt, (p,s,k) ∉ flow_bound_arcs or (p,s,k) ∈ reserve_down_input_arcs
  M = capacity_max_coeff[p,s,k] · availability[p,d,t] on capped / uncapped arcs
  φ = 1 where v_flow is the input (k = p), 1/slope[p,d,t] on a direct unit's input→output arc
      (s ≠ p ≠ k); both reserve terms only for units (connections: connection_reserve_*, _reserve)

Caps every flow by the built capacity of its process (units of unitsize). On indirect-unit input arcs M = input_share_max · full-load input · a, a = x(availability) = (slope·W(a₀) + section)/(slope·W(1) + section) (a₀ = availability, W(y) the output-side fuel width filled to y, section only for a unit with an online variable); a ≥ availability (never tighter than the physical derated input), = availability when every output shares one conversion_flow_coeff (#102). Uncapped arcs (conversion_flow_coeff = 0) have M = 1 and RHS = p_flow_upper. Input arcs of units without invest/divest are bounded on v_flow instead (flow_bound_arcs). The reserve terms are the reserve that raises the flow: upward reserve held at the sink, and downward reserve held at the source of a unit (it consumes more), converted to the arc's flow. A bound input arc gets this row as well when it carries such a reserve (its v_flow bound stays, redundant). A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:2119 (_eq_max_flow)

  ∀ (p,s,k,d,t) ∈ pss_dt, (p,d) ∈ pd_neg_cap

docs.text:
Names: maxOutputSum, maxOutputSum_negCap

Σ_k v_flow[p,p,k,d,t] + Σ_k Σ_r v_reserve_up[p,r,k,d,t]
  − av·Σ v_invest_p[p,d′] + av·Σ v_divest_p[p,d′]
  ≤ av · existing_count[p,d]
  ∀ p ∈ process_indirect with an output arc k, (d,t);   av = availability[p,d,t]

The capacity of an indirect (multi-flow) unit is the maximum sum of its outputs; maxFlow caps each output arc alone. capacity_max_coeff is not applied. Negative-capacity (p,d) rows get only the ≥ twin maxOutputSum_negCap: with both, a k-output unit would need Σ out = c while maxFlow pins every arc to c. existing_count[p,d] is the value maxFlow's output arcs of p carry (all equal; max collapses them); a unit without an existing row gets 0. Availability defaults to 1.0 for processes without availability data. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

docs.title: EQ. ramp_{sink,source}_{up,down}_constraint
docs.text:
Names: ramp_sink_up_constraint, ramp_sink_down_constraint, ramp_source_up_constraint, ramp_source_down_constraint

Units without online variables (as c14a): v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] − v_flow[p,s,k,d′,t′] + R↑[p,s,k,d,t]

  ≤ +ρ̄ · c[p,s,k,d,t] · (existing_count[p,d] + Σ_{d″} v_invest_p[p,d″] − Σ_{d″} v_divest_p[p,d″])        (up)

v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] − v_flow[p,s,k,d′,t′] − R↓[p,s,k,d,t]

  ≥ −ρ̄ · c[p,s,k,d,t] · (existing_count[p,d] + Σ v_invest_p − Σ v_divest_p)                              (down)

Units with online variables (linear or integer class), room on the units online, split by unit state: v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] − v_flow[p,s,k,d′,t′] + R↑[p,s,k,d,t]

  ≤ c · ( ρ̄ · (v_online[p,d,t] − v_startup[p,d,t]) + SU[p,s,k,d,t] · v_startup[p,d,t] )
    − F[p,s,k,d′,t′] · v_shutdown[p,d,t]                                                                  (up)

v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] − v_flow[p,s,k,d′,t′] − R↓[p,s,k,d,t]

  ≥ −c · ( ρ̄ · (v_online[p,d,t] − v_startup[p,d,t]) + SD′[p,s,k,d′,t′] · v_shutdown[p,d,t] )
    + F[p,s,k,d,t] · v_startup[p,d,t]                                                                     (down)
  ρ̄ = ramp_speed_{dir}_{side}[p,node] · 60 · (step_duration[d′,t′] + step_duration[d,t]) / 2
  SU = min(1, ml[p,s,k,d,t] + ½ · ramp_speed_up_{side} · 60 · step_duration[d,t])
  SD′ = min(1, ml[p,s,k,d′,t′] + ½ · ramp_speed_down_{side} · 60 · step_duration[d′,t′])
  ml = min_load (output-measured arc) or x(min_load) / input_share_max (indirect unit's input arc), 0
    without min_load;  F = the arc's floor per unit online (arc_floor_share): min_load on the only arc of
    a unit's output measure, min_load · capacity_min_coeff on an output of a multi-output unit with
    capacity_min_coeff > 0, else 0
  ∀ (p,s,k) ∈ process_source_sink_ramp_limit_{side}_{dir}, (d,t,d′,t′) ∈ dt_ramp_link; on a link inside one
    period (d′ = d) only where ρ̄ < 1

On a continuation roll the first step of a period ramps from the previous roll's realized flow

  (dt_ramp_carry): v_flow[p,s,k,d′,t′] → f̂[p,s,k,d,t] (p_roll_continue_flow, a constant), step_duration
  [d′,t′] → its carried duration; for units with online variables F[d′,t′] → 0 (no shutdown term on the
  up row) and SD′ → max(1, f̂[p,s,k,d,t] / (c[p,s,k,d,t] · ĉ[p])) (1 where the carried online count
  ĉ = p_roll_continue_online is 0 — no stoppers then; exact and always feasible, unlike a fixed κ/c).

A coarse process (processCoarse, _coarse_flows.ramp_rows) ramps between its coarse steps: t = b (named by its

  first fine step), (d′,t′) = b⁻, the coarse step that holds the fine predecessor of b's first step, and
  step_duration → Δ_b = Σ_{t∈b} Δt, so ρ̄ = speed · 60 · (Δ_b⁻ + Δ_b)/2 (no row inside a coarse step; with
  24-h steps an in-period row exists only for a speed below 1/1440 per minute); a time-varying source factor
  c is its coarse-step mean; the carried step is the arc's last realized coarse step (its length carried).
  With online variables v_online is the step's value, v_startup / v_shutdown the events at b (start-ups and
  shut-downs relative to b⁻, online_change); c and F are their means over b (F[b⁻] over b⁻) and
  SU[b] = mean share over b of a unit started at b's start: ml + ½·ρ_b while ρ_b ≤ 1 − ml, else
  1 − (1 − ml)²/(2·ρ_b), ρ_b = ramp_speed_up · 60 · Δ_b, ml the mean over b (SD′[b⁻] likewise with the down
  speed over b⁻: the exact mean of a linear ramp that reaches full load within the step).

Steps without a predecessor, on arcs that hold reserve in that direction there (prundt):

  R↑ ≤ ρ·c·cap (up),  −R↓ ≥ −ρ·c·cap (down),  ρ = ramp_speed · 60 · step_duration[d,t] < 1;
  cap = v_online[p,d,t] for units with online variables, built units otherwise.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:2304 (_eq_ramp)

docs.title: EQ. ramp_{sink,source}_{up,down}_reserve_coarse
docs.text:
Names: ramp_sink_up_reserve_coarse, ramp_sink_down_reserve_coarse, ramp_source_up_reserve_coarse, ramp_source_down_reserve_coarse

R↑[p,s,k,d,b] ≤ room_b · cap (up),  −R↓[p,s,k,d,b] ≥ −room_b · cap (down)
  ∀ arc of a coarse process with the ramp limit, holding reserve in that direction on its coarse step (d,b)
  (b = its first fine step) with some ρ_t < 1;  room_b = min_{t∈b, ρ_t<1} ρ_t · c[p,s,k,d,t], ρ_t the room of
  the fine row at t: ramp_speed · 60 · (step_duration[d′,t′] + step_duration[d,t]) / 2 with t's ramp
  predecessor (d′,t′) (a carried one: the arc's carried duration p_roll_continue_flow_duration, as the
  carried ramp row), ramp_speed · 60 · step_duration[d,t] without one;  c the arc's capacity factor at t;
  cap = v_online (units online of the step) or the built units

A coarse process holds one reserve and one flow per coarse step: the fine rows inside the step (no flow change) would bound the reserve by each step's own room, so the smallest binds; the ramp between coarse steps above still holds the reserve together with the flow change. R↑ = Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,up,k,d,t] + φ·Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,down,s,d,t]

  (raises the arc: up at its sink, down at its source)

R↓ = Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,down,k,d,t] + φ·Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,up,s,d,t]

  (lowers it: down at its sink, up at its source)
  φ = 1 where v_flow is the input (indirect unit's input arc, sink-less unit), 1/slope on a direct arc;
  units only.

Limits the change of a flow between two consecutive steps, plus the reserve it holds in that direction, to its ramp room: ramp_speed is a share of capacity per minute and flows are step averages, so the room between two step averages is the speed × the distance between the two step centres (a valid bound for every trajectory that obeys the speed; it is the tight one for a linear ramp). For a unit with online variables the units online in both steps change by at most ρ̄ each, a unit starting in step t reaches at most SU (half a step's ramp above min load, the startup-step limit of maxFlow_online) and a stopping unit drops from at least its floor F; downwards a stopping unit drops at most from SD′ (the pre-shutdown limit) and a starting unit rises to at least F. v_startup / v_shutdown are relative to the same predecessor (online_change), so a start/stop pair with online unchanged gains c·(ml − ½·ρ·Δ) − F ≤ 0 of room on the only output of a unit (research_backbone_startup_ramp.md); on an input, or on one output of a multi-output unit, a pair can still gain up to the min-load share, paid by the startup cost. A step has a predecessor (dt_ramp_link) only where it is adjacent on the timeline in the un-rolled solve: no cyclic wrap at the first step of a solve or of a period that does not continue the previous one, no row across a gap or at the start of a representative block. Rows inside one period with ρ̄ ≥ 1 cannot bind and are not built (unchanged from c14a: every term of the online-capacity split is still implied there, design §1.4). Cross-period and carried rows are always built (the capacity, or the online predecessor, can differ). c scales the room as the arc's capacity is scaled: capacity_max_coeff[p,k] on the sink side; on the source side input_share_max[p,s], or on an indirect unit's input arc p_indirect_input_cap. v_flow and v_reserve are in units of unitsize, existing_count = capacity / unitsize. Arcs with conversion_flow_coeff = 0 get no row. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:2345 (_eq_ramp)

docs.title: EQ. ramp_change_eq
docs.text:
v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] − v_flow[p,s,k,d′,t′] − v_ramp_up[p,s,k,d,t] + v_ramp_down[p,s,k,d,t] = 0
  ∀ (p,s,k) ∈ process_source_sink_ramp_cost, (d,t,d′,t′) ∈ dt_ramp_link   (every link, no room filter)
carried row (dt_ramp_carry): v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] − v_ramp_up + v_ramp_down = f̂[p,s,k,d,t] (p_roll_continue_flow)
coarse process: t = b (its coarse step, named by the first fine step), (d′,t′) = b⁻, as _coarse_flows.ramp_rows

Splits the change of a flow between a step and its ramp predecessor into an increase and a decrease, both priced by the ramp cost (OBJ. ramp_cost), in units of unitsize. The predecessors are those of the ramp limits: no row at the first step of a solve, after a gap in the timeline, at a period that does not continue the previous one or at a representative-block start; cross-period links are kept; a stochastic branch's first step links to the shared predecessor; a continuation roll's first step ramps from the flow the previous roll realized, so a change at a roll boundary is charged once, in the roll that realizes it. Arcs with conversion_flow_coeff = 0 have rows too (that parameter removes the ramp limits, not the cost). Reserves are not part of the change. An indirect unit's input and output arcs are priced separately, each by its own side.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:2445 (_eq_ramp_cost)

docs.title: EQ. max{Invest,Divest}_var_bound[_n]
docs.text:

v_invest_p[p,d] ≤ max_units[p,d]   ∀ (p,d) ∈ pd_invest_set     (maxInvest_var_bound)
v_divest_p[p,d] ≤ max_units[p,d]   ∀ (p,d) ∈ pd_divest_set     (maxDivest_var_bound)

v_divest_n[n,d] ≤ max_units[n,d]   ∀ (n,d) ∈ nd_divest_set     (maxDivest_var_bound_n)

Caps the units invested or divested in one period (max_units = p_entity_max_units). Emitted as rows, not as variable bounds.

docs.title: EQ. max{Invest,Divest}_entity_period_{p,n}
docs.text:
Names: maxInvest_entity_period_p, maxInvest_entity_period_n, maxDivest_entity_period_p, maxDivest_entity_period_n

Σ_{(p,o,d) ∈ edd_invest_commission} v_invest_p[p,o] · unitsize[p] + carried_commission[p,d]
                                     ≤ invest_max_period[p,d]   ∀ (p,d) with a decision coming online in d,
                                                                  p ∈ ed_invest_period_set
(n: v_invest_n with state_unitsize[n], n ∈ ed_invest_period_set ∩ nd_invest_set)
v_divest_p[p,d] · unitsize[p]        ≤ divest_max_period[p,d]   ∀ (p,d) ∈ ed_divest_period_set ∩ pd_divest_set
v_divest_n[n,d] · state_unitsize[n]  ≤ divest_max_period[n,d]   ∀ (n,d) ∈ ed_divest_period_set ∩ nd_divest_set

Caps the capacity coming online or retired in one period for entities with a per-period limit (e.g. invest_method = invest_period_total). An investment decided in o comes online in d = c(o) (construction lead time); without a lead time c(o) = o and the row is v_invest_p[p,d] · unitsize[p] ≤ invest_max_period[p,d] over ed_invest_period_set ∩ pd_invest_set, the form built when no decision of the solve has a lead time. carried_commission is the capacity earlier solves of a chain decided that comes online in d. The cap is raw capacity with unitsize on the LHS, as in the other invest caps, so the row dual is in objective units per unit of capacity.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:3056 (_eq_invest_period_caps)

docs.title: EQ. max{Invest,Divest}_entity_total[_path][_n]
docs.text:
Names: maxInvest_entity_total, maxInvest_entity_total_n, maxInvest_entity_total_path, maxInvest_entity_total_path_n, maxDivest_entity_total, maxDivest_entity_total_n, maxDivest_entity_total_path, maxDivest_entity_total_path_n

Σ_{d ∈ D(leaf)} v_invest_p[p,d] · unitsize[p]  ≤  max(0, invest_max_total[p] − prior_inv[p])
  ∀ p ∈ e_invest_total ∩ process_source_sink ∩ P(v_invest_p) (, leaf)
Σ_{d ∈ D(leaf)} v_divest_p[p,d] · unitsize[p]  ≤  max(0, divest_max_total[p] − prior_div[p])
  ∀ p ∈ e_divest_total ∩ process_source_sink ∩ P(v_divest_p) (, leaf)
  prior_inv[e] = p_entity_invested[e]  (capacity realized by all earlier solves of the
    chain, retired or not); prior_div[e] = p_entity_divested[e]  (capacity retired by all
    earlier solves of the chain, at realized non-branch periods only)
  _n: v_invest_n / v_divest_n with state_unitsize[n], n ∈ nodeState
  _path: one row per (entity, leaf), D(leaf) = periods of the leaf, only for (entity, leaf)
    pairs that have the variable

Caps the amount built (retired) over the chain; reinvestments count, retirements do not reduce it. Capacity in service is cumulative_max_capacity. Rows only for entities that have the variable in this solve (#43). If a user realizes a period in one solve and invests in it again in a later one, it is counted twice in prior_inv — same as the old (now-removed) max_d(p_entity_previously_invested_capacity) form; no fixture does this.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:3122 (_eq_invest_total_caps)

docs.title: EQ. maxRetired_existing_{p,n}
docs.text:
Names: maxRetired_existing_p, maxRetired_existing_n

Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active} v_divest_p[p,d′] · unitsize[p]  ≤  pre_existing[p,d] − retired_carried[p,d]
  ∀ (p,d) with some (p,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active, p ∈ process_source_sink
Σ_{(n,d′,d) ∈ ndd_divest_active} v_divest_n[n,d′] · state_unitsize[n]  ≤  pre_existing[n,d] − retired_carried[n,d]
  ∀ (n,d) with some (n,d′,d) ∈ ndd_divest_active, n ∈ nodeState
  edd_divest_active = {(e,d′,d) : (e,d′) ∈ ed_divest_set, yr[d′] ≤ yr[d] < EOL[e]}, EOL[e] the end of
    life of the entity's pre-existing capacity (from the start of the run; none for reinvest_automatic)
  pre_existing = p_entity_pre_existing (the user's existing × unitsize, lifetime-gated: MW, MWh)
  retired_carried = p_entity_retired_carried (retirements of earlier solves of a chain still counting in d)

Only capacity that existed before the run can be retired: the capacity retired so far and still counting in d stays within the pre-existing capacity of d (a declining existing map, or an entity that also invests, cannot retire more than was there). A retirement option exists only where pre_existing > 0.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:3187 (_eq_retired_existing)

docs.title: EQ. conversion_indirect
docs.text:
Σ_{s ∈ in(p)} v_flow[p,s,p,d,t] · unitsize[p] · conv_in[p,s]
  + Σ_s Σ_{(t_s,t,δ) ∈ delay} v_flow[p,s,p,d,t_s] · unitsize[p] · delay_weight[p,δ] · conv_in[p,s]
  = Σ_{k ∈ out(p)} v_flow[p,p,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · slope[p,d,t] · conv_out[p,k]
    + v_online[p,d,t] · section[p,d,t] · unitsize[p]
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ process_indirect_dt
  section[p,d,t] = min_load·(1/eta_min − 1/eta) / (1 − min_load)
  slope[p,d,t] = 1/eta − section[p,d,t]   (= (1/eta − min_load/eta_min) / (1 − min_load))
    for min_load_efficiency units (eta = efficiency, default 1; min_load = 0 where not authored;
    eta_min = efficiency_at_min_load, else efficiency); slope = 1/eta and no section for the other units
    (indirect units never fold conv_in/conv_out into slope/section themselves — see conv_in/conv_out below)

Energy balance of an indirect (multi-flow) unit: weighted input equals weighted output times the slope. conv_in / conv_out = source / sink conversion_flow_coeff (default 1); unequal sink coefficients express e.g. the heat/electricity trade-off of an extraction CHP. The first input sum covers undelayed units; delayed units take their inputs at the earlier source-side steps t_s (dtt__delay_duration, _delay.delayed_input_expr), t being the sink-side time. Section term (indirect min_load_efficiency units, linear and integer v_online): the input of an indirect unit is its own v_flow, so this is the only place the section fuel enters; node balance, commodity cost, CO2 and the reported inputs all read that v_flow. It carries no conversion_flow_coeff; for a delayed unit it sits on the output side at time t. Rows without a v_online column lack the term.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:3243 (_eq_conversion)

docs.title: EQ. minInputShare
docs.text:
conv[p,s] · v_flow[p,s,p,d,t]  ≥  share_min[p,s] · Σ_{s′ ∈ in(p)} conv[p,s′] · v_flow[p,s′,p,d,t]
  ∀ (p,s) with share_min[p,s] > 0, p ∈ process_indirect with ≥ 2 inputs, (p,d,t) ∈ process_indirect_dt

While the unit runs, input s supplies at least the share input_share_min of its current input energy (conv = source conversion_flow_coeff, default 1). The row is homogeneous: with no input it reads 0 ≥ 0, so it needs no online variable. unitsize cancels (v_flow is per unitsize on every input of p).

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:3306 (_eq_min_input_share)

docs.title: EQ. co2_max_period
docs.text:
Σ_{(p,s,k,c,g) ∈ flow_from_co2_capped, t}
    (v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·slope[p,d,t] + v_online[p,d,t]·section[p,d,t]·unitsize[p])
    · co2_content[c]·w[d,t]
  + Σ_{(p,s,k,c,g) ∈ flow_from_co2_capped_noEff, t} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·co2_content[c]·w[d,t]
  − Σ_{(p,s,k,c,g) ∈ flow_to_co2_capped, t} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·co2_content[c]·w[d,t]
  + Σ_{(p,n,c,g) ∈ startup_from_co2_capped, t} v_startup[p,d,t]·startup_energy[p,n,d]·unitsize[p]
      · co2_content[c]·w[d,t]/step_duration[d,t]   (start-up energy: an event, no step_duration)
  ≤ co2_max_period[g,d] · f_d_k[d]  −  co2_cum_realized_tonnes[g,α(d)] / period_share[d]
  ∀ (g,d) ∈ group_d_co2_capped;   w = step_duration · timestep_weight / period_share
  f_d_k[d] = (realized hours of α(d) from earlier solves + this solve's hours of d) / complete hours of α(d)
  α(d) = the period label of a forecast branch period d, d itself otherwise; period_share, f_d_k and the
  realized carry of a forecast come from α(d) unless it has its own row: every forecast continues from
  its period's realized history (the realization solve's carry)

Caps the annualised CO2 emissions of a group in each period (tonnes per year): dividing by period_share, the LHS is the emissions of the solve's own steps of d annualised over their hours. The RHS (_co2_period_cap_with_carry) is this period's remaining budget as of this roll: f_d_k[d] (1 outside rolling / chained solves) is the cumulative share of d's hours reached by the end of this roll's horizon, and the realized carrier (0 on the first solve of a chain) is what earlier rolls / solves already emitted for this exact period, net of removal credits (#19) — never negative by construction (#38, Q22; see the helper's own docstring). Emissions come from the fuel that processes draw from the group's nodes when it carries a CO2-emitting commodity c, measured as in co2_price_eff (_eff_fuel_input): on eff processes the output flow times slope plus, for min_load_efficiency units (linear and integer v_online), the section fuel of the units online. noEff processes take neither slope nor section (applying them would over-count). The removal term (#19, Q14) subtracts flows into the same group's node(s) — e.g. DAC/BECCS — unsplit, no slope, same measure as flow_to_co2_priced; it only loosens the cap, never tightens it.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:3505 (_eq_co2_max_period)

docs.title: EQ. co2_max_total[_path]
docs.text:
Names: co2_max_total, co2_max_total_path

Σ_{(p,s,k,c,g) ∈ flow_from_co2_capped_total, d∈D(leaf),t}
    (v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·slope[p,d,t] + v_online[p,d,t]·section[p,d,t]·unitsize[p])
    · co2_content[c]·w_y[d,t]
  + Σ_{(p,s,k,c,g) ∈ flow_from_co2_capped_total_noEff, d∈D(leaf),t}
    v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·co2_content[c]·w_y[d,t]
  − Σ_{(p,s,k,c,g) ∈ flow_to_co2_capped_total, d∈D(leaf),t} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·co2_content[c]·w_y[d,t]
  + Σ_{(p,n,c,g) ∈ startup_from_co2_capped_total, d∈D(leaf),t}
    v_startup[p,d,t]·startup_energy[p,n,d]·unitsize[p]·co2_content[c]·w_y[d,t]/step_duration[d,t]
  ≤ co2_max_total[g] · horizon_fraction_reached  −  Σ_d R_rep[g,d]
  ∀ g ∈ group_co2_max_total (, leaf);   w_y = step_duration · timestep_weight / period_share · years_represented[d]
  R_rep[g,d] = realized tonnes of d from earlier rolls / solves · years_represented[d] / period_share[d],
  with the share and years of the solve that realized them (the w_y its own row gave them)

Caps the CO2 emissions of a group over the horizon the solve represents (tonnes): each period's annualised emissions (as in co2_max_period, section fuel included) times the years the period represents, summed over the periods — the measure of the model CO2 output. years_represented is not discounted. The RHS (_co2_total_cap_with_carry) is the remaining budget as of this roll: without it, each solve of a chain and each roll of a rolling solve got the FULL cap again for only its own periods / window, over-allowing roughly by the number of rolls / chained solves (#38) — fixed the same way the commodity ladder's cumulative tier cap was (#89/#143): horizon_fraction_reached scales the fixed whole-horizon budget down to what's allocated so far, and the realized carrier (0 on the first solve of a chain) — net of removal credits (#19), weighted like the LHS (R_rep, not physical tonnes: a realized step counts years_represented / period_share times its tonnes, as it did in the row of the solve that realized it) — is subtracted; never negative by construction. The removal term (#19, Q14) mirrors co2_max_period's: flows into the same group's node(s), unsplit, no slope; it only loosens the cap. _path (Q16, #52): under recourse every forecast branch got its own copy of the whole-horizon budget summed into ONE row, letting N branches spend N× the cap between them (the stochastic fan is parallel futures, not N consecutive years). One row per (g, leaf) fixes it: the LHS sums only the leaf's own periods (shared pre-reveal trunk periods belong to every leaf, same as the invest/divest _path families); the RHS is the SAME remaining whole-horizon budget repeated per leaf (horizon_fraction_reached and the realized carry are chain-wide, not per-branch quantities — the carry is kept exactly as _co2_total_cap_with_carry computes it, same as the entity/group total-cap _path families reuse their own bare cap per leaf).

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:3646 (_eq_co2_max_total)

docs.title: EQ. process_constraint_{equal,less_than,greater_than}[_period]
docs.text:
Names: process_constraint_equal, process_constraint_equal_period, process_constraint_less_than, process_constraint_less_than_period, process_constraint_greater_than, process_constraint_greater_than_period

Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ flow_constraint[cn]} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·flow_coef[p,s,k,cn]
  + Σ_n v_state[n,d,t]·state_unitsize[n]·node_state_coef[n,cn]
  + Σ_e inv[e,d]·invested_coef[e,cn]
  + Σ_e con[e,d]·in_construction_coef[e,cn]
  + Σ_e v_divest[e,d]·us[e]·retired_coef[e,cn]
  + Σ_e pre[e,d]·prebuilt_coef[e,cn]
  + Σ_e cap[e,d]·capacity_coef[e,cn]
  + Σ_{p ∈ process_online} v_online[p,d,t]·online_coef[p,cn]
  = / ≤ / ≥  constant[cn] (or constant[cn,d] for a period map)
  ∀ (cn,d,t) ∈ cdt_{eq,le,ge} with a flow, state or online coefficient   (process_constraint_*)
  ∀ (cn,d) of the other constraints of cdt_{eq,le,ge}             (process_constraint_*_period)
where, for e a process p (us = unitsize, existing = capacity = existing_count·unitsize) or a storage node n
(us = state_unitsize, existing = capacity, the storage capacity), MW (MWh):
  inv[e,d] = Σ_{(e,o,d) ∈ edd_invest_commission} v_invest[e,o]·us[e] + carried_commission[e,d]
  con[e,d] = Σ_{(e,o,d) ∈ edd_invest_in_construction} v_invest[e,o]·us[e] + carried_in_construction[e,d]
  pre[e,d] = existing[e,d] − carried_commission[e,d] + Σ_{(e,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_lookback} v_invest[e,d′]·us[e]
                           − Σ_{(e,d′,d) ∈ edd/ndd_divest_active, d′ ≠ d} v_divest[e,d′]·us[e]
  cap[e,d] = existing[e,d] + Σ_{(e,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest[e,d′]·us[e]
                           − Σ_{(e,d′,d) ∈ edd/ndd_divest_active} v_divest[e,d′]·us[e]

A linear constraint authored by the user over flows (MW), storage states (MWh) and capacities. The invested term is the capacity that comes online in d (an investment decided in o with a construction lead time comes online in c(o); without one c(o) = o and inv[e,d] = v_invest[e,d]·us[e]); the in-construction term is the capacity decided but not yet online (zero without a lead time); the retired term counts the retirements of d; pre is the capacity in service at the start of d (existing plus earlier investments still alive, minus earlier retirements, also those of the same solve: a single solve and a chain of solves give the same row); cap is the capacity in service in d, the measure of maxFlow and the cumulative-capacity rows. cap = pre + inv − retired, with or without a lead time. carried_* are the investments earlier solves of a chain decided with a lead time (constants; existing holds them from their start of operation, so pre subtracts the part coming online in d). The online term counts the units online (of unitsize) in each step; integer with binary startup, continuous with linear. v_online is the variable of the process's UC class (v_online_linear / v_online_integer). Terms without data are absent. The existing-capacity terms are constants and enter as Param terms. A constraint without flow, state and online terms is the same in every step of a period, so it gets one row per period (the _period family) instead of one per step. The constraint axis is cn (c is the commodity axis). Dims: flow, state and online terms (cn, d, t); every capacity term (cn, d), broadcast over t on the per-step rows. A row whose terms all vanish in the solve (its entities have no flow, state, investment or retirement there) is left out: a configuration error when the remaining existing-capacity constant sense constant cannot hold, else a warning naming the constraint. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Row rule (coarse steps): a per-step constraint whose flow and online terms are all on coarse processes and whose state terms are on coarse nodes gets one row per coarse step, process_constraint_*_coarse = the row's Δt-weighted mean over the step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr); its coefficients are constant, so it is the per-step row itself on one flow per step (the units online of a coarse process are one level per coarse step). A constraint with a fine flow, online or state term keeps its rows per solve step and reads the coarse flows and units online at their constant value.

docs.title: EQ. process_constraint_{equal,less_than,greater_than}_period_total
docs.text:
Names: process_constraint_equal_period_total, process_constraint_less_than_period_total, process_constraint_greater_than_period_total

Σ_t w[d,t]·( Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ flow_constraint[cn]} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]·unitsize[p]·flow_coef[p,s,k,cn]
             + Σ_{p ∈ process_online} v_online[p,d,t]·online_coef[p,cn] )
  + H[d]·( Σ_e inv[e,d]·invested_coef[e,cn] + Σ_e con[e,d]·in_construction_coef[e,cn]
           + Σ_e v_divest[e,d]·us[e]·retired_coef[e,cn] + Σ_e pre[e,d]·prebuilt_coef[e,cn]
           + Σ_e cap[e,d]·capacity_coef[e,cn] )
  = / ≤ / ≥  constant[cn] (or constant[cn,d] for a period map)
  ∀ (cn,d) ∈ cdt_{eq,le,ge}, cn ∈ constraint_period_total, window_fraction[d] = 1
w[d,t] = step_duration[d,t]·timestep_weight[d,t] / period_share[d];   H[d] = Σ_t w[d,t]
inv, con, pre, cap, us and the existing / carried constants as in process_constraint_* (_eq_user_constraints).

One row per period over the period's time-integrated, annualised terms (per year: flows in MWh, units online in unit-hours, the constant in the constraint's unit per year), the weighting of co2_max_period. H is the number of hours the period's modelled steps stand for in a year (8760 for a full year, also with representative periods, whose weights are normalised); computed, not 8760, so a roll window or a varying step duration gets its own. Every capacity term, and the existing / carried capacity constants, are multiplied by H: each term is its per-step quantity integrated over the period, so a coefficient keeps its per-step meaning (flow − 0.3·capacity ≤ 0 caps the annual capacity factor at 0.3). State terms are rejected by the reader (a state summed over steps is not an energy). A row needs the whole period in the solve: a period that the solve holds in part (window_fraction \< 1, the look-ahead tail of a roll) has no row; a rolling solve whose rolls do not each realize whole periods has none at all (user_constraint_period_total_off, the run's pre-solve check names the constraints and the solve). Stochastic branch periods are their own d (no probability weight: each forecast meets the limit). Coarse flows and units online enter through their alias on the fine steps (exact: Σ_t v·Δt). Dims: flow and online terms (cn, d, t) summed over t; capacity terms and constants (cn, d).

docs.text:

    n ∉ bind_forward_only ∪ bind_within_timeblock ∪ bind_within_solve ∪ bind_within_period ∪ nodeStateBlock

Pins the state at the first step to the share state_start of the built storage capacity (state units). Only where no state of the node was realised before this solve (carried: the nodes of roll_continue_state), i.e. the first solve of the model and of each nested level. The nodes left are the representative-period (blended weights) nodes, whose first step starts from v_state_rp_start. bind_forward_only nodes get their start through nodeBalance_eq (_fix_start_terms); the cyclic nodes (bind_within_timeblock, bind_within_solve, bind_within_period, bind_intraperiod_blocks) are pinned by storage_state_start_binding_cyclic_period. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

docs.title: EQ. storage_state_start_binding_cyclic_period
docs.text:
v_state[n,d′,t′] − state_start[n]·Σ_{(n,d″,d′) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_n[n,d″]
  + state_start[n]·Σ_{(n,d″,d′) ∈ ndd_divest_active} v_divest_n[n,d″]
  = state_start[n] · capacity[n,d′] / state_unitsize[n]
  ∀ n ∈ storage_fix_start ∩ (bind_within_timeblock ∪ bind_within_solve ∪ bind_within_period
    ∪ looping nodeStateBlock), n ∉ carried, (n,d,t) ∈ nodeState_first_dt, (d′,t′) = the step (d,t) starts
    from (the node's wrap), (n,d′,t′) ∉ the steps node_balance_fix_quantity_eq_lower fixes

The first step of a cyclic node starts from its wrap target, so the start state is pinned there, to the share state_start of the built storage capacity (state units): the last step of the first timeblock (bind_within_timeblock; in a roll, of the timeblock's part in the roll), of the solve (bind_within_solve) or of the first period (bind_within_period, bind_intraperiod_blocks). Only where no state of the node was realised before this solve (the first solve of the model and of each nested level); a later solve neither pins nor carries a cyclic node (it cycles within the solve). Where an upper-level solve fixes the state at the wrap target the upper value wins (the two equalities would sit on one variable). A bind_intraperiod_blocks node that chains forward (fix_start_end, or a roll that holds its first period only in part) has its start in nodeBalanceBlock_eq (_fix_start_terms); fix_start_end nodes of the other cyclic methods are forward-only in the solve (_run_model._fix_start_end_chains_forward). A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

docs.title: EQ. storage_within_solve_path_end
docs.text:
v_state[n,d,t_last(d)] − v_state[n,d*,t_last(d*)] = 0
  ∀ n ∈ bind_within_solve, d ∈ period_last, d ≠ d*, (n,d,t_last(d)) and (n,d*,t_last(d*)) ∈ nodeState_last_dt,
    unless both ends are already set (each is a step storage_state_start_binding_cyclic_period pins or
    node_balance_fix_quantity_eq_lower fixes)
  d* = the last period the solve's first steps wrap to (the state-change lag of bind_within_solve,
    _self_discharge.state_links): the last period key of the solve, the trunk's wrap target
bind_within_solve closes one loop per path of a stochastic solve.  The first step of the solve continues from
the last step of d* only, so this row ends every other path (period_last: the solve's last period and its
forecast branch siblings) at the same level: every branch's end is the level the trunk starts from.  With a
fan in the solve's first period each root forecast's first step continues from the last step of its own path
(dtttdt_within_solve), so equal ends also give all the forecasts the same start.  A deterministic solve has
one last period and no rows.  A fix_start node keeps the rows where only one end is pinned (a fan after the
trunk period: the pin sits at d*'s end); with both ends pinned or fixed the row would only repeat (or
contradict) those values.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:4499 (_eq_storage_within_solve_path_end)

docs.title: EQ. storage_state_fan_start
docs.text:
v_state[n,d,t_first(d)] − v_state[n,d″,t_first(d″)] = 0
  ∀ n ∈ bind_forward_only, (n,d,t_first(d)) and (n,d″,t_first(d″)) ∈ nodeState_first_dt with no start term
    (n ∉ storage_fix_start ∪ carried), d = the first root (sorted), d″ ∈ the other roots, one row
    per group of roots that non_anticipativity_storage_state_first does not already tie to d's group
  roots = the periods of nodeState_first_dt (built from period_first_of_solve): the forecast branch periods
    of a fan in the solve's first period; one root without a fan: no rows

The first step of a bind_forward_only node has no state change (dtttdt_forward_only): without fix_start or a carried state it is free, so each forecast of a fan in the first period could pick its own start level from what it later sees. The fan has only forecasts (no realized member), so this row is what makes their start the same. A fix_start or carried node starts every root from the same value already (_fix_start_terms, the roll carry). For a node of an include_stochastics group, non_anticipativity_storage_state_first may tie the first step of a root to its reference forecast already (a tie window shorter than the root period): those pairs are left out, read from that row's domain.

docs.text:
v_state[n,d,t] − state_end[n]·Σ_{(n,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_n[n,d′]

    (n,d,t) ∉ the steps node_balance_fix_quantity_eq_lower / node_storage_usage_fix_le fix

Pins the state at the end of the last step of the entire model to the share state_end of the built storage capacity (state units), in every sub-solve whose horizon holds that step (storage_solve_at_model_end, _carry_routing.reaches_model_end: e.g. both an investment solve and the last dispatch roll; each nested level's solve that holds it; a roll whose look-ahead runs to it); each last period (each terminal branch of a stochastic solve) ends there. storage_fix_end = fix_end ∪ fix_start_end. Where an upper-level solve fixes the quantity or caps the usage at that step the upper value wins; a nested fix_price steers the end through the objective and keeps the pin. A fix_start_end node chains forward whatever its storage_binding_method (_run_model._fix_start_end_chains_forward, _self_discharge.block_forward_nodes), so its start is in the first step's balance and never on this state; a cyclic node is pinned here by fix_end only. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

docs.text:
v_state[n,d,t] − reference_value[n,d,t]·Σ_{(n,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_n[n,d′]
  + reference_value[n,d,t]·Σ_{(n,d′,d) ∈ ndd_divest_active} v_divest_n[n,d′]
  = reference_value[n,d,t] · capacity[n,d] / state_unitsize[n]
  ∀ n ∈ storage_use_reference_value, (n,d,t) ∈ horizon_end,
    (n ∈ nodeStateBlock ⇒ d ∈ period_block_chain), (n,d,t) ∉ the steps an upper-level solve fixes
  horizon_end = nodeState_last_dt ∩ period_last  ∪  block_tail_end

Pins the state at the end of the solve horizon to the reference share of the built storage capacity (state units), as maxState and the start pins count it. period_last is the solve's last period and its stochastic branch siblings only: an earlier period of a multi-period solve is not a horizon end. Nodes with a competing end condition are not in storage_use_reference_value; a bind_intraperiod_blocks node is, in a rolling solve, and is pinned where the roll holds the period only in part (there its blocks chain forward instead of looping): at the roll end and at block_tail_end, the last step of a chained part-period tail that a period held whole follows (nothing continues from it, _self_discharge.block_tail_ends). Where an upper-level solve fixes the node at the step (nested fix_quantity, fix_usage, fix_price) the upper value overrides the reference value: two equalities on one state (fix_quantity), a usage cap the pin could make infeasible (fix_usage), or a price meant to steer that end (fix_price). reference_value on the pinned rows only: as a coefficient of the invest / divest sums it would otherwise span every (n, d_invest, d, t) of the solve. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] ± (Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,k,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,s,d,t] · φ[p,s,k,d,t])
  − profile[f,d,t]·av[p,d,t]·Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_p[p,d′]
  + profile[f,d,t]·av[p,d,t]·Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active} v_divest_p[p,d′]

  ∀ (p,s,k,f) ∈ process_profile_{upper,lower,fixed}, (d,t) ∈ dt

The upper limit adds the reserve that raises the arc's flow (up at the sink; down at a unit's source), the lower limit subtracts the reserve that lowers it (down at the sink; up at a unit's source); a source-side reserve is converted to the arc's flow by φ (1 where v_flow is the input, 1/slope on a direct unit's input→output arc).
