    other_operational_cost[p,d,t] ≠ 0 (constant, period, time or period × time).
O&M cost of connections with an efficiency, priced on the flow of each direction.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5108 (_obj_variable_cost)

docs.title: OBJ. startup_cost
docs.text:
Σ_{(p,d,t) ∈ pdt_online_{linear,integer}} v_startup_{linear,integer}[p,d,t] · startup_cost[p,d] · unitsize[p] · w_ev[d,t]
  w_ev = timestep_weight · inflation_op / period_share · branch_weight

Cost of starting up units, startup_cost in currency/MW started. A startup is an event, so the weight has no step_duration.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5129 (_obj_startup_cost)

docs.title: OBJ. ramp_cost
docs.text:
Σ_{(p,s,k,d,t) ∈ R} (v_ramp_up + v_ramp_down)[p,s,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · rc[p,s,k] · w_ev[d,t]
  rc[p,s,k] = p_ramp_cost_arc = Σ_{side ∈ {source s, sink k}, ramp_method[p,side] ∈ {ramp_cost, both}}
              ramp_cost[p,side]   (> 0; a direct unit's one arc takes both sides)
  w_ev = timestep_weight · inflation_op / period_share · branch_weight   (as startup_cost)

Cost of changing a flow, ramp_cost in currency per MW of change of the step-average flow, up and down alike. A change is an event, as a start-up, so the weight has no step_duration: ramping 0 → X → 0 costs 2·rc·X whatever the step lengths. A start-up from 0 pays both its startup cost and this cost.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5153 (_obj_ramp_cost)

docs.title: OBJ. storage_reference_price
docs.text:
− Σ_{(n,d,t) ∈ horizon_end, (n,d) ∈ reference_price}
    v_state[n,d,t]·state_unitsize[n] · reference_price[n,d] · w_ev[d,t]
  horizon_end = nodeState_last_dt ∩ period_last  ∪  block_tail_end   (as storage_state_solve_horizon_
                reference_value: the solve's last period and its branch siblings, and in a rolling solve the
                end of a chained bind_intraperiod_blocks tail that a looping period follows)
  w_ev = timestep_weight · inflation_op / period_share · branch_weight

Values the energy left in storage at the end of the solve horizon (revenue, hence the minus), reference_price in currency/MWh. The price comes from use_reference_price nodes or from the storage-price handoff of a previous solve. An end-of-horizon valuation is a point event, so the weight has no step_duration. Rows with a zero price are kept.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5183 (_obj_storage_reference_price)

docs.title: OBJ. invest_cost_p
docs.text:
Σ_{(p,d) ∈ pd_invest_set} v_invest_p[p,d]·unitsize[p] · annual_discounted[p,d] · bw[d]
  + Σ_{(p,d) ∈ pd_invest_set} v_invest_p[p,d]·unitsize[p] · lifetime_fixed_cost[p,d] · bw[d]

Cost of process capacity decided in period d, currency/MW: the investment annuity summed over the discounted years it operates within the horizon, and the inflation-adjusted fixed cost over the same years of its lifetime. With a construction lead time the capacity operates from its start of operation c(d): both windows start there, and the invest cost, interest rate, lifetime and fixed cost are those of c(d) (invest_cost is an overnight cost); without one c(d) = d. No w_op: both factors are already per period.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5228 (_obj_invest_divest)

docs.title: OBJ. divest_cost_p
docs.text:
− Σ_{(p,d) ∈ pd_divest_set} v_divest_p[p,d]·unitsize[p] · lifetime_fixed_cost_divest[p,d] · bw[d]
  − Σ_{(p,d) ∈ pd_divest_set} v_divest_p[p,d]·unitsize[p] · annual_divest_discounted[p,d] · bw[d]
  lifetime_fixed_cost_divest[p,d] = Σ_{d′ ∈ W(p,d)} fixed_cost[p,d′]·1000·inflation_op[d′]
  annual_divest_discounted[p,d] = ann(salvage_value[p,d], discount_rate[p,d], lifetime[p,d])
                                  · Σ_{d′ ∈ S(p,d)} inflation_inv[d′]
  W(p,d) = the solve's periods d′ with yr[d] ≤ yr[d′] < EOL[p] (the window of edd_divest_active: until the
    end of life of p's pre-existing capacity, the end of the horizon for reinvest_automatic)
  S(p,d) = the solve's periods d′ with yr[d] ≤ yr[d′] < yr[d] + lifetime[p,d] (raw lifetime)

Saving from process capacity retired in period d, currency/MW: the fixed cost of the existing capacity it no longer pays (each period's, with the factor the existing fixed cost has), and the salvage-value annuity over the discounted years of lifetime inside the horizon, the basis of an investment's annuity (so retiring existing capacity and building identical new capacity gains nothing).

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5246 (_obj_invest_divest)

docs.title: OBJ. invest_cost_n
docs.text:
Σ_{(n,d) ∈ nd_invest_set} v_invest_n[n,d]·state_unitsize[n] · annual_discounted[n,d] · bw[d]
  + Σ_{(n,d) ∈ nd_invest_set} v_invest_n[n,d]·state_unitsize[n] · lifetime_fixed_cost[n,d] · bw[d]

As invest_cost_p for storage capacity, currency/MWh of storage.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5268 (_obj_invest_divest)

docs.title: OBJ. divest_cost_n
docs.text:
− Σ_{(n,d) ∈ nd_divest_set} v_divest_n[n,d]·state_unitsize[n] · lifetime_fixed_cost_divest[n,d] · bw[d]
  − Σ_{(n,d) ∈ nd_divest_set} v_divest_n[n,d]·state_unitsize[n] · annual_divest_discounted[n,d] · bw[d]

As divest_cost_p for storage capacity (W over ndd_divest_active's window).

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5282 (_obj_invest_divest)

docs.title: OBJ. existing_fixed_cost
docs.text:
Σ_{(e,d)} existing[e,d] · fixed_cost[e,d] · inflation_op[d] · bw[d]
  bw = pd_branch_weight, factor 1 when absent

Fixed cost of the capacity that exists in each period, currency (fixed_cost in currency/MW/year). A constant: it moves the objective value but not the solution. Added only with include_existing_fixed_cost; when pd_branch_weight is present, periods without a weight row drop out.

Source: flextool/engine/model/core.py:5306 (_obj_existing_fixed_cost)

docs.title: DC power flow
docs.text: DC power flow: linearised AC flow on the connections of a DC power-flow network.

docs.title: VAR. v_angle
docs.text:
−π ≤ v_angle[n,d,t] ≤ π   ∀ n ∈ node_dc_power_flow, (d,t) ∈ dt

Voltage angle of node n, radians (π = 3.14159265). Variable bounds are scalar, so the reference nodes are pinned to 0 by dc_reference_angle_eq.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_dc_power_flow.py:184 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_angle (coarse-angle nodes)
docs.text:
Names: v_angle

−π ≤ v_angle[n,d,b] ≤ π   ∀ n ∈ coarse-angle nodes, (d,b) the coarse steps of n (b = its first fine step)
  coarse-angle node = a node of a DC network component whose every line is a coarse process and whose
  nodes all have the same coarse steps (flex_data.coarse_angle_steps)

One angle per coarse step, held over its fine steps (a level: b.v_angle is indexed on every fine step, _coarse_flows.alias). Every node of a component with a DC line at the solve's step keeps an angle per solve step, so the fine line keeps its per-step physics.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_dc_power_flow.py:189 (add_variables)

docs.title: EQ. dc_reference_angle_eq
docs.text:
v_angle[n,d,t] = 0   ∀ n ∈ node_reference_angle, (d,t) ∈ dt
  (a coarse-angle node: (d,b) its coarse steps, b = the step's first fine step)

Fixes the angle reference of each connected DC network.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_dc_power_flow.py:233 (_eq_reference_angle)

docs.title: EQ. dc_flow_eq
docs.text:
(v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] − v_flow_back[p,s,k,d,t]) · unitsize[p]
  = susceptance[p] · (v_angle[s,d,t] − v_angle[k,d,t])
  ∀ (p,s,k) ∈ DC arcs (dc_arcs_frame), (d,t) ∈ dt

Linearised AC flow: the signed flow (MW) on a DC arc follows the angle difference of its end nodes. v_flow_back is absent when the model has no reverse-flow variable. The rows run over dt. Row rule (coarse steps): a coarse line whose both end nodes are coarse-angle nodes gets one row per coarse step, dc_flow_eq_coarse = the row's mean over the step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr; the susceptance is constant, so it is the row itself on one flow and two angles per step). Any other line keeps a row per solve step and reads a coarse flow at its constant value (a coarse line in a component with a fine DC line holds the angle difference of its per-step angles constant over the coarse step).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_dc_power_flow.py:258 (_eq_dc_flow)

docs.title: Unit commitment
docs.text: Unit commitment: units (and connections) online, startups, shutdowns and minimum up/down times.

docs.title: VAR. v_online_linear / v_startup_linear / v_shutdown_linear
docs.text:
Names: v_online_linear, v_startup_linear, v_shutdown_linear

v_online_linear[p,d,t], v_startup_linear[p,d,t], v_shutdown_linear[p,d,t] ≥ 0
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ p_online_dt, p ∈ process_online_linear

Units online, and units started / shut down: the change of units online, online_change (count of unitsize), continuous.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:46 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_online{sfx} / v_startup{sfx} / v_shutdown{sfx} (coarse processes)
docs.text:
Names: v_online_linear, v_online_integer, v_startup_linear, v_startup_integer, v_shutdown_linear, v_shutdown_integer

on[p,d,b], su[p,d,b], sd[p,d,b]   ∀ p ∈ processCoarse ∩ process_online, (d,b) the coarse steps of p
  (b = its first fine step b_first)

Units online once per coarse step, held over its fine steps (a level: b.v_online_* is indexed on every fine step, _coarse_flows.alias); the units started / shut down at the step's start (events: registered at b only, not aliased, so a sum over t counts each once and a fine row of an interior step has no event term).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:52 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_online_integer / v_startup_integer / v_shutdown_integer
docs.text:
Names: v_online_integer, v_startup_integer, v_shutdown_integer

v_online_integer[p,d,t] ∈ ℤ≥0, v_startup_integer[p,d,t], v_shutdown_integer[p,d,t] ≥ 0
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ p_online_dt, p ∈ process_online_integer

As the linear family, but units online are integer; startups and shutdowns stay continuous. Continuous when the solve's reduce_unit_detail_method relaxes integers (d.relax_integrality; same names, rows and _integer class).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:64 (add_variables)

docs.title: EQ. maxOnline_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxOnline_linear, maxOnline_integer

v_online[p,d,t] − Σ v_invest_p[p,d′] + Σ v_divest_p[p,d′]  ≤ existing_count[p,d]
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ p_idx

Units online cannot exceed the units built. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:141 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. online_change_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: online_change_linear, online_change_integer

v_online[p,d,t] − v_online_prev[p,d,t] − v_startup[p,d,t] + v_shutdown[p,d,t]  =  0
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ p_idx;   v_online_prev as derived above (three pieces)

The change in units online is the units started minus the units shut down (Backbone's q_startshut). With maxStartup / maxShutdown below, a startup without a unit coming online, or a shutdown without one going offline, is impossible; a fleet (unitsize \< built) can still start and stop units in the same step (both cost nothing extra on the ramp rows of a single-output arc, part C) — a single integer unit cannot (maxStartup / maxShutdown forbid it there).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:216 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxStartup_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxStartup_linear, maxStartup_integer

v_startup[p,d,t] − v_online[p,d,t]  ≤  0                                 ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ p_idx

Units started in a step are online in it.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:229 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxShutdown_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxShutdown_linear, maxShutdown_integer

v_shutdown[p,d,t] + v_online[p,d,t] − Σ v_invest_p[p,d″] + Σ v_divest_p[p,d″]  ≤  existing_count[p,d]
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ p_idx whose online predecessor is v_online of the SAME period d (a dt_ramp_link with
  d_previous = d, or a dt_online_wrap; the same-period predecessor keeps the shutdown bound)

Units shut down in a step are offline in it. Not built where the predecessor is in another period or carried from an earlier roll (capacity may differ there — a unit online at the end of the previous period / roll must still be able to "shut down" even if this step's capacity is lower); sd ≤ v_online_prev follows there from online_change + maxStartup instead (su ≤ on_t ⇒ sd = su − on_t + on_prev ≤ on_prev). A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:236 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxFlow_online_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxFlow_online_linear, maxFlow_online_integer

v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve_up[p,r,k,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve_down[p,r,s,d,t] · φ[p,s,k,d,t]
  ≤  κ[p,s,k] · ( v_online[p,d,t] · availability[p,d,t] − red_su[p,s,k,d,t] · v_startup[p,d,t]
                  − max(0, red_sd − red_su)[p,s,k,d,t] · v_shutdown[p,d,t⁺] )
  ∀ (p,s,k) capped arc of an online process, (d,t) ∈ dt;   φ as in maxFlow, units only;
  κ = capacity_max_coeff[p,s,k]

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:266 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxFlow_online_shutdown_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxFlow_online_shutdown_linear, maxFlow_online_shutdown_integer

(maxFlow_online LHS)
  ≤  κ · ( v_online · availability − red_sd · v_shutdown[p,d,t⁺]
           − max(0, red_su − red_sd) · v_startup[p,d,t] )
  ∀ rows of maxFlow_online with red_sd > 0 and a UNIQUE successor t⁺

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:273 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxFlow_online_shutdown_branch_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxFlow_online_shutdown_branch_linear, maxFlow_online_shutdown_branch_integer

(maxFlow_online LHS)
  ≤  κ · ( v_online · availability − red_sd · v_shutdown[p,d⁺,t⁺]
           − max(0, red_su − red_sd) · v_startup[p,d,t] )
  ∀ (row of maxFlow_online, successor (d⁺,t⁺) of (d,t)) with red_sd > 0, at a (d,t) with SEVERAL
    successors (a branch point: several mid-horizon branches continuing from the same trunk step)
red_su = max(0, availability − SU),
  SU = min(1, min_load[p,d,t] + ½ · ramp_speed_up · 60 · step_duration[d,t])
  over the sides of the arc with an up ramp limit (process_source_sink_ramp_limit_{sink,source}_up; the
  smaller SU when both); red_sd likewise with ramp_speed_down at the pre-shutdown step (d,t); 0 without a
  ramp limit.  (d⁺,t⁺) = a successor whose ramp predecessor (dt_ramp_link) is (d,t) — the same period
  (today's only case) or the next continuing period (#98).

A coarse process (processCoarse): the averaged twins maxFlow_online{sfx}_coarse,

  maxFlow_online_shutdown{sfx}_coarse and maxFlow_online_shutdown_branch{sfx}_coarse (_coarse_flows.add_cstr)
  with the reduction on the coarse grid: red_su[p,s,k,d,b] = max(0, ā_b − SU_b) at the start-ups of b and
  red_sd = max(0, ā_b − SD_b) at the shut-downs of the coarse successor b⁺ (the coarse step whose first
  step's ramp predecessor lies in b, _coarse_flows.coarse_links); ā_b, m̄l_b the Δt-weighted means over b,
  SU_b = m̄l_b + ½·ρ_b while ρ_b ≤ 1 − m̄l_b, else 1 − (1 − m̄l_b)²/(2·ρ_b), ρ_b = ramp_speed_up · 60 · Δ_b
  (the mean share over the whole step of a unit started at its start that ramps up to full load within
  it; SD_b with the down speed: a unit stopping at the end of b); κ its step mean.

A unit's flow and the reserve that raises it — upward reserve at the arc's sink and "consume more" downward reserve at its source — are limited by the units online (spinning reserve: an offline unit holds neither). The reserve terms are maxFlow's (units only; an online connection's reserve is in connection_reserve_*_online_*). Units starting in step t reach at most SU of their capacity on average over the step (synchronised at min load, then ramping as fast as they may: half a step's ramp on average; owner question Q-c14a-A), units shutting down after step t at most SD in t. Two rows, so capacity online for a single step gets the smaller of the two limits instead of both reductions (exact for any mix of starts and stops; GMPL's one row with both reductions forbids one-step runs). At a branch point (several successors of one (d,t): several mid-horizon branches continuing from the same trunk step) the shutdown cross-term cannot be split across the single maxFlow_online row (one v_flow[t] variable, one row); it is dropped there (maxFlow_online keeps only its startup term, a valid — looser — bound) and maxFlow_online_shutdown_branch gives the tight, correctly-isolated bound per branch instead: summing the branches' v_shutdown into one row would let several mutually-exclusive branches each buy back a whole unit of ramp room from the trunk step. Only capped arcs (direct arcs and indirect output arcs, see _capped_arcs): indirect input arcs are tied to the outputs by conversion_indirect, and conversion_flow_coeff = 0 arcs are uncapped. Availability and capacity_max_coeff are densified to their 1.0 defaults so an unauthored unit keeps its row. The reduction is per arc (a multi-output unit's maxOutputSum_online is not reduced).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:278 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxFlow_back_online_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxFlow_back_online_linear, maxFlow_back_online_integer

v_flow_back[p,s,k,d,t]  ≤  κ[p,s,k] · availability[p,d,t] · v_online[p,d,t]
  ∀ (p,s,k) ∈ twoway1var_arcs with p online, (d,t) ∈ dt;   κ = capacity_max_coeff (1.0 defaults)

The reverse flow of a one-variable connection is limited by the units online, as its v_flow is by maxFlow_online: one online status covers both directions (the mirror of maxFlow_back). No reserve term (connection reserve has its own rows, connection_reserve_*). DC power-flow lines never get here (a startup_method on them raises in core._prepare).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:380 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxInputFlow_online_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxInputFlow_online_linear, maxInputFlow_online_integer

v_flow[p,s,p,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve_down[p,r,s,d,t]
  ≤ input_cap[p,s,p,d,t] · ( v_online[p,d,t] · x(availability)[p,d,t] − red_su · v_startup[p,d,t]
                             − max(0, red_sd − red_su) · v_shutdown[p,d,t⁺] )
  ∀ (p,s,p) input arc of an online indirect unit that is in reserve_down_input_arcs or has a source-side
    ramp limit with a reduction, (d,t) ∈ dt
  input_cap = p_indirect_input_cap (input_share_max × full-load input per unit of capacity)

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:404 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxInputFlow_online_shutdown_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxInputFlow_online_shutdown_linear, maxInputFlow_online_shutdown_integer

(maxInputFlow_online LHS) ≤ input_cap · ( v_online · x(availability) − red_sd · v_shutdown[p,d,t⁺]
                                          − max(0, red_su − red_sd) · v_startup[p,d,t] )
  ∀ rows of maxInputFlow_online with red_sd > 0 and a UNIQUE successor t⁺

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:412 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxInputFlow_online_shutdown_branch_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxInputFlow_online_shutdown_branch_linear, maxInputFlow_online_shutdown_branch_integer

(maxInputFlow_online LHS) ≤ input_cap · ( v_online · x(availability) − red_sd · v_shutdown[p,d⁺,t⁺]
                                          − max(0, red_su − red_sd) · v_startup[p,d,t] )
  ∀ (row of maxInputFlow_online, successor (d⁺,t⁺) of (d,t)) with red_sd > 0, at a (d,t) with several
    successors (a branch point) — split per successor exactly as maxFlow_online_shutdown_branch,
    never summed across mutually-exclusive branches.
x(y) = (slope · W(y) + section) / (slope · W(1) + section): the input drawn at output level y per unit of
  full-load input (W(y): the output-side fuel width filled up to y, as in p_indirect_input_cap; section
  only for min_load_efficiency units).  x(availability) replaces availability: the section is drawn per
  unit online, so availability × full-load input would cap the derated full output (x = availability
  without a section).
red_su = max(0, x(availability) − SU_in), SU_in = min(1, x(min_load) / input_share_max[p,s]
  + ½ · ramp_speed_up · 60 · step_duration) from the input node's ramp speeds (red_sd likewise), so a
  started unit can always draw what it needs at min load.  (d⁺,t⁺) = a successor whose ramp
  predecessor (dt_ramp_link) is (d,t) — the same period (today's only case) or the next continuing
  period (#98).

A coarse process: the averaged twins maxInputFlow_online{sfx}_coarse (+ _shutdown, _shutdown_branch), with

  input_cap and x(availability) as step means and the reduction on the coarse grid as in maxFlow_online
  (SU_in_b, SD_in_b from the step-mean x(min_load) / input_share_max and ρ_b).

The online analogue of maxFlow on an indirect unit's input arc: consuming more needs online capacity, and a starting (stopping) unit draws at most its startup (pre-shutdown) share of the input. The other inputs and the outputs are not adjusted (the per-arc simplification of the input-side floors).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:416 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. maxOutputSum_online_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: maxOutputSum_online_linear, maxOutputSum_online_integer

Σ_k v_flow[p,p,k,d,t] + Σ_k Σ_r v_reserve_up[p,r,k,d,t]  ≤  v_online[p,d,t] · availability[p,d,t]
  ∀ p ∈ process_indirect online with an output arc k, (p,d,t) ∈ p_idx

The online analogue of maxOutputSum: the sum of an indirect unit's outputs and of the upward reserve it holds at those outputs is limited by the units online. No capacity_max_coeff term; availability defaults to 1.0.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:440 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. minimum_uptime_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: minimum_uptime_linear, minimum_uptime_integer

v_online[p,d,t]  ≥  Σ_{(p,d′,t′,d,t) ∈ uptime_lookback} v_startup[p,d′,t′] + carry_up[p,d,t]
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ pdt_uptime_set ∩ this class ∩ online_rows

A unit started within the minimum uptime stays online. uptime_lookback = {(p,d′,t′,d,t) : (d′,t′) = (d,t), or (d′,t′) an ancestor of (d,t) along dt_ramp_link

  with elapsed(d′,t′ → d,t) = Σ step_duration over the chain from (d′,t′) up to, not including, (d,t)
  < min_uptime[p]} — the chain stops at a step without a ramp predecessor (solve start, a period that
  does not continue the previous one, a gap in the timeline, a representative-block start, a forecast
  branch that starts the solve); no cyclic wrap.

carry_up[p,d,t] = Σ_{h ∈ online_history} startup[p,h] over the root r ∈ dt_ramp_carry that is (d,t) or an

  ancestor of it along dt_ramp_link, with elapsed(r → d,t) + hours_to_end[h] < min_uptime[p]
  (d.uptime_carry, 0-filled; absent where no step continues the previous solve's last realized step).

A coarse process: rows and look-back only at the first fine steps of its coarse steps (its only start-ups),

  so elapsed(b′ → b) = Σ of the coarse durations from b′ up to b: a start-up counts while the steps since
  its start last less than min_uptime, i.e. min_uptime in whole coarse steps, rounded up.  A row whose
  look-back holds only its own step and no carry (the previous coarse step lasts ≥ min_uptime) is maxStartup
  and is not built.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:471 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. minimum_downtime_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: minimum_downtime_linear, minimum_downtime_integer

v_online[p,d,t] + Σ_{(p,d′,t′,d,t) ∈ downtime_lookback} v_shutdown[p,d′,t′] + carry_dn[p,d,t]
  − Σ v_invest_p[p,d″] + Σ v_divest_p[p,d″]  ≤  existing_count[p,d]
  ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ pdt_downtime_set ∩ this class

A unit shut down within the minimum downtime stays offline: existing − v_online ≥ Σ v_shutdown, with the invest/divest terms of maxOnline (without them an invest-only unit with existing = 0 could never be online). downtime_lookback: as uptime_lookback with min_downtime[p] (a coarse process as in minimum_uptime; a row

  whose look-back holds only its own step and no carry is implied by maxShutdown / online_change).

carry_dn: as carry_up with shutdown[p,h] and min_downtime[p] (d.downtime_carry, 0-filled). A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:513 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. online_fix_eq_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: online_fix_eq_linear, online_fix_eq_integer

v_online[p,d,t] = p_fix_online[p,d,t]   ∀ (p,d,t) ∈ online_rows with a p_fix_online value
  (a coarse process: at the first fine step of each coarse step; its pin is the same on every fine step of
  the step, or the process keeps the solve's step, flex_data.coarse_pin_varies)

In a separate-dispatch solve, pins units online to the commitment of the parent solve. Only declared v_online cells are pinned. p_fix_online is Utf8-keyed: it is joined to the native-typed index through Utf8 copies of (p, d, t).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_online.py:554 (add_constraints)

docs.title: The exact transfer method
docs.text: The exact transfer method: a connection flows in one direction per time step.

docs.title: VAR. v_exact_forward
docs.text:
v_exact_forward[p,d,t] ∈ {0, 1}   ∀ p ∈ process_exact with both arcs, (d,t) ∈ dt
1: the exact connection is set to its forward direction (node_1 → node_2 of connection__node__node) in the
step, 0: to the reverse direction.  One binary per connection: the whole connection transfers in one
direction.  No cost, no inter-temporal link.  Continuous in [0, 1] when the solve's reduce_unit_detail_method
relaxes integers (d.relax_integrality); every such level also clears process_exact, so the variable is then
not declared at all.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_exact.py:109 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_exact_forward (coarse connections)
docs.text:
Names: v_exact_forward

v_exact_forward[p,d,b] ∈ {0, 1}   ∀ p ∈ processCoarse ∩ process_exact, (d,b) the coarse steps of p
  (b = its first fine step b_first)

One direction per coarse step, held over its fine steps (a level: b.v_exact_forward is indexed on every fine step, _coarse_flows.alias), as the connection's flows are one value per coarse step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_exact.py:117 (add_variables)

docs.title: EQ. maxFlow_exact_forward / maxFlow_exact_reverse
docs.text:
Names: maxFlow_exact_forward, maxFlow_exact_reverse

v_flow[p,a,b,d,t] − Ū[p,a,b,d,t] · v_exact_forward[p,d,t]  ≤  0                         (forward)
v_flow[p,b,a,d,t] + Ū[p,b,a,d,t] · v_exact_forward[p,d,t]  ≤  Ū[p,b,a,d,t]              (reverse)
  ∀ p ∈ process_exact, (a,b) = (node_1, node_2), (d,t) ∈ dt
  Ū = p_flow_upper · capacity_max_coeff · availability (structural upper bound, units of unitsize)

An exact connection does not flow both ways at once (docs: the exact method needs a binary variable): in each step it carries flow in one direction only. maxFlow and maxFlow_online still bound each direction by the built and the online capacity; with investment Ū is a valid big-M (GMPL used v_online_integer and the unit count as the switch, which fails for a non-integer number of units). A coarse connection: maxFlow_exact_forward_coarse / maxFlow_exact_reverse_coarse, the rows' mean over each coarse step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr): v_flow ≤ Ū_b · v_exact_forward[p,d,b] with Ū_b the step mean of Ū — the flow and the direction are one value per step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_exact.py:138 (add_constraints)

docs.title: Unit output floors
docs.text: Unit output floors: minimum load, per-output floors and downward-reserve headroom.

docs.title: EQ. minFlow_minload_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: minFlow_minload_linear, minFlow_minload_integer

Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ A_p} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]  ≥  v_online[p,d,t] · min_load[p] + Rdn_p[p,d,t]
  ∀ p online with min_load, (p,d,t) ∈ p_idx
  process_minload = units with min_load > 0 on some (d,t) of this solve; not authored = 0 (no floor)

Minimum load, once per unit on the sum of its output measure. Rdn_p sums the reducing reserves over A_p, so downward reserve cannot take the unit below it. The floor is not scaled by availability.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_unit_floors.py:94 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. minFlow_output_floor_{linear,integer}
docs.text:
Names: minFlow_output_floor_linear, minFlow_output_floor_integer

v_flow[p,p,k,d,t]  ≥  v_online[p,d,t] · min_load[p] · capacity_min_coeff[p,k] + Rdn_k[p,k,d,t]
  ∀ (p,p,k) ∈ A_p of a multi-output unit with capacity_min_coeff[p,k] > 0, (p,d,t) ∈ p_idx

Per-output floor of a running unit; capacity_min_coeff must lie in [0, 1].

Source: flextool/engine/model/_unit_floors.py:114 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. minFlow_reserve
docs.text:
Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ A_p} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]  ≥  Rdn_p[p,d,t]
  ∀ unit p with a reducing reserve on A_p, (p,d,t) ∈ prundt without a minFlow_minload row

Zero floor of units without a minimum-load row: a unit cannot offer more downward reserve than its output. A coarse unit: minFlow_reserve_coarse, the row's mean over each coarse step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_unit_floors.py:144 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. minFlow_reserve_arc
docs.text:
v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]  ≥  Rdn_a[p,s,k,d,t]
  ∀ unit arc (p,s,k) with a reducing reserve, outside A_p or one of several arcs in A_p,
    (p,d,t) ∈ prundt, without a minFlow_output_floor row

Per-arc zero floor where the per-unit rows cannot see the arc. A coarse unit: minFlow_reserve_arc_coarse.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_unit_floors.py:163 (add_constraints)

docs.title: Group soft floors
docs.text: Group soft floors: capacity margin, inertia and the non-synchronous share limit.

docs.title: VAR. vq_capacity_margin
docs.text:
vq_capacity_margin[g,d] ≥ 0   ∀ g ∈ groupCapacityMargin, d ∈ D_inv
  D_inv = period_invest ∩ periods of dt: the solve's investment periods and, in a stochastic fan, the
  forecast branch periods of those anchors (a period label has no dt); one slack per forecast

Capacity margin shortfall of group g in period d, as a fraction of group_capacity_for_scaling: MW = vq_capacity_margin · group_capacity_for_scaling[g,d].

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:240 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_capacity_margin_slack_energy
docs.text:
v_capacity_margin_slack_energy[s,d] ≥ 0   ∀ s ∈ ∪_g S(g), d ∈ D_inv
  S(g) = the storage nodes with an upward balance slack that feed N(g) (capacity_margin_storage_slack_nodes)

The energy the upward balance slack of storage node s makes in period d, MWh (capacityMargin_slack_energy). The capacity margin takes it back, so slack energy cannot pose as storage delivery.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:252 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. vq_inertia
docs.text:
vq_inertia[g,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ g ∈ groupInertia, (d,t) ∈ dt

Inertia shortfall of group g, as a fraction of its inertia limit: MWs = vq_inertia · inertia_limit[g,d,t].

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:264 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. vq_inertia, vq_non_synchronous (coarse rows)
docs.text:
Names: vq_inertia, vq_non_synchronous

vq[g,d,b] ≥ 0   ∀ g whose inertia / non-synchronous row is averaged over coarse steps (the row rule), (d,b)
  the coarse steps of its row (b = the step's first fine step)

One shortfall per coarse step, held over its fine steps (a level, _coarse_flows.alias), as the row it relaxes.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:269 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. vq_non_synchronous
docs.text:
vq_non_synchronous[g,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ g ∈ groupNonSync, (d,t) ∈ dt

Non-synchronous infeed of group g above its allowed share, as a fraction of group_capacity_for_scaling: MW = vq_non_synchronous · group_capacity_for_scaling[g,d].

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:279 (add_variables)

docs.title: EQ. capacityMargin
docs.text:
Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ K(g)} (Σ_{d′} v_invest_p[p,d′] − Σ_{d′} v_divest_p[p,d′]) · unitsize[p] · κ[g,p,s,k,d,t] · icap[g,d]
  + Σ_{n ∈ N(g)} B¬FV[g,n,d,t] · icap[g,d]
  − Σ_{n ∈ N(g)} vq_state_down[n,d,t] · icap[g,d]
  − Σ_{s ∈ S(g)} v_capacity_margin_slack_energy[s,d] / Δt[d,t] · icap[g,d]
  + vq_capacity_margin[g,d]
  ≥ (M[g,d] + Σ_{n ∈ N(g)} demand[n,d,t]) · icap[g,d]
    − Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ K(g)} existing_count[p,d] · unitsize[p] · κ[g,p,s,k,d,t] · icap[g,d]
  ∀ g ∈ groupCapacityMargin, (d,t) ∈ dt : d ∈ D_inv
  groupCapacityMargin = groups with capacity_margin_method manual or share_of_peak
  D_inv = period_invest ∩ periods of dt (investment periods of the solve; a period label has no dt, so a
  fan contributes its forecast branch periods, one row per forecast); a solve without investment periods
  has no capacity margin
  N(g) = nodes of g in nodeBalance without a storage state;  icap = inv_group_cap = 1 / group_capacity_for_scaling
  F(g), V(g) = the unit output arcs into N(g) that count at capacity (capacity_margin_counted_arcs): not of a
  storage-backed unit (an input from a storage-state node, Σ input_share_max of its other inputs < 1), not of
  a unit with an input from N(g), not conversion_flow_coeff 0; V(g) those with an upper_limit or fixed profile
  K(g) = F(g) ∪ V(g), except that a unit of maxOutputSum (process_indirect) keeps only its first arc into N(g)
  κ = c · av (firm arc);  min(c, profile) · av (VRE arc);  min(av, Σ_{its arcs into N(g)} κ[arc]) (a unit of
  maxOutputSum: its outputs share one capacity);  c = capacity_max_coeff (p_arc_max_cap_coef, default 1),
  av = availability (default 1), profile = the smallest value of the arc's upper_limit and fixed profiles
  B¬FV[g,n,d,t] = the flow terms of nodeBalance_eq at n (balance_flow_terms, power: no Δt) without the arcs
  of F(g) ∪ V(g) and without the arcs left out (capacity_margin_left_out_arcs: the connections with both ends
  in N(g), the lossy converters inside g); the other units' output and input (slope, section), connections at
  N(g) (v_flow, v_flow_back), Benders half-flows; only at the (g, n) pairs of N(g).  The start-up input
  draw (startup_input_method, core._startup_draw: energy per start-up event, not capacity) is not a term, so
  with a draw at a node of N(g) (a unit started on grid electricity) the substituted balance below differs
  from the row by that draw
  S(g) = the storage nodes with an upward balance slack that feed N(g) through a storage-backed unit or a
  connection (capacity_margin_storage_slack_nodes);  v_capacity_margin_slack_energy = Σ_t vq_state_up · Δt
  (capacityMargin_slack_energy)
  demand = −inflow_real / Δt (pdtNodeInflow_per_step: the inflow before any energy margin)
  M[g,d] = capacity_margin[g,d] (manual)  |  capacity_margin_share[g,d] · P[g,d] (share_of_peak), 0 where not
  authored;  P[g,d] = max(0, max_t Σ_{n ∈ N(g)} demand[n,d,t]) over the period's original time series
  (before representative periods and new_stepduration; _capacity_margin_peak, resolve_capacity_margin)
  Σ_{d′} over edd_invest_set / edd_divest_active

Substituting the balance of each n ∈ N(g) (flow_FV + B¬FV + q_up − q_down = demand) gives

  Σ_{K} (counted capacity − flow into N(g)) + vq ≥ M + Σ_n q_up − (slack energy of S(g)) / Δt:

only firm and VRE headroom holds the margin. Each counted capacity bounds the unit's dispatch into N(g) (maxFlow, profile_flow_*, maxOutputSum), so the headroom is never negative. Storage-backed units, imports, exports and the group's own consumption count by their flow: imports and storage help by displacing firm output, exports add to the requirement. Energy dumped with vq_state_down does not count, and neither does energy that a storage node's balance slack makes (it could be stored and sent at the binding step). Lines and lossy converters inside g are left out, so their losses are not part of the requirement and shedding the demand behind them cannot lower it: unserved energy (q_up) leaves the row unchanged where counted capacity served it, and is priced once, by penalty_up. Units fed from fuel or commodity nodes count at capacity: the fuel is assumed to last through the peak. Existing capacity is a constant and moves to the right-hand side. The row is scaled by icap, which makes the slack a fraction of group_capacity_for_scaling. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Row rule (coarse steps): a group whose flow members (the processes of B¬FV) are all coarse processes gets one row per coarse step, capacityMargin_coarse = the row's Δt-weighted mean over the step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr): availability, the profile, the inflow and the slope act through their step means, so the margin covers the step-mean demand, not its peak (named in the coarse-flow behaviour notice). Otherwise the rows stay per solve step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:672 (_eq_capacity_margin)

docs.title: EQ. capacityMargin_slack_energy
docs.text:
v_capacity_margin_slack_energy[s,d] = Σ_{t : (d,t) ∈ dt} vq_state_up[s,d,t] · Δt[d,t]
  ∀ (s,d) of v_capacity_margin_slack_energy

The energy made by storage node s's upward balance slack over the period's steps. Energy made at any step can be stored and sent into the group at the binding step, so the capacityMargin row takes back the whole period's slack energy, in MW at its own step (÷ Δt): one variable per (s,d) keeps the rows sparse.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:850 (_eq_slack_energy)

docs.title: EQ. inertia_constraint
docs.text:
Σ_{side ∈ {source, sink}} Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ arcs_side(g)} x[p,·,d,t] · inertia_constant[p,side] · unitsize[p]
  + vq_inertia[g,d,t] · inertia_limit[g,d,t]
  ≥ inertia_limit[g,d,t]
  ∀ g ∈ groupInertia, (d,t) ∈ dt
  groupInertia = groups with has_inertia = yes;  inertia_limit[g,d,t] = the authored constant, period, time
  or period + time value (a time map covers every time step of the solve: a gap is an input error,
  _direct.check_group_limit_time_coverage), 0 for a group without any value or an authored 0 (no requirement:
  the row reads Σ … ≥ 0 and its slack is in no row)
  arcs_side(g) = arcs whose side node is in g and that carry an inertia constant on that side
  x = v_online[p,d,t] for p ∈ process_online (linear or integer), else v_flow[p,s,k,d,t]

Synchronous machines connected to the group's nodes supply inertia (MWs) in proportion to the units online, or to their flow when they have no online variable; the shortfall is penalised. The slack is a fraction of the limit. Row rule (coarse steps): a group whose inertia providers are all coarse processes gets one row per coarse step, inertia_constraint_coarse = the row's mean over the step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr), on one slack per step; the limit enters as its Δt-weighted step mean, and a limit that varies within a coarse step is named in the coarse-flow behaviour notice. Otherwise per solve step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:1221 (_eq_inertia)

docs.title: EQ. non_sync_constraint
docs.text:
Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ in_ns(g)} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t] · icap[g,d]
  + Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ back_in_ns(g)} v_flow_back[p,s,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t] · icap[g,d]
  + Σ_{n ∈ N(g)} positive_inflow[n,d,t] · icap[g,d]
  − vq_non_synchronous[g,d,t] · Δt[d,t]
  ≤ ns_limit[g,d,t] · icap[g,d] · ( Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ out_noEff(g)} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
                                + Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ out_eff(g)} v_flow[p,s,k,d,t] · slope[p,d,t] · unitsize[p]
                                                           · Δt[d,t]
                                + Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ out_eff(g), p ∈ process_min_load_eff}
                                      v_online[p,d,t] · section[p] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
                                + Σ_{(p,s,k) ∈ back_out(g)} v_flow_back[p,s,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
                                − Σ_{n ∈ N(g)} negative_inflow[n,d,t] )
  ∀ g ∈ groupNonSync, (d,t) ∈ dt
  groupNonSync = groups with has_non_synchronous = yes
  N(g) = nodes of g;  icap = inv_group_cap;  ns_limit = non_synchronous_limit (constant, period, time or
  period + time); a group without any value, and an authored 0, read as 0 (the right-hand side then
  vanishes: no non-synchronous infeed without the penalised slack); a time map covers every time step of
  the solve (a gap is an input error)
  in_ns(g)      = arcs (p,s,k), k ∈ N(g), (p,k) ∈ process_sink_nonSync, (p,g) ∉ inside
  back_in_ns(g) = twoway1var_arcs (p,s,k), s ∈ N(g), (p,s) ∈ process_sink_nonSync, (p,g) ∉ inside
  out_*(g)      = arcs (p,s,k), s ∈ N(g), (p,g) ∉ inside
  back_out(g)   = twoway1var_arcs (p,s,k), k ∈ N(g), (p,g) ∉ inside
  process_sink_nonSync = unit arcs with is_non_synchronous ∪ (c,n) for is_DC connections c and their nodes n
  inside = process_group_inside_nonSync: processes with a source and a different sink node in g
  positive_inflow / negative_inflow = max(inflow_real, 0) / min(inflow_real, 0);  inflow_real = the node's
  inflow before the invest-solve energy margin

Non-synchronous infeed into the group (flagged unit arcs, DC connections, positive exogenous inflow) is at most ns_limit times the group's supply, measured as the energy its nodes deliver to processes, exports and the real demand (an energy margin does not count); the excess is penalised. Flows between nodes of the group are neither (inside). The reverse flow of a one-variable / DC arc arrives at the arc's source and leaves its sink, lossless, as in nodeBalance_eq. The slack has no icap, which makes it a fraction of group_capacity_for_scaling. slope already holds the sink/source coefficient ratio of multi-arc processes. Row rule (coarse steps): a group whose processes are all coarse gets one row per coarse step, non_sync_constraint_coarse = the row's Δt-weighted mean over the step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr), on one slack per step: the non-synchronous share then holds for the step's energy, with the inflow, the slope and the limit through their step means (named in the coarse-flow behaviour notice). Otherwise per solve step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:1291 (_eq_non_sync)

docs.title: OBJ. inertia / non-synchronous / capacity margin slack
docs.text:
Names: inertia_penalty, non_synchronous_penalty, capacity_margin_penalty

+ Σ_{(g,d,t)} vq_inertia[g,d,t] · inertia_limit[g,d,t] · penalty_inertia[g,d] · w_op[d,t]
+ Σ_{(g,d,t)} vq_non_synchronous[g,d,t] · gcs[g,d] · penalty_non_synchronous[g,d] · w_op[d,t]
+ Σ_{g ∈ groupCapacityMargin, d ∈ D_inv} vq_capacity_margin[g,d] · gcs[g,d] · penalty_capacity_margin[g,d]
                                                        · inflation_op[d] · bw[d] · 1000
  gcs = group_capacity_for_scaling;  w_op = b.op_factor
  bw = pd_branch_weight[d], 1 where it has no row (deterministic and pre-reveal periods)

Each slack is scaled back to physical units (MWs, MW) and priced per hour of operation. The capacity margin is a planning quantity: it is priced once per period, weighted by pd_branch_weight, without step weights, and its penalty is authored in CUR/kW (× 1000 to CUR/MW). In a stochastic fan each forecast branch period keeps its own slack and pays it with its probability. The output layer (calc_slacks) reports the same costs for the realized periods (weight 1).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_group_slack.py:1429 (objective_terms)

docs.title: Reserves
docs.text: Reserves: capacity held back from the energy market to cover a reserve requirement of a node group.

docs.title: VAR. v_reserve
docs.text:
v_reserve[p,r,ud,n,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ (p,r,ud,n,d,t) ∈ prundt

Reserve r in direction ud (up / down) that process p holds for node n, in units of unitsize like v_flow: MW = v_reserve · unitsize[p].

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:527 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_reserve (coarse processes)
docs.text:
Names: v_reserve

v_reserve[p,r,ud,n,d,b] ≥ 0   ∀ p ∈ processCoarse, (p,r,ud,n) of prundt, (d,b) the coarse steps of p
  (b = its first fine step b_first)

One reserve per coarse step, held over its fine steps (a level: b.v_reserve is indexed on every fine step, _coarse_flows.alias); the requirement rows still read it at every solve step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:532 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. vq_reserve
docs.text:
0 ≤ vq_reserve[r,ud,g,d,t] ≤ 1   ∀ (r,ud,g) ∈ reserve_upDown_group, (d,t) ∈ dt

Shortfall of the reserve requirement of group g, as a fraction of the largest requirement: MW = vq_reserve · scale[r,ud,g,d,t] (reserve_shortfall_scale).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:541 (add_variables)

docs.title: VAR. v_reserve_total
docs.text:
v_reserve_total[r,ud,g,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ (r,ud,g) ∈ rug_total, (d,t) ∈ dt
  rug_total = (r,ud,g) with an n-1 row (in fail_g) and at least one provider in pruna_g

Reserve held for group g by all its providers, MW: at most reserve_sum (reserve_total_upper). Lets each n-1 row subtract the failing process's own reserve instead of repeating every other provider, and replaces reserve_sum in the timeseries / dynamic rows of the same group. No cost.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:550 (add_variables)

docs.title: EQ. reserveBalance_timeseries_eq
docs.text:
reserve_sum[r,ud,g,d,t] + vq_term[r,ud,g,d,t]  ≥ reservation[r,ud,g,d,t]
  ∀ (r,ud,g) ∈ reserve_upDown_group_method_timeseries, (d,t) ∈ dt
  reserve_sum is replaced by v_reserve_total for (r,ud,g) ∈ rug_total

Reserve held for a group covers its authored reservation timeseries, or the shortfall is penalised. RHS 0 when no reservation is authored. Reserve of every provider counts at full MW (no efficiency slope). A group that also has n-1 rows uses its total v_reserve_total: it is at most reserve_sum, enters only ≥ rows and has no cost, so the rows are equivalent (same optimal value for every right-hand side).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:684 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. reserveBalance_dynamic_eq
docs.text:
reserve_sum[r,ud,g,d,t] + vq_term[r,ud,g,d,t]
  ≥ Σ_{(p,s,n) ∈ process_source_sink, (p,r,ud,n) ∈ irr_g} v_flow[p,s,n,d,t] · unitsize[p] · ratio[p,r,ud,n]
  + Σ_{(p,n,k) ∈ eff_out, (p,r,ud,n) ∈ irr_g}
      (v_flow[p,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · slope[p,d,t] + v_online[p,d,t] · section[p,d,t] · unitsize[p])
      · ratio[p,r,ud,n]
  + Σ_{(p,n,k) ∈ process_source_sink \ eff_out, (p,r,ud,n) ∈ irr_g} v_flow[p,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[p]
      · ratio[p,r,ud,n]
  + Σ_{(p,n,k) ∈ twoway1var_arcs, (p,r,ud,n) ∈ irr_g} v_flow_back[p,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · ratio[p,r,ud,n]
  + Σ_{(p,s,n) ∈ twoway1var_arcs, (p,r,ud,n) ∈ irr_g} v_flow_back[p,s,n,d,t] · unitsize[p] · ratio[p,r,ud,n]
  + group_demand[r,ud,g,d,t]
  ∀ (r,ud,g) ∈ reserve_upDown_group_method_dynamic, (d,t) ∈ dt
  group_demand = ratio_g[r,ud,g] · Σ_{n : (g,n) ∈ group_node} max(−inflow[n,d,t], 0) / Δt[d,t]
  ratio_g = reserve__upDown__group.increase_reserve_ratio;  inflow in MWh per step without the
            energy margin (p_negative_inflow, the real demand), so group_demand is MW in the step
  irr_g   = process_reserve_upDown_node_increase_reserve_ratio with n ∈ group g
  ratio   = increase_reserve_ratio;   eff_out = process_source_sink_eff
  section term only for min_load_efficiency units with online variables (v_online_linear / _integer)
  reserve_sum is replaced by v_reserve_total for (r,ud,g) ∈ rug_total

The requirement grows with the flows into and out of the group's nodes (e.g. variable generation and consumption), in the upward and the downward rows alike: the ratio stands for the flow's variability, which can go either way (unlike large_failure, which is directional). A flow out of a node counts as drawn from it, as in nodeBalance_eq: on an efficiency arc the input is v_flow · slope plus the min-load section (_drawn_terms). The reverse flow of a one-variable (and DC) arc arrives at the arc's source and leaves its sink, as in nodeBalance_eq (lossless, no slope). The group term adds the demand of the group's nodes (negative inflow only; a node with positive inflow does not count) times the group's ratio (group_demand_requirement). RHS 0 when nothing drives it. A group that also has n-1 rows uses v_reserve_total, as in the timeseries rows.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:707 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. reserveBalance_up_n_1_eq / reserveBalance_down_n_1_eq
docs.text:
Names: reserveBalance_up_n_1_eq, reserveBalance_down_n_1_eq

v_reserve_total[r,ud,g,d,t]
  − Σ_{n : (f,r,ud,n) ∈ pruna_g} v_reserve[f,r,ud,n,d,t] · unitsize[f] · reliability[f,r,ud,n]
  + vq_term[r,ud,g,d,t]
  ≥ up:   Σ_{(f,s,n) ∈ process_source_sink, (f,r,ud,n) ∈ lfr_g} v_flow[f,s,n,d,t] · unitsize[f] · ratio[f,r,ud,n]
    down: Σ_{(f,n,k) ∈ eff_out, (f,r,ud,n) ∈ lfr_g} (v_flow[f,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[f] · slope[f,d,t]
                                                   + v_online[f,d,t] · section[f,d,t] · unitsize[f])
                                                  · ratio[f,r,ud,n]
          + Σ_{(f,n,k) ∈ process_source_sink \ eff_out, (f,r,ud,n) ∈ lfr_g} v_flow[f,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[f]
              · ratio[f,r,ud,n]
  + up:   Σ_{(f,n,k) ∈ twoway1var_arcs, (f,r,ud,n) ∈ lfr_g} v_flow_back[f,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[f] · ratio[f,r,ud,n]
    down: Σ_{(f,s,n) ∈ twoway1var_arcs, (f,r,ud,n) ∈ lfr_g} v_flow_back[f,s,n,d,t] · unitsize[f] · ratio[f,r,ud,n]
  ∀ (r,ud,g,f) ∈ fail_g, (d,t) ∈ dt
  pruna_g = the providers of the reserve_sum above, per group
  lfr_g   = process_reserve_upDown_node_large_failure_ratio with n ∈ group g,
            (r,ud,g) ∈ reserve_upDown_group_method_n_1 with ud = up / down
  fail_g  = (r,ud,g,f): f in lfr_g with a flow (v_flow or v_flow_back) into (up) / out of (down) a node of g
  ratio   = large_failure_ratio;   f is the row dim p_fail;   eff_out, section as in the dynamic row

Reserve covers the loss of each large process f separately (the largest failure binds): upward reserve the loss of its output into the group, downward reserve the loss of its consumption from the group. The failing process's own reserve, at every node of the group, does not count: it is subtracted from the group total. All rows of a group share vq_term, so the priced shortfall is the largest deficit. The lost consumption is the flow the process draws from the node, as in nodeBalance_eq (output · slope plus the min-load section on an efficiency arc); a lost output counts at unitsize. A one-variable (or DC) connection also fails while flowing backwards: its v_flow_back arrives at the arc's source and leaves its sink (lossless). No row for a group without a failing process; a group without providers (or without reliability data) has no v_reserve_total term. Nonzeros grow with providers + failing processes per group.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:789 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. reserve_total_upper
docs.text:
v_reserve_total[r,ud,g,d,t] − reserve_sum[r,ud,g,d,t]  ≤  0   ∀ (r,ud,g) ∈ rug_total, (d,t) ∈ dt
v_reserve_total enters only ≥ requirement rows, with a positive sign,
and has no cost, so an upper bound is enough: the n-1 rows above are
exactly the per-provider form (one row per failing process, its own
reserve not counted) with v_reserve_total = reserve_sum, and the
timeseries / dynamic rows of the group are those with reserve_sum.

This needs reserve_sum ≥ 0, which holds because providers have reliability > 0 (process_reserve_upDown_node_active) and unitsize > 0; otherwise v_reserve_total ≥ 0 would add a constraint. When v_reserve_total > 0, the magnitude of this row's dual is the sum of the duals of the group-step's rows that use v_reserve_total (opposite sign convention: ≤ row against ≥ rows).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:863 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. reserve_process_upward / reserve_process_downward
docs.text:
Names: reserve_process_upward, reserve_process_downward

v_reserve[p,r,ud,n,d,t] − max_share[p,r,ud,n] · c[p,n,d,t] · Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_p[p,d′]
  + max_share[p,r,ud,n] · c[p,n,d,t] · Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active} v_divest_p[p,d′]
  ≤ max_share[p,r,ud,n] · c[p,n,d,t] · existing_count[p,d]
  ∀ (p,r,ud,n,d,t) ∈ prundt with ud = up / down (a coarse process: reserve_process_{upward,downward}_coarse,
    the row's mean over each coarse step, _coarse_flows.add_cstr: one reserve per step under the step-mean c)
  c = 1 at a node the process feeds, and for connections;
  at an input node n of a unit (n the source of one of its arcs and not a sink):
    c = input_cap[p,n,p,d,t]           indirect unit (input_share_max × full-load input per unit)
    c = slope[p,d,t] + section[p,d,t]  direct unit's input→output arc (full-load input = capacity /
                                       efficiency; section only for min_load_efficiency units with
                                       online variables)
    c = 1                              sink-less unit (its capacity is the input), and
                                       conversion_flow_coeff = 0 inputs

A process holds at most max_share of the built capacity of its flow at that node as reserve (units of unitsize; built = existing + invested − retired, also for units with online variables). At an input node the capacity is the input's (_input_capacity_factor). max_share not authored → no reserve (RHS 0). A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:882 (add_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. reserve_fix_eq
docs.text:
v_reserve[p,r,ud,n,d,t] = p_fix_reserve[p,r,ud,n,d,t]   ∀ (p,r,ud,n,d,t) ∈ prundt with a p_fix_reserve value
  (a coarse process: at the first fine step of each coarse step; its pin is the same on every fine step of
  the step, or the process keeps the solve's step, flex_data.coarse_pin_varies)

In a realization solve, pins the reserve each process holds to the non-anticipativity-tied reserve of the stochastic solve it realizes (that solve's reference forecast on its tied steps). Only declared v_reserve cells are pinned. p_fix_reserve is Utf8-keyed: it is joined to the native-typed index through Utf8 copies.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:940 (_add_reserve_fix)

docs.title: EQ. connection_reserve_up / connection_reserve_down
docs.text:
Names: connection_reserve_up, connection_reserve_down

x_in[p,n,d,t] − s_out[p,n,d,t] · x_out[p,n,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,up,n,d,t]
  − M_in · Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_p[p,d′]
  + M_in · Σ_{(p,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active} v_divest_p[p,d′]  ≤  C_in[p,n,d,t]   (up)
x_out[p,n,d,t] − x_in[p,n,d,t] / s_out[p,n,d,t] + Σ_r v_reserve[p,r,down,n,d,t] / s_out[p,n,d,t]
  − M_out · Σ v_invest_p[p,d′] + M_out · Σ v_divest_p[p,d′]  ≤  C_out[p,n,d,t]                         (down)
  ∀ connection p (process_source_sink \ process_unit) with (p,r,ud,n,d,t) ∈ prundt, ud = up (down)
  x_in  = flow of p arriving at n:  v_flow[p,m,n,d,t], or v_flow_back[p,n,m,d,t] of a one-variable / DC arc
  x_out = flow of p leaving n (measured where it arrives):  v_flow[p,n,m,d,t], or v_flow_back[p,m,n,d,t]
  s_out = slope[p,d,t] when x_out is v_flow on an arc of process_source_sink_eff, else 1 (power drawn at n per
          unit of x_out)

          b.flow_cap_mult: capacity_max_coeff · availability · existing_count and coef · availability)

docs.text:
Names: connection_reserve_up_online_linear, connection_reserve_up_online_integer, connection_reserve_down_online_linear, connection_reserve_down_online_integer

  in-channel arc / the down row's out-channel arc)   ∀ rows above with p online and that channel present

docs.title: EQ. connection_reserve_{up,down}_exact
docs.text:
Names: connection_reserve_up_exact, connection_reserve_down_exact

  same LHS − Ū · v_exact_forward[p,d,t]  ≤  0     when that channel is the exact connection's forward arc
  same LHS + Ū · v_exact_forward[p,d,t]  ≤  Ū     when it is the reverse arc
  ∀ rows above with p ∈ process_exact;  Ū = p_flow_upper · capacity_max_coeff · availability of the arc

A coarse connection: each family as \<family>_coarse, the row's mean over each coarse step

  (_coarse_flows.add_cstr): one reserve and one flow per step under the step-mean capacity and availability.

A connection's reserve at a node is limited by its net position there: upward reserve by the free capacity into n plus the flow out of n it can stop, downward reserve by the flow into n it can stop plus the free capacity out of n (converted to power at n by the efficiency). One row per capacity bound (built, online, exact direction) of the channel whose capacity the reserve uses, so each row holds one channel's capacity. A one-way connection gets a floor at its sending node (upward reserve ≤ what it draws there) and its old capacity row at the receiving node; a one-variable connection's rows bound the reserve by its signed flow (C ∓ f). Reserve at a node the connection does not link is 0. maxFlow / maxFlow_online carry the upward reserve of units only (b.reserve_up_to_sink_units); the profile cap profile_flow_upper_limit keeps the connection's in-arc term (conservative: it does not count stopping the out-flow). A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:1109 (_add_connection_reserve_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. reserve_storage_up_floor
docs.text:
v_state[n,d,t] · state_unitsize[n]
  − Σ_{(p,r,ud,nb,g) ∈ providers_up(n)} v_reserve[p,r,ud,nb,d,t] · unitsize[p] · duration[r,ud,g] · slope[p,d,t]
  ≥ 0
  ∀ n ∈ storage nodes of upward providers, (d,t) ∈ dt
  providers_up: upward reserve for nb by a process with source n ∈ nodeState and sink nb, or by a
    one-variable / DC connection whose arc runs nb → n (its reverse flow v_flow_back runs n → nb; slope 1)

Upward reserve from storage is backed by stored energy (MWh) for the reserve duration (hours); slope = 1/η converts output to energy drawn. Reliability is not applied: the energy matches the full committed MW. No slack: with v_reserve = 0 the row is v_state ≥ 0, so a provider that cannot sustain the duration commits less and the group pays the shortfall penalty. Couples to the intra-period state v_state only, not to the representative-period state v_state_inter. Row rule: a storage node n whose state is coarse (constant within its coarse step, stateConstantCoarse_eq) and whose providers are all coarse processes gets one row per coarse step, reserve_storage_up_floor_coarse (the row's mean over the step of the providers' partition, _coarse_flows.add_cstr): the reserve, the state and the step-mean slope are then all one value per step. Otherwise the row stays per solve step and reads a coarse provider's reserve at its constant value. The same for reserve_storage_down_headroom.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_reserve.py:1443 (_add_storage_energy_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. reserve_storage_down_headroom

  + Σ_{(n,d′,d) ∈ ndd_divest_active} v_divest_n[n,d′] · state_unitsize[n]
  − Σ_{(n,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_n[n,d′] · state_unitsize[n]
  ≤ state_upper[n,d,t] · state_unitsize[n]
  ∀ n ∈ storage nodes of downward providers, (d,t) ∈ dt
  providers_down: downward reserve for nb by a process with source nb and sink n ∈ nodeState, or by a
    one-variable / DC connection whose arc runs n → nb (its reverse flow runs nb → n; slope 1)

Downward reserve into storage needs free storage capacity (MWh) for the reserve duration; 1/slope = η converts input to energy stored. The capacity terms are those of maxState, in MWh. Same notes as the floor. A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  Divest: v_divest_p with group_retire_{max,min}_period over gd_divest_period (same restriction)
  _n: the node analogues with v_invest_n / v_divest_n and state_unitsize[n]

With a construction lead time the invest rows count capacity coming online in d:

  Σ_{p : (g,p) ∈ group_entity} (Σ_{(p,o,d) ∈ edd_invest_commission} v_invest_p[p,o] · unitsize[p]
                                + carried_commission[p,d])  ≤ / ≥ group_invest_{max,min}_period[g,d]
  over the (g,d) where a member's decision comes online, g with a per-period limit (c(o) = o without a lead
  time: the form above).

Bounds the capacity a group of entities builds or retires in one period, MW (MWh for storage nodes); processes and storage nodes of a group get separate rows. Group retire_{max,min}_period is not a schema parameter, so the divest rows are reachable only with off-schema data. Under recourse ``gd_invest_period`` / ``gd_divest_period`` list a group's own invest/divest period's branch periods too (#67); a branch period with no member actually invest/divest-eligible there (e.g. a branch's own 0 beating the anchor's cost, #82) gets no row, not a vacuous 0 ≥ a positive floor.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_cumulative_invest.py:452 (_eq_group_entity_period)

Σ_{p:(g,p)∈group_entity} Σ_{d∈D(leaf)} v_invest_p[p,d]·unitsize[p]
  ≤ max(0, group_invest_max_total[g] − Σ_{p∈g} prior_inv[p])   (maxInvestGroup_entity_total[_path]_p)
  ≥ max(0, group_invest_min_total[g] − Σ_{p∈g} prior_inv[p])   (minInvestGroup_entity_total_path_p)
  ∀ g ∈ g_invest_total (, leaf)
  prior_inv[p] = p_entity_invested[p]  (capacity realized by all earlier solves of the
    chain); the group's prior sums every member of the axis kind, not only those with the
    variable in THIS solve — their earlier investment still counts
  _n: storage-node members, state_unitsize[n]
  max: _path (one row per (g, leaf)) only under recourse, like the entity max side.
  min: always _path — a plain per-group row, summed across alternative branches, would let
    one branch meet the floor for every branch (Q3, same reason as the entity min side)

Changed from per-(g,d) "invested and still alive" rows to one row per group (per leaf); processes and storage nodes of a group get separate rows.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_cumulative_invest.py:567 (_eq_group_invest_total)
