docs.title: EQ. {max,min}InvestGroup_entity_cumulative
docs.text:
Names: maxInvestGroup_entity_cumulative, minInvestGroup_entity_cumulative

Σ_{p : (g,p) ∈ group_entity} Σ_{d′ : (p,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_p[p,d′] · unitsize[p]
  + Σ_{n : (g,n) ∈ group_entity} Σ_{d′ : (n,d′,d) ∈ edd_invest_set} v_invest_n[n,d′] · state_unitsize[n]
  − Σ_{p : (g,p) ∈ group_entity} Σ_{d′ : (p,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active} v_divest_p[p,d′] · unitsize[p]
  − Σ_{n : (g,n) ∈ group_entity} Σ_{d′ : (n,d′,d) ∈ ndd_divest_active} v_divest_n[n,d′] · state_unitsize[n]
  ≤ cumulative_max_capacity[g,d] − Σ_{e : (g,e) ∈ group_entity} existing[e,d]   (max…)
  ≥ cumulative_min_capacity[g,d] − Σ_{e : (g,e) ∈ group_entity} existing[e,d]   (min…)
  ∀ g ∈ g_invest_cumulative (invest_method = cumulative_limits, #5/B-Q3), d with a cap value
  and some member alive (invest) or retirable (divest) in d

Keeps the capacity of a group in a period (existing + invested and still alive − every retirement up to and including d, #30b) within its cumulative limits (schema "[MW or MWh]"); processes and storage nodes share one row. Max rows: groups that author the cap at all (any period), restricted to periods the group actually has a candidate (g, d) row for; FA-12 (check_max_cap) then catches a period that same group's own map leaves out — mirrors the entity-level cumulative row (previously this family had no FA-12 check at all, unlike the entity-level row). Min rows: the periods with a value other than 0 (a min of 0 is no floor). A period map that leaves out an investment period of the solve cannot reach here: pass 1b refuses it (``require_period_coverage``). Capacity invested by earlier solves of a chain is not counted (pre-existing, separate item). A retirement v_divest[e,d′] counts in d iff (e,d′,d) ∈ edd_divest_active (ndd_divest_active):

  d′ ≤ d < EOL[e], the end of life of e's pre-existing capacity (none for reinvest_automatic).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_cumulative_invest.py:697 (_eq_group_invest_cumulative)

docs.title: EQ. {max,min}Cumulative_flow_solve[_path]
docs.text:
Names: maxCumulative_flow_solve, maxCumulative_flow_solve_path, minCumulative_flow_solve, minCumulative_flow_solve_path

Σ_{d,t} F[g,d,t]·w_y[d,t]  ≤ max_cumulative_flow[g] · Σ_{d,t} w_y[d,t]   (max…)
                           ≥ min_cumulative_flow[g] · Σ_{d,t} w_y[d,t]   (min…)
  ∀ g with a max / min_cumulative_flow (, per leaf under recourse)
  F = net flow into the group (_group_flow)
  w_y[d,t] = step_duration[d,t]·timestep_weight[d,t]·r[d]
  r[d] = (years_represented[d]/period_share[d]) / max_d′(years_represented[d′]/period_share[d′])

Limits the energy flowing into a flow group over the solve to an average power times the weighted hours of the solve — the same weighting every operational cost term already carries (op_factor), so a representative period or an unequal roll window does not under/over-count its hours. Under recourse each scenario path gets its own row (_path, one per (g, leaf), leaf_rows): a plain per-group row, summed across branches, would let one branch's surplus cover another's deficit. Constraints carry no stochastic branch weight — each branch must respect the limit on its own, unlike the objective (owner decision).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_cumulative_invest.py:813 (_eq_cumulative_flow_solve)

docs.title: EQ. {max,min}Cumulative_flow_period
docs.text:
Names: maxCumulative_flow_period, minCumulative_flow_period

Σ_t F[g,d,t]·sd[d,t]·tw[d,t]  ≤ max_cumulative_flow[g,d] · Σ_t sd[d,t]·tw[d,t]   (max…)
                              ≥ min_cumulative_flow[g,d] · Σ_t sd[d,t]·tw[d,t]   (min…)
  ∀ (g,d) with a max / min_cumulative_flow
  F = net flow into the group (_group_flow); sd = step_duration, tw = timestep_weight

Limits the energy flowing into a flow group in each period to an average power times the weighted hours of the period — the same timestep_weight every operational cost term already carries (op_factor), so a representative-period step does not count as a full unweighted hour. A branch period that authors no value of its own reads its anchor's value (broadcast_to_period's branch-period inheritance); it still gets its own (g,d) row here, not merged with the anchor's — the continuation fan always starts at a solve's first step (_branch.py, d_leaf_lf), so no period is ever split into an anchor fragment and a branch fragment within one solve, and there is nothing to merge.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_cumulative_invest.py:871 (_eq_cumulative_flow_period)

docs.title: EQ. {max,min}Instant_flow
docs.text:
Names: maxInstant_flow, minInstant_flow

F[g,d,t]  ≤ max_instant_flow[g,d,t]   (maxInstant_flow)
          ≥ min_instant_flow[g,d,t]   (minInstant_flow)
  ∀ (g,d,t) ∈ _instant_flow_support(cap, dt)
  F = net flow into the group (_group_flow), MW

Limits the net power flowing into a flow group in every step. The cap may be authored as a scalar, period map, time map or period-time map; the rows cover every active step of its shape. Row rule (coarse steps): a flow group whose processes are all coarse gets one row per coarse step, {max,min}Instant_flow_coarse = the row's Δt-weighted mean over the step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr): the step's constant net flow against the step-mean cap (named in the coarse-flow behaviour notice when the cap varies within a step). A group with a fine process keeps its rows per solve step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_cumulative_invest.py:909 (_eq_instant_flow)

docs.title: Commodity price ladder
docs.text: Commodity price ladder: a commodity bought in tiers, each with its own price and quantity.

docs.title: VAR. v_trade
docs.text:
v_trade[c,n,d,i] ≥ 0   ∀ (c,n,d,i) ∈ cndi_ladder = cndi_ladder_ann ∪ cndi_ladder_cum

Purchase of commodity c at node n in period d in price tier i, in units of the commodity unitsize: MWh = v_trade · commodity_unitsize[c].

Source: flextool/engine/model/_commodity_ladder.py:295 (add_variables)

docs.title: EQ. commodity_ladder_balance
docs.text:
Σ_i v_trade[c,n,d,i] · commodity_unitsize[c]
  = Σ_{(p,n,k,c) ∈ flow_from_commodity_eff, t}
      (v_flow[p,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · slope[p,d,t] + v_online[p,d,t] · section[p,d,t] · unitsize[p]) · w[d,t]
  + Σ_{(p,n,k,c) ∈ flow_from_commodity_noEff, t} v_flow[p,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · w[d,t]
  − Σ_{(p,s,n,c) ∈ flow_to_commodity, t}         v_flow[p,s,n,d,t] · unitsize[p] · w[d,t]
  + Σ_{(p,n,c) ∈ startup_from_commodity, t} v_startup[p,d,t] · startup_energy[p,n,d] · unitsize[p]
      · timestep_weight[d,t]   (start-up energy, MWh per event: no step_duration; core._startup_draw)
  ∀ (c,n,d) ∈ cnd_ladder;   w = step_duration · timestep_weight

The period's net purchase of commodity c at node n (buy − sell, MWh) is split into price tiers. The efficiency-arc term uses the shared fuel measure _eff_fuel_input (core.py), so min_load_efficiency units' part-load section fuel counts toward the tiers too, same as commodity_cost_eff / co2_price_eff / the CO2 caps (#56) — before this fix a ladder commodity bought by such a unit was under-counted by the part-load fuel. A term is absent when its flow set is empty or there are no processes.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_commodity_ladder.py:328 (_eq_ladder_balance)

docs.title: EQ. ladder_tier_cap_annual_roll
docs.text:
Σ_n v_trade[c,n,d,i] · commodity_unitsize[c]
  ≤  quantity_ann[c,i,d] · period_share[d] · f_d_k[d] − realized_ann[c,i,α(d)]
  ∀ (c,i,d) with (c,n,d,i) ∈ cndi_ladder_ann and quantity_ann[c,i,d] < 1e29
  f_d_k[d] = (realized hours of α(d) from earlier solves + this solve's hours of d) / complete hours of α(d)
  α(d) = the period label of a forecast branch period d, d itself otherwise; period_share, f_d_k and the
  realized carry of a forecast come from α(d) unless it has its own row: every forecast continues from
  its period's realized history (the realization solve's carry)
quantity_ann is a per-YEAR amount (GMPL "per-year MWh"): period_share[d] scales it down to this
period's own share of the modelled year, matching the price term's inflation_op/period_share
annualisation (#89) — a 48h solve of a 48h period gets 48h/8760 of the annual tier, not the whole
year's worth.  f_d_k[d] (1 outside rolling) further scales it to the share of the period's own
hours reached by the end of this roll's horizon (f_d_k already measures exactly that — see
p_f_d_k_from_source) — the quantity allocated so far, as of this roll.  realized_ann[c,i,d] (the
same per-(c,i,d) carried-purchases Param the cumulative ladder uses, 0 when absent) is what
earlier rolls already bought against that allocation, so the remaining budget can never go
negative: an earlier roll could buy at most up to its own (earlier) horizon end and realized
only part of that (#143's fix applies here too — no clamp needed, the row is feasible by
construction instead of approximately-compliant). Unlimited tiers (quantity ≥ 1e29) get no row.

Branch periods of a stochastic solve use their anchor period's quantity (and price) unless they have their own (inherit_branch_periods). share, f_d_k and the realized carry of a forecast come from α(d) unless it has its own row (branch_periods_inherit): every forecast continues from its period's realized history (the realization solve's carry); without it a null share/fdk would clamp the tier to 0, and a realized 0 would re-open the period's already-spent budget (#59).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_commodity_ladder.py:382 (_eq_tier_cap_annual)

docs.title: EQ. ladder_tier_cap_cumulative_roll
docs.text:
Σ_{n,d} v_trade[c,n,d,i] · commodity_unitsize[c]
  ≤  quantity_cum[c,i] · Σ_d (years_represented[d] · realized_hours[d] / 8760) − Σ_d realized[c,i,d]
  ∀ (c,i) ∈ ci_ladder_cumulative with quantity_cum[c,i] < 1e29;  (c,n,d,i) ∈ cndi_ladder_cum

Caps what tier i supplies over the whole modelled horizon. quantity_cum, like quantity_ann, is a per-modelled-YEAR amount: Σ_d (years_represented[d] · realized_hours[d] / 8760) is the real- calendar-years-equivalent of representative dispatch simulated so far — realized_hours[d]/8760 annualises each period's own realized representative-sample hours up to a full calendar year (the hours-form of period_share[d]·f_d_k[d], #89's annualisation), and years_represented[d] then multiplies that by the number of real calendar years period d stands for (co2_max_total scales its emissions cap the same way, docs: "each period's annualised emissions times the years it represents"); without it a period block representing several years was charged for only one (p_ladder_cum_weight, load_data). Sums over every period the chain has ever touched — not just the ones still active this roll — the same reason f_d_k itself is read from a provider CSV that folds finished periods back in (#143): without that, this sum would reset to the new period's own local progress each time the chain moved on, while realized kept climbing, eventually driving this row negative. "quantity allocated up to the end of this roll's horizon" is monotone non- decreasing across rolls — the same requirement #89's fix gives the annual cap — and realized (what earlier rolls actually bought, always ≤ what their own, earlier horizon end allocated) can never exceed it, so the row is feasible by construction; no clamp. Without p_ladder_cum_weight (load_data couldn't build the years_represented/realized_hours Param — e.g. a synthetic fixture that skips the derived-param pass) the weight is Σ f_d_k over the path's periods, fan labels left out (a member's f_d_k holds its period's realized hours), the pre-years_represented-fix formula; realized = tier MWh bought by earlier solves (0 when absent). Unlimited tiers get no row.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_commodity_ladder.py:491 (_eq_tier_cap_cumulative)

docs.title: EQ. ladder_tier_cap_cumulative_roll_path
docs.text:
Σ_{n, d∈D(leaf)} v_trade[c,n,d,i] · commodity_unitsize[c]
  ≤ quantity_cum[c,i] · ( Σ_{d∈D(leaf)} w[d] + Σ_{d∉period_in_use} w[d] ) − Σ_d realized[c,i,d]
  ∀ (c,i) ∈ ci_ladder_cumulative with quantity_cum[c,i] < 1e29, leaf ∈ d_leaf, when v_trade spans >1 leaf

One row per scenario path (#58): the pooled row's weight summed every forecast into one budget, letting the forecasts buy N× the tier between them. w[d] = years_represented[d]·realized_hours[d]/8760 (p_ladder_cum_weight; fallback f_d_k[d] with this solve's fan labels left out). D(leaf) = the leaf's branch periods, its fan labels and the shared pre-reveal periods (the (d, leaf) join of d_leaf, as in the invest/divest _path families' leaf_rows); a shared period's weight counts once on each path. The second sum is the periods earlier solves and rolls finished: one realized past shared by every path, matching realized, which is the chain-wide carry of what that past bought. Every period of period_in_use with a weight lies on some leaf (raises otherwise), so the second sum holds only the finished history; it is added only when non-zero. A chained earlier solve's period missing from this solve's p_years_represented.csv counts with years_represented 1 (as in the pooled row). No branch weight on the row: constraints are per path, the branch weights belong to the objective.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_commodity_ladder.py:535 (_eq_tier_cap_cumulative)

docs.title: OBJ. commodity ladder
docs.text:
Names: commodity_ladder_cost

+ Σ_{(c,n,d,i) ∈ cndi_ladder_cum} v_trade[c,n,d,i] · cu[c] · price_cum[c,i]
                                  · inflation_op[d] / period_share[d] · bw[d]
+ Σ_{(c,n,d,i) ∈ cndi_ladder_ann} v_trade[c,n,d,i] · cu[c] · price_ann[c,i,d]
                                  · inflation_op[d] / period_share[d] · bw[d]
  cu = commodity_unitsize;  bw[d] = branch_weight[d,t], the same for every t of d (factor 1 outside
  stochastic solves)

Each tier's purchase at its price, annualised per period and weighted by the probability of the period's branch, as w_op weights the other operational costs. v_trade is already a period sum, so no step duration or timestep weight enters; a period whose branch weight varies over t raises.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_commodity_ladder.py:632 (objective_terms)

docs.title: Non-anticipativity
docs.text: Non-anticipativity: decisions taken before a forecast is revealed are equal in every forecast branch.

docs.title: EQ. non_anticipativity_storage_use
docs.text:
net[n,d,t] − net[n,b,t] = 0
  net[n,d,t] = Σ_{(p,s,n) ∈ flow_to_n} v_flow[p,s,n,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
             − Σ_{(p,n,k) ∈ flow_from_nodeBalance_eff}
                 (v_flow[p,n,k,d,t] · slope[p,d,t] + v_online[p,d,t] · section[p,d,t]) · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
             − Σ_{(p,n,k) ∈ flow_from_nodeBalance_noEff} v_flow[p,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
             − Σ_{(p,s,n) ∈ twoway1var_arcs} v_flow_back[p,s,n,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
             + Σ_{(p,n,k) ∈ twoway1var_arcs} v_flow_back[p,n,k,d,t] · unitsize[p] · Δt[d,t]
             − Σ_{(p,n) ∈ startup_to_balance} v_startup[p,d,t] · startup_energy[p,n,d] · unitsize[p]
  ∀ n ∈ nodes of groupStochastic ∩ nodeBalance, (d,b) ∈ forecast star, (d,t) ∈ tied steps
  section only for p ∈ process_min_load_eff (v_online = v_online_linear or v_online_integer)

The net flow into a stochastic node is the same in every forecast over the tied steps: exactly the flow terms of nodeBalance_eq, built by the same helper (_balance_terms.balance_flow_terms). It ties the flows, not v_state, and leaves out the balance slacks: they could otherwise absorb a flow difference. The section input counts because efficiency and min_load may differ between forecasts. A node of the group without an energy balance (e.g. a commodity node) has no balance flow terms to tie. A coarse process has one flow column per coarse step, so a tie at one of its steps holds the whole step; it is coarse only where each of its coarse steps is wholly tied or wholly untied (flex_data.coarse_tie_straddles). Row rule (coarse steps): a node whose processes are all coarse gets one tie per wholly tied coarse step, non_anticipativity_storage_use_coarse = the row's Δt-weighted mean over the step (_coarse_flows.add_cstr, the weights of forecast d's coarse step, which the reference forecast b shares over the tied steps): the forecasts' net energy into n over the step is the same, with a forecast-specific slope or section through its step mean. A node with a fine process keeps its ties per solve step, reading the coarse flows constant.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_non_anticipativity.py:208 (add_dispatch_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. non_anticipativity_storage_state_first
docs.text:
v_state[n,d,t_first(d)] − v_state[n,b,t_first(d)] = 0
  ∀ n ∈ nodes of groupStochastic, (d,b) ∈ forecast star, t_first(d) = first tied step of d,
    only where the tied steps of d are fewer than the v_state steps of (n,d)

The net-charge tie above fixes the shape of the state over the tied steps but leaves a constant offset between forecasts; this row removes it. Where the tied steps cover the whole horizon the state is already bound at both ends (start and reference value) and the row is redundant, so it is emitted only when untied steps follow (rolling). The offset is pinned at the optimum, not by construction: interior drift stays feasible where balance slack or forecast-specific inflow absorbs it. v_online and v_reserve need no analogue: their ties pin the variable itself at every tied step.

Source: flextool/engine/model/_non_anticipativity.py:254 (add_dispatch_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. non_anticipativity_rp_block_start
docs.text:
v_state_rp_start[n,d,t] − v_state_rp_start[n,b,t] = 0
  ∀ n ∈ nodes of groupStochastic ∩ nodeState_rp, (d,b) ∈ forecast star, (d,t) ∈ tied steps,
    (d,t) and (b,t) ∈ rp_block_first, (n,d,b,t) ∉ the rows of non_anticipativity_storage_state_first

A representative block starts from a free level; inside the tie window it is a decision taken before the forecast is known, so it is the same in every forecast (the net-flow tie fixes only the shape of the state within the block). A block whose first step already has a non_anticipativity_storage_state_first row is left out: there v_state at t_first (the end of the block's first step) is tied, so its start is tied up to the forecasts' difference in balance slack (and inflow) over that step; the net flows of the step are tied already. The base-period levels v_state_inter need no tie of their own: inside the window they follow from the tied net flows, these block starts and the shared chain start (the trunk period's end level, or rp_inter_period_fan_start).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_non_anticipativity.py:279 (add_dispatch_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. non_anticipativity_online_{integer,linear}
docs.text:
Names: non_anticipativity_online_integer, non_anticipativity_online_linear

v_online[p,d,t] − v_online[p,b,t] = 0
  ∀ p ∈ process_online_{integer,linear}, (d,b) ∈ forecast star, (d,t) ∈ tied steps,
    (p,d,t) and (p,b,t) ∈ p_online_dt

Units online are the same in every forecast over the tied steps, the committed section decided before the forecast is known (inside a fan: the committed cells of its period label, solve_data/committed_in_fan). With no tied step (shared_operation_periods = [], or a rolling fan only in the look-ahead) they are free. A coarse process (processCoarse) is tied once per coarse step, at its first fine step: it is coarse only where each of its coarse steps is wholly tied or wholly untied and both forecasts have the same coarse steps (flex_data.coarse_tie_straddles).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_non_anticipativity.py:326 (add_dispatch_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. non_anticipativity_reserve
docs.text:
v_reserve[p,r,ud,n,d,t] − v_reserve[p,r,ud,n,b,t] = 0
  ∀ (p,r,ud,n) ∈ process_reserve_upDown_node_active, (d,b) ∈ forecast star, (d,t) ∈ tied steps

Reserve offered is the same in every forecast over the tied steps. A coarse process is tied once per coarse step, at its first fine step (coarse only where each coarse step is wholly tied or untied, as the units online).

Source: flextool/engine/model/_non_anticipativity.py:365 (add_dispatch_constraints)

docs.title: EQ. non_anticipativity_{invest,divest}_{p,n}
docs.text:
Names: non_anticipativity_invest_p, non_anticipativity_invest_n, non_anticipativity_divest_p, non_anticipativity_divest_n

v_invest[e,d] − v_invest[e,b] = 0,   v_divest[e,d] − v_divest[e,b] = 0
  ∀ (d,b) ∈ pd_non_anticipativity, (e,d) and (e,b) ∈ {pd,nd}_{invest,divest}_set,
    e = process (p) or node (n); the divest sets hold the periods with pre-existing capacity only

Investment and divestment inside the window are the same in every branch. Divestment must be tied too: under recourse it has a column per branch like investment, and a free divestment would let the net capacity existing + invest − divest differ across branches. pd_non_anticipativity.b holds period labels typed on the branch axis; it is re-typed on the period axis, the axis of the invest sets' d and of the variable view's b. The (e,b) check drops every pair when the branches have no invest column of their own.

Σ_{t∈b} w[K,d,b,t] · ( LHS_t − RHS_t )  {≤,=,≥}  E[K,d,b]      w = Δt / Δ_b,  Δ_b = Σ_{t∈b} Δt
  ∀ coarse row key K (a coarse process p, or a row key whose every member is coarse: row_partition — a group
  g, a user constraint cn, a stochastic node n, a DC arc between coarse-angle nodes), (…, d, b)
  its coarse steps (b = its first fine step b_first);  LHS_t / RHS_t = the level terms of the fine row of the
  family at (d, t);  E = the row's event terms on the coarse grid (start-ups at b, shut-downs at the coarse
  successor b⁺: the capacity reduction of maxFlow_online / maxInputFlow_online and their _shutdown rows);
  only where the fine family has a row of K at every fine step of b — a key whose rows cover part of b (a
  limit authored on part of the step) keeps its fine rows there, reading the coarse terms at their constant
  value (_split)

The fine row's Δt-weighted average over the coarse step. The flow is one column per coarse step, so its own term averages to itself; time-varying availability, profile, efficiency (slope) and capacity coefficients act through their step means (the mean of a product, not the product of means); so do the units online and the reserve (one value per coarse step) times a time-varying availability, profile or minimum load. With one time-varying limit per arc the averaged row allows exactly the energy the fine rows allow over the step; with several it is their convex relaxation (it can be looser).

docs.title: Benders decomposition master
docs.text: Benders (Option C) regional decomposition — master + multi-cut loop.

docs.title: VAR. C
docs.text:
C[conn] ≥ 0   ∀ conn ∈ the connections of the cross-region arcs

Capacity invested in a trade connection, in units of its unitsize (as v_invest_p): one column per connection, summed over the periods it may invest in (the hand master, master="hand").

Source: flextool/engine/solve/_benders.py:1114 (_build)

docs.title: VAR. f
docs.text:
f[p,source,sink,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ cross-region arcs (p,source,sink), (d,t) on the arc's grid

Trade flow on a cross-region arc, in units of the connection's unitsize, keyed by the same (p,source,sink) triple the region half-flows carry so the pin values map 1:1.

Source: flextool/engine/solve/_benders.py:1122 (_build)

docs.title: VAR. eta
docs.text:
eta[r] ≥ eta_floor   ∀ regions r

The recourse cost of region r that the optimality cuts bound from below (scaled objective units). The large-negative finite floor (_ETA_FLOOR_MULT) keeps the cut-less iter-0 master optimal without cutting off the optimum; the f̄ = 0 bootstrap then seeds the real cuts.

Source: flextool/engine/solve/_benders.py:1134 (_build)

docs.title: EQ. trade_capacity
docs.text:
C[conn] − f[p,source,sink,d,t] ≥ 0   ∀ arcs (p,source,sink) of conn, (d,t) on the arc's grid

A trade flow stays within the capacity invested in its connection. Both sides are in units of the connection's unitsize, so it cancels. One row per (arc, d, t); the connection key is a join column so Where aligns f with its connection's C. Existing capacity of the connection is not in the row: the hand master treats every trade connection as greenfield (the flextool master path counts it).

Source: flextool/engine/solve/_benders.py:1143 (_build)

docs.title: EQ. maxInvest
docs.text:
C[conn] ≤ Σ_{d ∈ invest periods of conn} max_units[conn,d]   ∀ conn

Caps the invested capacity (max_units = p_entity_max_units, units of unitsize), mirroring the monolith's maxInvest_var_bound; it also bounds the master before enough cuts accumulate.

Source: flextool/engine/solve/_benders.py:1166 (_build)

docs.title: OBJ. master_objective
docs.text:
Σ_conn C_cost[conn] · C[conn] + Σ_r eta[r]
  C_cost[conn] = s · unitsize[conn] · Σ_{d ∈ invest periods of conn} (annual_discounted[conn,d]
                                                                  + lifetime_fixed_cost[conn,d])
  s = obj_scale (scale_the_objective), so the master lives in the scaled space of the regions

The invest cost of the trade capacity, as OBJ. invest_cost_p of the monolith, plus the regions' recourse costs.

Source: flextool/engine/solve/_benders.py:1185 (_build)

docs.title: Results catalogue
docs.text: Every result table FlexTool writes, generated from the code. A table is written to output_parquet/<scenario>/<table>.parquet, and with CSV output to output_csv/<scenario>/ under the CSV name of the default output settings. The parquet's top column level is scenario; the levels below it are listed as column levels. Membership sets are flat tables whose first column is scenario, followed by the listed row levels; timeline_breaks is a flat (period, time) table. Units are the default convention of FlexTool (MW, MWh, CUR); see Model outputs for what the results mean and how they are computed.

docs.title: Parameter catalogue
docs.text:
Every input parameter of this FlexTool version, generated from its database schema: one table per entity class. The topic pages of Model parameters explain what the parameters do and how they work together; the parameter groups page explains the group labels.

  • Unit is the unit of the default convention (MW, MWh, CUR for the model currency, tonnes of CO2). FlexTool does not check units: a model may use others consistently. dimensionless is a ratio or a share; MW or count is a number of units when virtual_unitsize is above 0.
  • Default is the default of the schema. When FlexTool runs it may derive or default other values; the results show what the model used.
  • Allowed shapes says what a value may be: a constant, or a map (an indexed table) over periods, over time, or over both (one or two index levels); a stochastic-time map has three levels (branch, analysis_time, time). A map whose index is something else names it: a map: constraint name → coefficient. Where FlexTool checks the shape, this is what it accepts; otherwise it comes from the description or the value types of the schema (a map with n index levels).
  • The same table as an Excel data dictionary, with the parameters a database uses: python -m flextool.docs_build --xlsx catalogue.xlsx --input-db input_data.sqlite (see Make a data dictionary for your model).

docs.title: commodity
docs.text:
A fuel or other product bought from, or sold to, outside the modelled system at a price (natural gas, coal, hydrogen for export).

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition co2_content tCO2/MWh a constant emission Constant. price CUR/MWh or other unit a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level) basics Price of the commodity. Constant, period or time. price_ladder_annual CUR/MWh; MWh/a a map over tiers and price / quantity (2 levels), or a map over periods, tiers and price / quantity (3 levels) basics Stepped supply curve for price_method price_ladder_annual. Map of tier → price and quantity (optionally per period). Quantity is per year; a shorter solve gets its share by the hours it covers. quantity = inf can be used to mark an unlimited last tier. price_ladder_cumulative CUR/MWh; MWh a map over tiers and price / quantity (2 levels) basics Stepped supply curve for price_method='price_ladder_cumulative'. 2d map with rows 'tier,price,quantity' — one row per tier, giving the tier's unit price and its cumulative quantity cap. 1-based integer tier index. quantity=inf marks an unbounded tail tier. Period-agnostic — the cap is a single total across the full model horizon. price_method a constant price price, price_ladder_annual, price_ladder_cumulative basics How the commodity's price enters the LP. 'price' = scalar or time-series price x flow (current behaviour); 'price_ladder_annual' = stepped supply curve with a per-year quantity cap per tier; 'price_ladder_cumulative' = stepped supply curve with a total-model quantity cap per tier (handoff-carried across rolling solves). unitsize MWh a constant basics Per-commodity scaling coefficient applied to the v_trade tier variable when the commodity uses the price-ladder feature (gated by commodity.price_method = price_ladder_annual or price_ladder_cumulative). When set, v_trade is expressed in user-MWh divided by this value; pick the unitsize so the largest tier quantity sits at O(10) in the scaled LP. The coefficient multiplies v_trade in the commodity_ladder_balance LHS, the per-tier cap LHS, and the per-tier objective term. When absent (the default), the price-ladder consumer substitutes 1.0 internally so v_trade is in user-MWh (identity scaling). Ignored entirely when commodity.price_method is not a price_ladder_* value.

docs.title: connection
docs.text:
A link that moves energy between two nodes: a transmission line, an interconnector or a pipeline, with its capacity, losses and costs.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition availability dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) 1 basics e.g. 0.9 means 90%. Fraction of capacity available for connection flows. Constant, period, time or period+time. constraint_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the connection's capacity in service in each period on the left side of the user constraint (existing plus investments still in service minus retirements). Coefficient per MW. Capacity in construction is not included. constraint_cumulative_pre_built_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity in service at the start of each period on the left side of the user constraint. This is existing capacity plus capacity that came online in earlier periods, minus earlier retirements. Capacity coming online in the period itself is in the invested term. Coefficient per MW. constraint_in_construction_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity in construction in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Capacity is in construction from the period of the investment decision until it comes online. It is zero without a construction lead time. Coefficient per MW. constraint_invested_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity that comes online in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Without a construction lead time, this is the capacity invested in that period. Coefficient per MW. constraint_online_coeff unit of the constraint per unit online a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the number of units of the connection online in each time step on the left side of the user constraint. One unit is virtual_unitsize; without it, the largest existing capacity, else 1000 MW (set virtual_unitsize when the capacity is invested). Needs online variables (startup_method linear or binary); a coefficient without them is an error. With linear startup the number is continuous. For MW online, use the unit size (MW per unit) as the coefficient. constraint_retired_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity retired in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Coefficient per MW. construction_lead_time years a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Time from the investment decision until the capacity starts to operate. The start is rounded to the start of a period (see construction_lead_time_method). Investments whose rounded start is after the end of the solve or the model horizon are not offered, with a warning. Constant or period. Default 0. construction_lead_time_method a constant immediate, closest_seam, previous_seam, next_seam investment How the start of operation (decision year plus construction_lead_time) is rounded to the start of a period. immediate: no lead time, the capacity operates from the decision period. closest_seam: the nearest period start; a tie goes to the later one. previous_seam: the period start before. next_seam: the period start after. Without a value: immediate when there is no lead time, else closest_seam. cumulative_max_capacity MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Maximum cumulative capacity (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. cumulative_min_capacity MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Minimum cumulative capacity (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. delay hours a constant, or a map with 1 index level tech_advanced Not yet applied to connections (planned): a connection delay is ignored (the connection is modelled as if no delay were set) and the model warns about it. Model a delayed flow with a unit. Intended meaning: a time delay between the input node and the output node, either a constant time difference in hours or a map of time differences (index: time difference in hours, value: weight; the weights should sum to 1). discount_rate dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) 0.05 investment e.g. 0.05 means 5% per year. Discount rate for investments (WACC). Reflects the financing cost and risk premium for this technology. When the model inflation_rate > 0, this should be a nominal rate. When inflation_rate = 0, this should be a real rate. Used to annualize investment costs over the lifetime: annuity = invest_cost x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-lifetime). 0 gives the straight-line annuity invest_cost / lifetime. No value means 0.05. Must be 0 or above. Constant or period. efficiency dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) 1 basics e.g. 0.9 means 90%. Efficiency of the connection. Constant, period, time or period+time. existing MW or count a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) basics Existing capacity or number of units. If virtual_unitsize is given, then existing is the number of units (capacity = existing × virtual_unitsize). Otherwise existing is the existing capacity of a single unit (typically in MW). Constant or period. fixed_cost CUR/kW/a a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Annual fixed cost. New capacity pays it only while it operates. Constant or period. invest_cost CUR/kW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Overnight investment cost of new capacity. It is paid as an annuity over the years the capacity operates. Construction time costs with their interest must be included here. Constant or period: the value of the period when the capacity is built (comes online) is used. invest_max_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Largest allowed capacity coming online in each period. Existing capacity and retirements do not change it. With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_max_total MW a constant investment Largest allowed total investment over all solves. Every investment decision counts, also reinvestments and investments that are no longer in service. Retirements and existing capacity do not reduce it. To limit the capacity in service, use cumulative_max_capacity. Constant. invest_method a constant not_allowed not_allowed, invest_no_limit, invest_period, invest_total, invest_period_total, retire_no_limit, retire_period, retire_total, retire_period_total, invest_retire_no_limit, invest_retire_period, invest_retire_total, invest_retire_period_total, cumulative_limits investment Choice of investment method: not_allowed, invest and retire indicate availability of investment and retirement. no_limit removes all limits even if there are limiting values set. period uses values set in invest/retire_max/min_period. total uses values set in invest/retire_max/min_total. invest_min_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Smallest required capacity coming online in each period. Existing capacity and retirements do not change it. With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_min_total MW a constant investment Smallest required total investment over all solves. Every investment decision counts, also reinvestments and investments that are no longer in service. Retirements and existing capacity do not reduce it. To limit the capacity in service, use cumulative_max_capacity. Constant. is_DC a constant no yes, no network Whether the connection is DC. Its flow into a group with a non-synchronous limit counts as non-synchronous, in both directions. Default no. lifetime years a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Operating lifetime. It starts when the capacity starts to operate: with a construction lead time, after the construction. Used with the interest rate to calculate the annuity. What happens at the end of the lifetime depends on lifetime_method: reinvest_automatic keeps the capacity to the end of the model horizon, reinvest_choice retires it, no_investment retires it once. Required when the connection invests or retires with a cost (invest_cost, salvage_value), and when lifetime_method is reinvest_choice or no_investment (also for existing capacity without investment). Constant or period. lifetime_method a constant reinvest_automatic reinvest_automatic, reinvest_choice, no_investment investment Choice how the investments behave after unit runs out of lifetime. Automatic reinvestment causes the model to keep the capacity until the end of model horizon and applies the annualized investment cost without further model choice. Choice of reinvestment removes the capacity at the end of the lifetime and the model needs to decide how much new capacity is to be built. other_operational_cost CUR/MWh a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) basics Other operational variable cost for trasferring over the connection. Constant, period, time or period+time. reactance p.u. a constant network Per-unit reactance of the transmission line. Used for DC power flow when the connection is within a nodeGroup that has transfer_method set to dc_power_flow_with_angles. The susceptance used in the flow equation is base_MVA / reactance. retire_max_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Largest allowed retirement in each period. Counts only what is retired in that period; existing capacity and investments do not change it. Constant or period. retire_max_total MW a constant retirement Largest allowed total retirement over all solves. Investments and existing capacity do not change it. Constant. retire_min_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Smallest required retirement in each period. Counts only what is retired in that period; existing capacity and investments do not change it. Constant or period. retire_min_total MW a constant retirement Smallest required total retirement over all solves. Investments and existing capacity do not change it. Constant. salvage_value CUR/kW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Salvage value for retiring capacity. Constant or period. startup_cost CUR/MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) tech_advanced Cost of starting up one MW of capacity. Constant or period. startup_method a constant no_startup no_startup, linear, binary tech_advanced Gives the connection online capacity in both directions. Flows and reserves are limited by the online capacity, and startup_cost is paid per MW brought online. No minimum load or minimum up/down time. Not allowed for dc_power_flow_with_angles lines. transfer_method a constant regular no_losses_no_variable_cost, regular, exact, variable_cost_only, unidirectional basics Choice of transfer method. Options: regular (default), no_losses_no_variable_cost, variable_cost_only, exact, unidirectional. 'unidirectional' restricts flow to source → sink only (single non-negative variable); 'regular'/'exact'/'variable_cost_only' are bidirectional two-variable variants; 'no_losses_no_variable_cost' is a single signed variable with no losses and no VOM. virtual_unitsize MW a constant basics Size of one unit. With it, existing is the number of units. Binary startups commit whole units of this size. Investments and retirements are continuous; their limits are in MW. No value: the existing capacity, or 1000 MW without it.

docs.title: constraint
docs.text:
A constraint the user writes: its terms (flows, capacities, storage states, units online) come from the constraint_..._coeff parameters of the other classes; here its sense and its constant. A constraint with only capacity terms holds once per period, otherwise once per time step.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition constant the constraint's own unit a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) 0 constraint Right-hand side of the user constraint. A period map gives each period its own value; it must cover every period of the solve. Constant or period. constraint_period_method a constant per_timestep per_timestep, period_total constraint How the user constraint is applied in time. per_timestep (default): a row for every time step (a constraint with only capacity terms has one row per period). period_total: one row per period over the sum of the time steps, each step's terms times its duration and weight, annualised (divided by the period's share of a year): flows count in MWh per year and units online in unit-hours per year; capacity terms and their existing capacity are multiplied by the hours of the year, and constant is per year. A state coefficient is not allowed. In a rolling solve the row is written only in a roll that realizes the whole period; otherwise the solve leaves it out with a warning. Constant. is_enabled a constant yes yes, no constraint Whether the entity is enabled. Set to 'no' to disable without deleting the entity. Constant. sense a constant equal greater_than, less_than, equal constraint The sense of the constraint ('greater_than', 'less_than' or 'equal').

docs.title: flowGroup
docs.text:
A set of flows (a unit or a connection into or out of a node) that share limits, such as a maximum instant flow or a cumulative flow over a period.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition flow_aggregator a constant none none, dispatch_plots_only, standalone_aggregator_only, both output Choice of flow-aggregation method for this flowGroup: 'none' (used for flow limits only, no aggregated output), 'dispatch_plots_only' (used as an aggregated flowGroup within 'print_dispatch' group of nodes - do not include one flow in multiple flow aggregators to avoid double counting), 'standalone_aggregator_only' (just make time series available for manual output processing / simple plots), 'both'. max_cumulative_flow MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) flow_limit Largest allowed average flow into the group. A constant gives one limit per solve; a period map gives one limit per period. Average flow times the weighted hours gives the energy limit. Constant or period. max_instant_flow MW a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) flow_limit Maximum instantenous flow for the aggregated flow of all group members. Constant, period, time or period+time. min_cumulative_flow MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) flow_limit Smallest required average flow into the group. A constant gives one limit per solve; a period map gives one limit per period. Average flow times the weighted hours gives the energy limit. Constant or period. min_instant_flow MW a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) flow_limit Minimum instantenous flow for the aggregated flow of all group members. Constant, period, time or period+time.

docs.title: group
docs.text:
A set of units, connections and nodes that share limits or targets (investment limits, CO2 limits, capacity margin, inertia) or that are reported together.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition base_MVA MVA a constant network Base power for the per-unit system used in DC power flow. Default 100. susceptance = base_MVA / reactance_pu. candidate_precapacity_to_avoid_big_m MW a constant network Small pre-existing capacity assigned to investment candidate connections in DC power flow groups that have zero existing capacity. This avoids the need for big-M / MIP constraints by ensuring the angle constraint is always active. Default 0.1 MW. The value should be small enough to not affect results but large enough for numerical stability. capacity_margin MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Capacity the group needs above its demand at every time step of an investment period. Used only with capacity_margin_method manual. No value means 0 (the demand must still be covered). Constant or period. capacity_margin_method a constant none none, manual, share_of_peak investment Whether the group needs a capacity margin in investment solves, and how the margin is given. none (default): no margin. manual: capacity_margin MW. share_of_peak: capacity_margin_share times the group's peak demand in the period. At every time step of an investment period, the capacity of the group's firm units (capacity x availability x capacity_max_coeff) and VRE units (capacity x profile x availability) must cover the group's demand plus the margin. Units fed from a storage node, connections and the units consuming from the group count by their actual flow, so exports add to the requirement; connections and lossy units inside the group are left out (their losses are not required). Units fed from fuel or commodity nodes count at capacity: the fuel is assumed to last. capacity_margin_share dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment e.g. 0.15 means 15%. Capacity margin as a share of the group's peak demand: the largest sum of the demand of the group's nodes over the period's full time series (before representative periods and new_stepduration). Used only with capacity_margin_method share_of_peak. No value means 0. Constant or period. co2_max_period tCO2/a a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) emission Largest annual CO2 emissions in each period. In a rolling solve, each roll may use the part of the limit its horizon reaches, minus what earlier rolls already emitted in that period. Constant or period. co2_max_total tCO2 a constant emission Largest CO2 emissions over the whole model horizon. Each period counts its annual emissions times its years_represented. Rolling solves and chains of solves pass the remaining budget on. Each stochastic forecast gets the whole remaining budget. Constant. co2_method a constant none none, price, period, total, price_period, price_total, period_total, price_period_total emission Choice of the CO2 method: none, price, period, total, price_period, price_total, period_total, price_period_total co2_price CUR/tCO2 a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) emission CO2 price for a group of nodes. Constant, period, time or period+time. cumulative_max_capacity MW or MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Maximum cumulative capacity for a group of entities (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. cumulative_min_capacity MW or MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Minimum cumulative capacity for a group of entities (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. decomposition_method a constant none none, benders_regional solve_advanced Decomposition strategy to apply to this group. Currently supported: 'none' (no decomposition — default), 'benders_regional' (group is solved as an independent region in the Benders master/subproblem decomposition, with shared-commodity trade coupling handled by the master). has_inertia a constant no yes, no network Whether the group has an inertia constraint. Without yes, inertia_limit is ignored. has_non_synchronous a constant no yes, no network Whether the group has a non-synchronous share limit. Without yes, non_synchronous_limit is ignored. include_stochastics a constant no yes, no model Includes the stochastic branches to be used for the nodes/units/connections in this group inertia_limit MWs a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) network Minimum synchronous inertia in the group. Used only when has_inertia is yes. No value (or 0) means no requirement. Constant, period, time or period+time. A time map must give a value for every time step of the solve (a missing time step is an error). Over a coarse time step the row uses the step mean. invest_max_period MW or MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Largest allowed capacity coming online in each period, summed over the group's units and connections (MW) and storage nodes (MWh). With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_max_total MW or MWh a constant investment Largest allowed total investment of the group over all solves. Every investment decision counts; retirements do not reduce it. Constant. invest_method a constant not_active not_active, invest_no_limit, invest_period, invest_total, invest_period_total, retire_no_limit, retire_period, retire_total, retire_period_total, invest_retire_no_limit, invest_retire_period, invest_retire_total, invest_retire_period_total, cumulative_limits investment How the group limits investment and retirement of its members. not_active: the group sets no limits. invest / retire / invest_retire: which decisions the limits apply to. _period uses the …_period limits, _total the …_total limits, _period_total both. no_limit: no limits even if values are set. cumulative_limits: uses the cumulative capacity limits. invest_min_period MW or MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Smallest required capacity coming online in each period, summed over the group's units and connections (MW) and storage nodes (MWh). With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_min_total MW or MWh a constant investment Smallest required total investment of the group over all solves. Every investment decision counts; retirements do not reduce it. Constant. new_stepduration hours a constant timeline Balances the energy of the group's nodes once per step of this length instead of every time step, e.g. daily hydrogen next to hourly electricity. Within the step, energy can move freely between time steps, and a storage node has one state per step. A unit or connection whose nodes are all in such groups also uses the longer step: it has one flow, units online and reserve per step, so the model gets smaller. Its limits, and rows that combine only such units and connections, apply to their average over the step, and ramp limits apply between steps. Units and connections with a node outside these groups keep the solve's time step, and so do those with a delay (an info line names them). Listing units or connections has no effect. Must be a multiple of the solve's step. non_synchronous_limit dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) network e.g. 0.8 means 80%. Largest share of non-synchronous supply in the group, measured against the real demand. Flows between the group's nodes do not count. Used only when has_non_synchronous is yes; no value means 0. Constant, period, time or period+time. A time map must give a value for every time step of the solve (a missing time step is an error). Over a coarse time step the row uses the step mean. penalty_capacity_margin CUR/kW/a a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) 5000 investment Penalty for violating the capacity margin constraint. Uses operational discounting (not annualized over lifetime like investment costs), so the value is not directly comparable to annualized investment costs. Constant or period. penalty_inertia CUR/MWs per hour a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) 5000 network Penalty for violating the inertia constraint. Cost scales with the duration of the violation. Constant or period. penalty_non_synchronous CUR/MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) 5000 network Penalty for violating the non synchronous constraint. Constant or period. print_dispatch a constant yes, no output Combines unit/connection flows, flowGroup aggregated flows, and other balance elements (slack, demand, internal_losses, etc.) into a set of timeseries and a preconfigured plot per group. print_indicators a constant yes, no output Output indicators for the set of nodes in the group (Loss of Load, VRE generation, etc.). reference_node a constant network Name of the reference bus node (angle fixed to zero) for DC power flow. Optional — if not specified, automatically selected as the node with the largest existing capacity in each connected component of the DC power flow network. retire_max_period MW or MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Largest allowed retirement in each period, summed over the group's members. Needs a retire …_period option in the group's invest_method. Constant or period. retire_max_total MW or MWh a constant retirement Largest allowed total retirement of the group over all solves. Needs a retire …_total option in the group's invest_method. Constant. retire_min_period MW or MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Smallest required retirement in each period, summed over the group's members. Needs a retire …_period option in the group's invest_method. Constant or period. retire_min_total MW or MWh a constant retirement Smallest required total retirement of the group over all solves. Needs a retire …_total option in the group's invest_method. Constant. share_loss_of_load a constant no equal, inflow_weighted, no flow_limit Force the upward slack of the nodes in this group to be equal or inflow (demand) weighted transfer_method a constant use_connection_transfer_methods use_connection_transfer_methods, no_losses_no_variable_cost, regular, exact, variable_cost_only, dc_power_flow_with_angles, unidirectional network Override transfer_method for all connections within this nodeGroup. Options: use_connection_transfer_methods (default, no override), no_losses_no_variable_cost, regular, exact, variable_cost_only, unidirectional, dc_power_flow_with_angles. Setting 'unidirectional' gates every member connection to one-way flow (source → sink only). Setting 'dc_power_flow_with_angles' uses B-theta DC power flow (requires reactance on connections). use_for_representative_periods a constant no yes, no solve_advanced A flag whether this group of nodes is an aggregation unit for net-load representative-period selection. When 'yes', the representative-periods preprocessor aggregates the member nodes' net load (demand minus available VRE) into a single regional signal used for clustering; when 'no' (default) the group is ignored by that selection. If no group carries the flag, the selection falls back to per-node net-load signals.

docs.title: model
docs.text:
Settings for the whole model: which solves run and in which order, inflation, and numerical settings.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition inflation_offset_investment years a constant 0 model Offset for when investment costs occur within a year. Default 0 (beginning of year). inflation_offset_operations years a constant 0.5 model Offset for when operational costs occur within a year. Default 0.5 (middle of year). inflation_rate dimensionless a constant model e.g. 0.02 means 2% per year. Model-wide inflation rate applied to all future costs. When inputs are in real (constant-price) terms, set to 0. When inputs are in nominal terms, set to expected inflation. Default: 0 (real inputs). max_flow_for_unconstrained_variables MW a constant 1000000 model Upper bound for capacities and flows that have no other limit: how much capacity an entity with invest_method invest_no_limit or invest_retire_no_limit (or cumulative_limits without cumulative_max_capacity) can add on top of its existing capacity, and the flow on a unit's input or output whose conversion_flow_coeff is 0. The value is used as given; with several model entities the largest value is used. Keep it large enough not to limit the real solution and small enough to avoid numerical problems. Default 1,000,000. output_horizon a constant no yes, no output Debug flag. yes writes one raw parquet file per LP variable and constraint, with every row of every solve and a realized column. Normal outputs do not change. periods_available a list of values (array) model (Optional) Array of periods available for the model. Periods that are in the data, but are not in period_timeset. small_number_threshold unit of each LP coefficient a constant 0.0001 model Coefficients and right-hand-side terms whose absolute value is below this are treated as 0 when building the optimisation problem. Reduces the numerical range (conditioning) of the LP. Default 0.0001. solves a list of values (array) model Sequence of solves in the model. Array. version a constant 79 model Contains database version information.

docs.title: node
docs.text:
A point where energy is balanced: demand, supply and transfers meet there. A node can also be a storage (its state is the energy stored) or a price-setting market.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition annual_flow MWh/a a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) basics Annual flow in energy units (always positive, the sign of inflow defines in/out). Inflow time series can be scaled to match annual flow. By default, there is no scaling of inflow. Constant or period. availability dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) 1 basics e.g. 0.9 means 90%. Fraction of capacity available for storage. Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time. constraint_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MWh a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the node's storage capacity in service in each period on the left side of the user constraint (existing plus investments still in service minus retirements). Coefficient per MWh. Capacity in construction is not included. constraint_cumulative_pre_built_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MWh a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity in service at the start of each period on the left side of the user constraint. This is existing capacity plus capacity that came online in earlier periods, minus earlier retirements. Capacity coming online in the period itself is in the invested term. Coefficient per MWh. constraint_in_construction_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MWh a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the storage capacity in construction in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Capacity is in construction from the period of the investment decision until it comes online. It is zero without a construction lead time. Coefficient per MWh. constraint_invested_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MWh a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity that comes online in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Without a construction lead time, this is the capacity invested in that period. Coefficient per MWh. constraint_retired_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MWh a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the storage capacity retired in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Coefficient per MWh. constraint_state_coeff unit of the constraint per MWh a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient) to represent the participation of the storage state in user-defined constraints. [state x coefficient] will be on the left side of the equation. construction_lead_time years a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Time from the investment decision until the storage capacity starts to operate. The start is rounded to the start of a period (see construction_lead_time_method). Investments whose rounded start is after the end of the solve or the model horizon are not offered, with a warning. Constant or period. Default 0. construction_lead_time_method a constant immediate, closest_seam, previous_seam, next_seam investment How the start of operation (decision year plus construction_lead_time) is rounded to the start of a period. immediate: no lead time, the storage capacity operates from the decision period. closest_seam: the nearest period start; a tie goes to the later one. previous_seam: the period start before. next_seam: the period start after. Without a value: immediate when there is no lead time, else closest_seam. cumulative_max_capacity MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Maximum cumulative capacity (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. cumulative_min_capacity MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Minimum cumulative capacity (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. discount_rate dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) 0.05 investment e.g. 0.05 means 5% per year. Discount rate for investments (WACC). Reflects the financing cost and risk premium for this technology. When the model inflation_rate > 0, this should be a nominal rate. When inflation_rate = 0, this should be a real rate. Used to annualize investment costs over the lifetime: annuity = invest_cost x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-lifetime). 0 gives the straight-line annuity invest_cost / lifetime. No value means 0.05. Must be 0 or above. Constant or period. energy_margin_adder MWh per time step of the timeline a constant, or a map over periods (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) 0 investment per time step of the timeline. Extra demand (negative inflow) added to every time step of the investment solve, when energy_margin_method = inflow_adder. The value is not a total that is divided over the steps: each time step gets the full value. On a timeline of 24 h time steps, a margin of 10 MW needs a value of 240. When the investment solve uses new_stepduration, a solve step gets the sum of the values of the time steps it combines (a constant or period value counts once per time step). Dispatch solves are not affected. 0 = off. Constant, period or period+time. energy_margin_method a constant none none, inflow_multiplier, inflow_adder investment How the node's investment-stage energy margin is applied. 'none' (default) = off, no scaling. 'inflow_multiplier' multiplies this node's inflow by 'energy_margin_multiplier' in the solve that carries investment periods only (dispatch solves are unaffected). 'inflow_adder' instead adds 'energy_margin_adder' MWh of extra demand (negative inflow) to each time step of that same investment solve. Both offset representative-period VRE optimism that would otherwise cause underinvestment. energy_margin_multiplier dimensionless a constant 1 investment e.g. 1.1 means 10% more demand. Multiplier applied to this node's inflow in the investment solve only, when energy_margin_method = 'inflow_multiplier'. Offsets representative-period VRE optimism (rep-period average VRE availability exceeds the annual average). 1 = off. e.g. 1.1 builds ~10% more capacity to serve the true annual demand under the true (lower) annual VRE. Constant. existing MWh or count a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) basics Existing storage capacity or number of storage units. If virtual_unitsize is given, then existing is the number of units (capacity = existing × virtual_unitsize). Otherwise existing is the existing capacity of a single unit (typically in MWh). Constant or period. fixed_cost CUR/kWh/a a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Annual fixed cost for storage. New storage capacity pays it only while it operates. Constant or period. inflow MWh per time step a constant, or a map over time (1 level), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) basics per time step. Energy flowing into the node in each time step (negative is outflow, e.g. demand). The value is the energy of the whole step, not a rate: on 1 h steps it equals the average MW, and on 3 h steps it is 3 × the average MW. When the step length of your data changes, rescale the values yourself, e.g. sum hourly values to get 3 h steps, or halve MW values for 0.5 h steps. FlexTool does not convert them, and time-series values whose time names are not on the timeline are ignored. FlexTool sums the values for you only when a solve's new_stepduration coarsens the timeline, and when a group's new_stepduration balances the node per coarse step. A constant value is used as the same energy in every step. Constant, time or stochastic time. inflow_method a constant use_original no_inflow, use_original, scale_in_proportion, scale_to_annual_flow, scale_to_annual_and_peak_flow basics Choice how to treat inflow time series. Empty defaults to 'use_original', which does not scale the time series. 'no_inflow' ignores the inflow time series. 'scale_to_annual_flow' scales the inflow time series by a single factor (shape preserved) so its annual energy equals 'annual_flow'. The annualisation uses each timestep's share of the year: for a full or evenly sampled timeline this is 8760/'hours_in_solve' (every step weighted equally); for a representative timeset with 'timeset_weights', each timestep is weighted by its declared share of the year, so a biased sample of timesteps still annualises correctly. The same weighting is used for energy reporting and operating-cost accounting, so the energy the model is scaled to serve, reports, and costs all coincide. If 'timeset_weights' do not reflect the true representativeness of your selected timesteps, the scaling factor - and therefore the absolute demand level - shifts accordingly; see the per-node 'f' diagnostic (inflow_scaling_diagnostics.csv). 'scale_in_proprotion' calculates a scaling factor by dividing 'annual_flow' with the sum of time series inflow (after it has been annualized using 'timeline_duration_in_years'). (With a representative timeset, the annual-energy match uses 'timeset_weights' as above.) 'scale_to_annual_and_peak_flow' scales the time series to match the 'annual_flow' target while transforming the time series to match the highest load with the 'peak_inflow'. (With a representative timeset, the annual-energy match uses 'timeset_weights' as above; the peak match stays unweighted.) invest_cost CUR/kWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Overnight investment cost of new storage capacity. It is paid as an annuity over the years the storage capacity operates. Construction time costs with their interest must be included here. Constant or period: the value of the period when the storage capacity is built (comes online) is used. invest_forced MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Forces exactly this much new storage capacity to come online in the period, overriding the investment optimisation (as setting invest_min and invest_max equal). Constant or period. invest_max_period MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Largest allowed storage capacity coming online in each period. Existing capacity and retirements do not change it. With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_max_total MWh a constant investment Largest allowed total investment over all solves. Every investment decision counts, also reinvestments and investments that are no longer in service. Retirements and existing capacity do not reduce it. To limit the capacity in service, use cumulative_max_capacity. Constant. invest_method a constant not_allowed not_allowed, invest_no_limit, invest_period, invest_total, invest_period_total, retire_no_limit, retire_period, retire_total, retire_period_total, invest_retire_no_limit, invest_retire_period, invest_retire_total, invest_retire_period_total, cumulative_limits investment Choice of investment method: either not_allowed or then a combination of 1) investment or retirement and 2) investment limits per period, all periods (total) or no_limits. invest_min_period MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Smallest required storage capacity coming online in each period. Existing capacity and retirements do not change it. With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_min_total MWh a constant investment Smallest required total investment over all solves. Every investment decision counts, also reinvestments and investments that are no longer in service. Retirements and existing capacity do not reduce it. To limit the capacity in service, use cumulative_max_capacity. Constant. lifetime years a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Operating lifetime. It starts when the storage capacity starts to operate: with a construction lead time, after the construction. Used with the interest rate to calculate the annuity. What happens at the end of the lifetime depends on lifetime_method: reinvest_automatic keeps the storage capacity to the end of the model horizon, reinvest_choice retires it, no_investment retires it once. Required when the node invests or retires with a cost (invest_cost, salvage_value), and when lifetime_method is reinvest_choice or no_investment (also for existing capacity without investment). Constant or period. lifetime_method a constant reinvest_automatic reinvest_automatic, reinvest_choice, no_investment investment Choice how the investments behave after unit runs out of lifetime. Automatic reinvestment causes the model to keep the capacity until the end of model horizon and applies the annualized investment cost without further model choice. Choice of reinvestment removes the capacity at the end of the lifetime and the model needs to decide how much new capacity is to be built. node_type a constant balance balance_within_period, commodity, balance, storage basics Role of this node in the LP. 'commodity' = price-exposed source/sink with no balance constraint (e.g. fuel imports, no storage); 'balance' = energy balance maintained every timestep (default); 'storage' = balance plus a state variable (battery, reservoir); 'balance_within_period' = balance aggregated over the whole period (e.g. an annual gas budget). peak_inflow MWh per time step a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) basics per time step. The highest inflow of a time step that the scaled inflow should reach. Use the same scale and sign as inflow (negative for a demand). Used only with inflow_method = scale_to_annual_and_peak_flow. If you change the step length, rescale it as you rescale inflow. Each period reaches its own peak_inflow; with a solve's new_stepduration, peak_inflow is matched per original time step. Constant or period. penalty_down CUR/MWh a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) 10000 basics Penalty cost for increasing consumption in the node (excess energy). Constant, period, time, period+time, or stochastic time. penalty_method a constant regular regular, off basics Whether this node has balance penalty (unserved-energy / over-supply slack) variables. 'regular' (default) keeps the penalty_up / penalty_down slack variables that let the node balance be violated at a cost. 'off' removes those slack variables entirely, making the node balance a hard equality (the solve becomes infeasible if the node cannot balance). Use 'off' only if certain that it will not make the model infeasible (a real solution exists) - infeasible models can be very difficult to debug. At the same time, 'off' will reduce variables and can direct infeasibilities to other, more desirable, nodes. penalty_up CUR/MWh a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) 10000 basics Penalty cost for decreasing consumption in the node (energy not served). Constant, period, time, period+time, or stochastic time. retire_max_period MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Largest allowed retirement of storage capacity in each period. Counts only what is retired in that period; existing capacity and investments do not change it. Constant or period. retire_max_total MWh a constant retirement Largest allowed total retirement over all solves. Investments and existing capacity do not change it. Constant. retire_min_period MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Smallest required retirement of storage capacity in each period. Counts only what is retired in that period; existing capacity and investments do not change it. Constant or period. retire_min_total MWh a constant retirement Smallest required total retirement over all solves. Investments and existing capacity do not change it. Constant. salvage_value CUR/kWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Salvage value of the storage. Constant or period. self_discharge_loss dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) storage e.g. 0.01 means 1% per hour. Loss of stored energy over time: the content shrinks by the factor 1/(1 + loss) every hour (with 0.01, by about 0.99% per hour), decaying continuously at ln(1 + loss) per hour. Constant, period, time or period+time. storage_binding_method a constant bind_forward_only bind_within_period, bind_within_solve, bind_forward_only, bind_intraperiod_blocks, bind_within_timeblock, bind_within_solve_blended_weights, bind_within_period_blended_weights, bind_forward_only_blended_weights storage Choice how the storage state will be maintained over discontinuous timelines. Seven cycle-scope methods (the state-continuity family): 'bind_within_timeblock' cycles state within each timeblock (cycle closes at block boundaries); 'bind_within_period' cycles within each FlexTool period and chains blocks inside the period; 'bind_within_solve' cycles across the whole solve horizon; 'bind_forward_only' (default) chains state forward across the solve with no end-to-start closure; 'bind_within_solve_blended_weights' is the representative-period variant of bind_within_solve (RP weighting + solve-level cycle closure); 'bind_within_period_blended_weights' is the RP variant of bind_within_period (per-period RP weighting, each period closes independently); 'bind_forward_only_blended_weights' is the RP variant of bind_forward_only (RP weighting, no cycle closure). One additional value, 'bind_intraperiod_blocks', is structurally an aggregation method rather than a cycle-scope method: state is held constant within each block and the block-total flow is balanced at the boundary. Silent-degrade behaviour: any '*_blended_weights' method on a node in a solve whose active timeset has no representative_period_weights is automatically downgraded to the corresponding non-RP variant for that solve, so the same storage entity can drive an RP investment solve and a chronological dispatch solve back-to-back. Separate parameters (e.g. 'storage_state_start') can force additional bindings. By default, storage start state is bound to 0. In a stochastic solve each forecast branch uses the representative periods of its period, and the blended_weights methods work per branch. In a rolling_window solve on representative periods the blended_weights methods are not applied: those nodes bind forward only (bind_forward_only), with a warning. storage_nested_fix_method a constant fix_nothing fix_nothing, fix_quantity, fix_price, fix_usage storage Used in nested solve sequences. Set this storage as a long term storage, which end state is passed to the lower level solves as a target. Fix_price requires storage_state_reference_price storage_solve_horizon_method a constant free free, use_reference_value, use_reference_price storage Choice how to treat storage state at the end of time horizon of each solve. 'free' lets the model choose the end state. 'use_reference_value' forces the end state to the specific value set in 'storage_state_reference_value'. 'use_reference_price' gives the storage state a price in the objective function based on the 'storage_state_reference_price'. storage_start_end_method a constant fix_nothing fix_start, fix_end, fix_start_end, fix_nothing storage Whether the storage state is fixed at the start and/or end of the whole model. fix_nothing (default): not fixed. fix_start, fix_end and fix_start_end use storage_state_start and storage_state_end, which must then have a value. storage_state_end dimensionless a constant storage 0-1, share of the storage capacity. Storage state at the end of the last solve, as a share of the storage capacity. Needed by fix_end and fix_start_end. Constant. storage_state_reference_price CUR/MWh a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) storage Price for the stored energy at the end of the solve horizon. Requires 'use_reference_price' in 'storage_solve_horizon_method'. Constant or period. storage_state_reference_value dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) storage 0-1, share of the storage capacity. Relative state of storage at then end of each solve (can be overwritten in the next solve). Requires 'use_reference_value' in 'storage_solve_horizon_method'. Constant, period, time or period+time. storage_state_start dimensionless a constant storage 0-1, share of the storage capacity.
