Storage state at the start of the first solve, as a share of the storage capacity. Needed by fix_start and fix_start_end. Constant. unit_of_measure a constant MWh basics Unit of measure of this node's amounts, e.g. m3, t, MWh_th (default MWh). A label only: FlexTool converts nothing. Flows into and out of the node, and the capacity of a unit whose output is this node (of a connection when both of its nodes have this unit), are rates in this unit per hour (MWh → MW, m3 → m3/h); storage state, storage capacity and inflow per time step are amounts (m3); annual results are per year (m3/a); prices and penalty_up/down are CUR per this unit. The per-kW costs (invest_cost, fixed_cost, salvage_value) of a unit whose capacity is in this unit, and the per-kWh costs of this node's storage, are per 0.001 of the rate or amount: 500 CUR per m3/h of capacity is entered as 0.5, and 20 CUR per m3 of storage as 0.02. An efficiency into or out of this node is output units per input unit (e.g. m3/MWh). virtual_unitsize MWh a constant basics Size of one unit. With it, existing is the number of units. Investments and retirements are continuous; their limits are in MWh. No value: the existing capacity, or 1000 MWh without it.

docs.title: profile
docs.text:
A time series of shares of capacity (for example wind or solar capacity factors), used as an upper limit, a lower limit or a fixed value for a flow or a storage state.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition profile dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) basics e.g. 0.3 means 30% of capacity. Profile values, e.g. the availability of wind power (capacity factor). Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time.

docs.title: solve
docs.text:
One optimisation run inside the model: its periods and time steps, whether it decides investments or dispatch, rolling or stochastic settings, and solver options.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition benders_in_out_weight dimensionless a constant 0 solve_advanced Benders decomposition: in-out separation stabilization weight (lambda) in f_sep = lambdacentre + (1-lambda)f_out. 0.0 (default) = off (exact Benders); values in (0,1) turn it on, larger = more stabilization. Only used when decomposition = 'benders'. Default 0.0. benders_max_iter count a constant 50 solve_advanced Benders decomposition: maximum number of outer (master/subproblem) iterations. Only used when decomposition = 'benders'. Default 50. benders_tolerance dimensionless a constant 0.001 solve_advanced Benders decomposition: relative optimality-gap tolerance (best_UB - LB)/|best_UB| for convergence of the outer loop. Only used when decomposition = 'benders'. Default 0.001. contains_solves a constant, or a list of values (array) solve_advanced Array of solves - used for nested solve sequencesArray of solves - used for nested solve sequences decomposition a constant none none, benders solve_advanced Decomposition scheme for this solve. 'none' (default) solves monolithically. 'benders' runs the solve through the Benders region-decomposition driver (a master trade layer coordinating per-region recourse subproblems via appended optimality cuts, producing a valid lower bound) over the groups whose group.decomposition_method is 'benders_regional' (requires at least two such region groups). The choice is per solve, so an investment solve can decompose while a later dispatch solve in the same chain stays monolithic. dispatch_realization_method a constant within_solve within_solve, separate_dispatch solve_advanced How the committed part of a stochastic solve is realized. within_solve (default): a realized: yes branch gets a realization solve automatically. separate_dispatch: always runs a separate realized dispatch solve; needs a realized: yes branch (error otherwise). fix_storage_periods a list of values (array), or a map with 2 index levels solve_advanced Array of periods where the storage_values are fixed when the node has storage_include_solve_fix_method is set invest_periods a list of values (array), or a map with 2 index levels solve_basics Array of periods in which investments can be decided. With a construction lead time, the capacity comes online later. new_stepduration hours a constant timeline Creates a new timeline from the old for this solve with this timestep duration. The new timeline sums inflow over the time steps that form each new time step (a constant inflow counts once per time step it combines) and averages the other time series (e.g. profile) over them, weighted by their durations. The new_stepduration must be a whole multiple of the timeline's time steps (on a timeline with time steps of different lengths, every new time step must end where a time step of the timeline ends); FlexTool stops with an error otherwise. period_timeset a map: period name → timeset name (1 level) solve_basics Map of periods with associated timesets that will be included in the solve. Index: period name, value: timeset name. realized_invest_periods a list of values (array), or a map with 2 index levels solve_advanced Array of the periods that will realize the investment decisions. If not used when the invest_periods exist. The realized_periods are used to realize invests as well realized_periods a list of values (array), or a map with 2 index levels solve_basics Array of periods that will be realized in the solve. reduce_system_detail_method a constant none none, reserves, inertia, non_synchronous, inertia_non_synchronous, reserves_inertia_non_synchronous, dc_power_flow, reserves_inertia_non_synchronous_dc_power_flow solve_advanced System detail that this solve leaves out, to make it faster. none (default): all detail. reserves: no reserve requirements. inertia: no inertia limits. non_synchronous: no non-synchronous share limits. dc_power_flow: the lines of dc_power_flow_with_angles groups are lossless transport limited by their capacity (no angles). A combination leaves out each named part. The capacity margin is always kept. reduce_unit_detail_method a constant none none, integers, integers_ramps, integers_min_limits, integers_ramps_min_limits, online, online_ramps solve_advanced Detail of units and connections that this solve leaves out, to make it faster (typically an investment solve). none (default): all detail. integers: binary startup_method is solved as continuous and exact connections behave as regular. integers_ramps: integers, and no ramp limits or ramp costs. integers_min_limits: integers, and no min_load, capacity_min_coeff floors or minimum up / down times. integers_ramps_min_limits: integers, no ramps and no min limits. Under the integers levels, a unit or connection whose online variables nothing in the solve still uses (no start-up cost, min_load, capacity_min_coeff floor, minimum up / down time, min_load_efficiency curve, constraint_online_coeff in a user constraint, reserve, inertia or ramp limit left) has none, as with startup_method no_startup; the run log names them. online: everything of integers_min_limits, and no online variables: no start-up costs, user constraints that count units online are left out whole, min_load_efficiency units use their full-load efficiency (less fuel than the curve at part load), and ramp limits apply to the capacity. Reserves are then limited by built capacity, not online capacity, and inertia is counted from flows. online_ramps: online, and no ramp limits or ramp costs. Never adds detail. rolling_duration hours a constant solve_advanced Optional. Duration of rolling, if not stated, assumed to be the whole timeline of the solve rolling_solve_horizon hours a constant solve_advanced Required if rolling_window solve. How long into the future the roll sees rolling_solve_jump hours a constant solve_advanced Required if rolling_window solve. Interval between the start points of the rolls. Should be smaller than the horizon scaling a constant full off, solver_only, basic, full solve_advanced Numerical scaling of this solve's LP. full (default): FlexTool rescales variables, constraints and costs and sets the solver's scaling. basic: no per-quantity rescaling. solver_only: only the solver's own scaling. off: no scaling at all. Try basic or solver_only if a solve fails numerically. The --scaling run option overrides it. shared_invest_periods a list of values (array) solve_advanced Periods where investments are the same in every stochastic branch (with recourse). No value or empty array: none. shared_operation_periods a list of values (array) solve_advanced Periods where operations are the same in every stochastic branch. No value: the committed time steps. Empty array: none. solve_mode a constant single_solve single_solve, rolling_window solve_basics A single_solve or rolling_window for a set of rolling optimisation windows solved in a sequence. solver a constant highs highs, gurobi, cplex, xpress, copt solve_advanced Solver to use for this solve. One of polar-high's available_solvers ('highs', 'gurobi', 'cplex', 'xpress', 'copt'). HiGHS is the bundled default; commercial solvers require a separate install and license. solver_arguments a map: option name → value (1 level) solve_advanced Map of HiGHS solver options (option name -> value), layered on top of the floor values in solver_config/highs.opt and below any CLI overrides (e.g. --solver-time-limit). Use this for ad-hoc HiGHS knobs that do not have a dedicated FlexTool parameter (solver_mip_gap). solver_mip_gap dimensionless a constant solve_advanced Relative MIP optimality gap at which the solver may stop early. Normalised across solvers by polar-high. None = solver default. solver_precommand a constant solve_advanced Not used: FlexTool never runs this command. Kept only so that older databases still read. stochastic_branches dimensionless a map: period, branch, analysis_time, realized → probability weight (4 levels) solve_advanced Forecast branches of the solve (map: period, branch, analysis_time, realized → probability weight). Weights are normalised per start time. At most one branch per start time may be realized: yes. That branch is not a weighted forecast; it adds a realization solve over the committed time steps. Without it, the solve reports investments only. stochastic_invest_method a constant none none, recourse solve_advanced How stochastic branches invest. none (default): one shared investment plan for all branches. recourse: each branch also invests at and after its branching period. timeline_hole_multiplier dimensionless a constant 1 solve_advanced Multiplier applied to the inverse-step-duration term in nodeBalance_eq and storage-binding constraints across timeline gaps (holes). Tunes how strongly state differences are penalised across discontinuities in the timeline. Default 1.0 mirrors the .mod default and matches pre-v44 Python-convention behaviour. years_represented years a map: period → years (1 level) solve_basics Map to indicate how many years the period represents before the next period in the solve. Used for discounting. Can be below one (multiple periods in one year). Index: period, value: years.

docs.title: timeline
docs.text:
The time steps of the input data and the duration of each.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition timestep_duration hours a map: time step name → time step duration in hours (1 level) timeline Map of time steps in the timeline. Index: time step name, value: time step duration in hours.

docs.title: timeset
docs.text:
A selection of time steps of a timeline that a solve uses (all of them, or for example representative weeks).

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition representative_period_weights dimensionless a map: base period start timestep, representative period start timestep → weight (2 levels) solve_advanced Representative-period weighting map (rank-2 nested Map: base period start timestep -> representative period start timestep -> weight). Created by the representative-periods preprocess tool; declares how much each representative period stands in for each base period. Its presence enables RP-aware storage-binding ('*_blended_weights'); its absence silently downgrades those methods to the non-RP behaviour. Mutually exclusive with 'timeset_weights' on the same timeset. The forecast branches of a stochastic solve use the representative periods of their period. timeline a constant timeline The name of the timeline that the timeset uses. (String) timeset_duration count of time steps a map: name of the timestep that starts the timeset → duration of the block in timesteps (1 level) timeline Index: name of the timestep that starts the timeset, value: duration of the block in timesteps. Defines the selection: which timesteps are in the solve and how many (this sets 'hours_in_solve'). Representativeness - each timestep's share of the year - is set separately by 'timeset_weights'. timeset_weights dimensionless a map over time (1 level) timeline Weight of each time step (map, index time). Weights how much each step counts in costs, energy and demand scaling. Normalised per period. Forecast branches use the weights of their period. Other shapes are an error. Cannot be set on a timeset that also has representative_period_weights (error).

docs.title: unit
docs.text:
A plant or device that turns inputs into outputs: a power plant, a wind or solar farm, an electrolyser, a heat pump, a battery inverter.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition availability dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) 1 basics e.g. 0.9 means 90%. Fraction of capacity available for flows from/to the unit. For online units, the online variable is multiplied by the availability. Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time. constraint_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the unit's capacity in service in each period on the left side of the user constraint (existing plus investments still in service minus retirements). Coefficient per MW. Capacity in construction is not included. constraint_cumulative_pre_built_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity in service at the start of each period on the left side of the user constraint. This is existing capacity plus capacity that came online in earlier periods, minus earlier retirements. Capacity coming online in the period itself is in the invested term. Coefficient per MW. constraint_in_construction_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity in construction in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Capacity is in construction from the period of the investment decision until it comes online. It is zero without a construction lead time. Coefficient per MW. constraint_invested_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity that comes online in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Without a construction lead time, this is the capacity invested in that period. Coefficient per MW. constraint_online_coeff unit of the constraint per unit online a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the number of units online in each time step on the left side of the user constraint. One unit is virtual_unitsize; without it, the largest existing capacity, else 1000 MW (set virtual_unitsize when the capacity is invested). Needs online variables (startup_method linear or binary, or a minimum_time_method); a coefficient without them is an error. With linear startup the number is continuous. For MW online, use the unit size (MW per unit) as the coefficient. constraint_retired_capacity_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient). Puts the capacity retired in each period on the left side of the user constraint. Coefficient per MW. construction_lead_time years a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Time from the investment decision until the capacity starts to operate. The start is rounded to the start of a period (see construction_lead_time_method). Investments whose rounded start is after the end of the solve or the model horizon are not offered, with a warning. Constant or period. Default 0. construction_lead_time_method a constant immediate, closest_seam, previous_seam, next_seam investment How the start of operation (decision year plus construction_lead_time) is rounded to the start of a period. immediate: no lead time, the capacity operates from the decision period. closest_seam: the nearest period start; a tie goes to the later one. previous_seam: the period start before. next_seam: the period start after. Without a value: immediate when there is no lead time, else closest_seam. conversion_method a constant constant_efficiency constant_efficiency, min_load_efficiency, none basics Choice of conversion method. cumulative_max_capacity MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Maximum cumulative capacity (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. cumulative_min_capacity MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Minimum cumulative capacity (considers existing, invested and retired capacity). Constant or period. delay hours a constant, or a map with 1 index level tech_advanced A time delay between the input nodes and the output nodes. Either a constant indicating the time difference in hours or a map of time differences (index: time difference in hours, value: weight). Each weight indicates its share of the original flow and the weights should sum to 1. Requires that the time resolutions in the model are always integer multiples of these time differences. discount_rate dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) 0.05 investment e.g. 0.05 means 5% per year. Discount rate for investments (WACC). Reflects the financing cost and risk premium for this technology. When the model inflation_rate > 0, this should be a nominal rate. When inflation_rate = 0, this should be a real rate. Used to annualize investment costs over the lifetime: annuity = invest_cost x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-lifetime). 0 gives the straight-line annuity invest_cost / lifetime. No value means 0.05. Must be 0 or above. Constant or period. efficiency dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) 1 basics Efficiency of the unit at full load: outputs / inputs, each flow weighted by its conversion_flow_coeff (default 1, giving plain sum of outputs / sum of inputs). May be above 1: a heat pump with COP 3 has 3; a unit whose output is measured in another unit of measure (e.g. m³ of water per MWh of electricity) uses that ratio. A min_load_efficiency unit can have different efficiency below full load (see efficiency_at_min_load). No effect on a unit without inputs or without outputs. Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time. efficiency_at_min_load dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels) basics Output / input at minimum load, like efficiency (e.g. 0.4; may be above 1). Efficiency of a min_load_efficiency unit at its minimum load. Fuel use is a straight line from minimum load (this efficiency) to full load (efficiency). Has no effect when min_load is 0: the efficiency at zero output is not defined. No value: efficiency applies at minimum load too. Constant, period, time or period+time. existing MW or count a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) basics Existing capacity or number of units. If virtual_unitsize is given, then existing is the number of units (capacity = existing × virtual_unitsize). Otherwise existing is the existing capacity of a single unit (typically in MW). Constant or period. fixed_cost CUR/kW/a a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Annual fixed cost. New capacity pays it only while it operates. Constant or period. invest_cost CUR/kW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Overnight investment cost of new capacity. It is paid as an annuity over the years the capacity operates. Construction time costs with their interest must be included here. Constant or period: the value of the period when the capacity is built (comes online) is used. invest_max_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Largest allowed capacity coming online in each period. Existing capacity and retirements do not change it. With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_max_total MW a constant investment Largest allowed total investment over all solves. Every investment decision counts, also reinvestments and investments that are no longer in service. Retirements and existing capacity do not reduce it. To limit the capacity in service, use cumulative_max_capacity. Constant. invest_method a constant not_allowed not_allowed, invest_no_limit, invest_period, invest_total, invest_period_total, retire_no_limit, retire_period, retire_total, retire_period_total, invest_retire_no_limit, invest_retire_period, invest_retire_total, invest_retire_period_total, cumulative_limits investment Choice of investment method: not_allowed, invest and retire indicate availability of investment and retirement. no_limit removes all limits even if there are limiting values set. period uses values set in invest/retire_max/min_period. total uses values set in invest/retire_max/min_total. invest_min_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Smallest required capacity coming online in each period. Existing capacity and retirements do not change it. With a construction lead time, the investment is decided earlier. Constant or period. invest_min_total MW a constant investment Smallest required total investment over all solves. Every investment decision counts, also reinvestments and investments that are no longer in service. Retirements and existing capacity do not reduce it. To limit the capacity in service, use cumulative_max_capacity. Constant. lifetime years a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) investment Operating lifetime. It starts when the capacity starts to operate: with a construction lead time, after the construction. Used with the interest rate to calculate the annuity. What happens at the end of the lifetime depends on lifetime_method: reinvest_automatic keeps the capacity to the end of the model horizon, reinvest_choice retires it, no_investment retires it once. Required when the unit invests or retires with a cost (invest_cost, salvage_value), and when lifetime_method is reinvest_choice or no_investment (also for existing capacity without investment). Constant or period. lifetime_method a constant reinvest_automatic reinvest_automatic, reinvest_choice, no_investment investment Choice how the investments behave after unit runs out of lifetime. Automatic reinvestment causes the model to keep the capacity until the end of model horizon and applies the annualized investment cost without further model choice. Choice of reinvestment removes the capacity at the end of the lifetime and the model needs to decide how much new capacity is to be built. min_downtime hours a constant tech_advanced Minimum time the unit stays offline after a stop. Needs minimum_time_method. The look-back stops at a gap in the timeline and at the first step of a solve. Constant. min_load dimensionless a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) basics 0-1, share of the online capacity. Minimum load of the unit as a share of its online capacity. Applies only if the unit has online variables. No value means 0. Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time. min_uptime hours a constant tech_advanced Minimum time the unit stays online after a start. Needs minimum_time_method. The look-back stops at a gap in the timeline and at the first step of a solve. Constant. minimum_time_method a constant min_uptime, min_downtime, both, none tech_advanced Choice between minimum up- and downtimes (none, min_downtime, min_uptime, both). Setting this to anything other than 'none' will activate online variables (at least linear) for the unit. Default: none (no minimum time constraints). retire_max_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Largest allowed retirement in each period. Counts only what is retired in that period; existing capacity and investments do not change it. Constant or period. retire_max_total MW a constant retirement Largest allowed total retirement over all solves. Investments and existing capacity do not change it. Constant. retire_min_period MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Smallest required retirement in each period. Counts only what is retired in that period; existing capacity and investments do not change it. Constant or period. retire_min_total MW a constant retirement Smallest required total retirement over all solves. Investments and existing capacity do not change it. Constant. salvage_value CUR/kW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) retirement Salvage value of the unit. Constant or period. startup_cost CUR/MW a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) tech_advanced Cost of starting up one MW of capacity. Constant or period. startup_method a constant no_startup no_startup, linear, binary tech_advanced Whether the unit has online variables. linear: any share of the capacity can be online. binary: whole units only (slower to solve). Online status links to the previous time step; that link stops at a gap in the timeline. virtual_unitsize MW a constant basics Size of one unit. With it, existing is the number of units. Binary startups commit whole units of this size. Investments and retirements are continuous; their limits are in MW. No value: the existing capacity, or 1000 MW without it.

docs.title: connection__node
docs.text:
The flow between a connection and one of its nodes (for user constraints).

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition constraint_flow_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient) to represent the participation of the flow from the connection to a node in user-defined constraints. [flow x coefficient] will be on the left side of the equation.

docs.title: connection__profile
docs.text:
Applies a profile as a limit on the flow of a connection.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition profile_method a constant none upper_limit, lower_limit, fixed, none basics Choice of profile method (upper_limit, lower_limit, fixed). Negative values also possible.

docs.title: node__profile
docs.text:
Applies a profile as a limit on the storage state of a node.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition profile_method a constant none upper_limit, lower_limit, fixed, none basics Choice of profile method (upper_limit, lower_limit, fixed). Negative values also possible.

docs.title: unit__inputNode
docs.text:
An input of a unit: the node it takes energy or fuel from, and the properties of that flow (costs, coefficients, ramping).

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition constraint_flow_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient) to represent the participation of the flow between unit and node in user-defined constraints. [flow x coefficient] will be on the left side of the equation. conversion_flow_coeff dimensionless a constant 1 basics default 1. Fuel-equivalent energy per unit of this flow. It enters the unit's conversion equation, not the node balance. Applies to simple units too. 0 takes the flow out of the capacity, ramp and minimum load limits. inertia_constant MWs/MW a constant network Inertia constant for a synchronously connected unit to this node. Constant. input_share_max dimensionless a constant 1 basics default 1. Largest share of the unit's full-load input energy (flow x conversion_flow_coeff) that this input may supply, relative to the unit's capacity (existing + invested - retired) times availability. 1 = this input alone can run the unit at full output (no effective limit); e.g. two inputs with 0.6 each can each supply at most 60% of the full-load input, so full output needs both. A lower-energy input is handled by its conversion_flow_coeff, not here. For a unit without outputs: fraction of the unit's capacity available to this input. Not applied to inputs with conversion_flow_coeff = 0. input_share_min dimensionless a constant 0 basics default 0. While the unit is running, the smallest share of the unit's current input energy (flow x conversion_flow_coeff) that this input must supply. 0 = no minimum. The shares of a unit's inputs may not sum above 1, and a share may not exceed the input's input_share_max. Setting it on every input with shares summing to 1 fixes the blend. Not applied to inputs with conversion_flow_coeff = 0. is_non_synchronous a constant no yes, no network Chooses whether the unit is synchronously connected to this node. other_operational_cost CUR/MWh a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) basics Other operational variable cost for energy flows. Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time. ramp_cost CUR/MW a constant tech_advanced Cost per MW of change in the step-average flow, up or down, between a time step and the step before it. Charged per change, independent of step length. Needs ramp_method ramp_cost or both. Constant. On a constant_efficiency unit with one input and one output, an input-side ramp cost prices the change of the unit's output flow. ramp_method a constant none ramp_limit, ramp_cost, both, none tech_advanced Choice of ramp method. ramp_limit limits the ramp speed. ramp_cost charges every change in the flow between consecutive time steps. both adds the limit as well. ramp_speed_down share of capacity per minute a constant tech_advanced Largest decrease of the flow between two time steps. No limit across a gap in the timeline. Constant. ramp_speed_up share of capacity per minute a constant tech_advanced Largest increase of the flow between two time steps. No limit across a gap in the timeline. Constant. startup_energy MWh per MW started a constant, or a map over periods (1 level) tech_advanced Energy taken from this input node per MW of capacity started up (start-ups x unit size). Used with startup_input_method startup_and_input or startup_only. Constant or period. startup_input_method a constant just_input just_input, startup_and_input, startup_only tech_advanced What the input arc supplies. just_input (default): the normal input flow. startup_and_input: the normal input flow, and each start-up of the unit also takes startup_energy x MW started from this node. startup_only: only the start-up energy; the arc has no flow and takes no part in the conversion, the capacity, input shares or ramps. The start-up input can be fuel (oil to start a coal unit), heat (from the tank of a CSP plant) or electricity. Needs online variables (startup_method linear or binary, or a minimum_time_method). The start-up input is priced as the node's commodity, counts in CO2 prices and caps and is dropped with the start-ups by reduce_unit_detail_method online. It is not part of constraint_flow_coeff, flow groups or the capacity margin.

docs.title: unit__outputNode
docs.text:
An output of a unit: the node it delivers to, and the properties of that flow (costs, coefficients, ramping).

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition capacity_max_coeff dimensionless a constant 1 basics default 1. Fraction of the unit's capacity (existing + invested - retired) available to this edge's upper cap (maxToSink / maxFromSource / ramp). 0 is a zero cap; to remove the edge from the capacity constraints altogether use conversion_flow_coeff = 0. For extraction CHP set to 1.0 on each output so each can reach full capacity when the other drops. capacity_min_coeff dimensionless a constant 0 basics default 0. Optional extra floor on this output of a unit with several outputs: while the unit is online, this output must be at least capacity_min_coeff x min_load x the online capacity. The unit's minimum load (min_load) applies once, to the sum of its outputs, and is not scaled by this coefficient. 0 = no separate floor on this output. Range 0..1. constraint_flow_coeff unit of the constraint per MW a map: constraint name → coefficient (1 level) constraint A map of coefficients (Index: constraint name, value: coefficient) to represent the participation of the flow between unit and node in user-defined constraints. [flow x coefficient] will be on the left side of the equation. conversion_flow_coeff dimensionless a constant 1 basics default 1. Fuel-equivalent energy per unit of this flow. It enters the unit's conversion equation, not the node balance. Applies to simple units too. 0 takes the flow out of the capacity, ramp and minimum load limits. inertia_constant MWs/MW a constant network Inertia constant for a synchronously connected unit to this node. Constant. is_non_synchronous a constant no yes, no network Chooses whether the unit is synchronously connected to this node. other_operational_cost CUR/MWh a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) basics Other operational variable cost for energy flows. Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time. ramp_cost CUR/MW a constant tech_advanced Cost per MW of change in the step-average flow, up or down, between a time step and the step before it. Charged per change, independent of step length. Needs ramp_method ramp_cost or both. Constant. On a constant_efficiency unit with one input and one output, an input-side ramp cost prices the change of the unit's output flow. ramp_method a constant none ramp_limit, ramp_cost, both, none tech_advanced Choice of ramp method. ramp_limit limits the ramp speed. ramp_cost charges every change in the flow between consecutive time steps. both adds the limit as well. ramp_speed_down share of capacity per minute a constant tech_advanced Largest decrease of the flow between two time steps. No limit across a gap in the timeline. Constant. ramp_speed_up share of capacity per minute a constant tech_advanced Largest increase of the flow between two time steps. No limit across a gap in the timeline. Constant.

docs.title: reserve__upDown__group
docs.text:
The reserve requirement of a group of nodes, for one reserve and direction.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition increase_reserve_ratio dimensionless a constant reserve Only for dynamic reserve methods. The requirement grows by this ratio times the demand of the group's nodes in each step (MW, real demand). Constant. penalty_reserve CUR/MW per hour a constant 5000 reserve Penalty for each MW of reserve shortfall (the reserve requirement of the group is soft). Constant. Default 5000 - applied to every reserve group that has no value of its own. reservation MW a constant, or a map over periods or over time (1 level), or a map over periods and time (2 levels), or a stochastic-time map (branch, analysis_time, time; 3 levels) reserve Amount of reserve to be reserved. Constant, period, time, period+time or stochastic time. reserve_duration hours a constant reserve Time span over which committed reserve power must be sustainable from storage. Energy obligation = reservation_MW × reserve_duration, corrected by the reserve provider's efficiency. Only affects reserve provided by units/connections that draw on (up) or charge (down) a storage node. Absent or 0 means no storage-energy coupling. Constant. reserve_method a constant no_reserve no_reserve, timeseries_only, dynamic_only, large_failure_only, timeseries_and_dynamic, timeseries_and_large_failure, dynamic_and_large_failure, all reserve Choice of reserve method: no_reserve, timeseries_only, dynamic_only, large_failure_only or their combinations. Dynamic and large_failure requirements need no separate reservation.

docs.title: unit__node__profile
docs.text:
Applies a profile as a limit on the flow of a unit to or from a node.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition profile_method a constant upper_limit upper_limit, lower_limit, fixed, none basics Choice of profile method (upper_limit, lower_limit, fixed). Negative values also possible.

docs.title: reserve__upDown__connection__node
docs.text:
Lets a connection provide a reserve, in one direction, to a node.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition increase_reserve_ratio dimensionless a constant reserve The reserve requirement grows by this ratio times the flow between the connection and the node, in either direction, for upward and downward reserve alike. Constant. is_enabled a constant yes yes, no reserve Whether the entity is enabled. Set to 'no' to disable without deleting the entity. Constant. large_failure_ratio dimensionless a constant reserve With a large_failure method, the reserve must cover the loss of this connection's flow times this ratio. Its own reserve does not count. Constant. max_share dimensionless a constant reserve Largest share of the connection's built capacity that can be held as this reserve at this node. Constant. reliability dimensionless a constant 1 reserve The share of the reservation that is counted to reserves (sometimes reserve sources are not fully trusted). Constant.

docs.title: reserve__upDown__unit__node
docs.text:
Lets a unit provide a reserve, in one direction, to a node.

parameter unit allowed shapes default allowed values group definition increase_reserve_ratio dimensionless a constant reserve The reserve requirement grows by this ratio times the flow between the unit and the node, for upward and downward reserve alike. At an input node, the flow is what the unit draws. Constant. is_enabled a constant yes yes, no reserve Whether the entity is enabled. Set to 'no' to disable without deleting the entity. Constant. large_failure_ratio dimensionless a constant reserve With a large_failure method, the reserve must cover the loss of this unit's flow times this ratio. Its own reserve does not count. Constant. max_share dimensionless a constant reserve Largest share of the unit's built capacity at this node that can be held as this reserve. At an input node, the capacity is the unit's full-load input there. Without a value the unit offers no reserve. Constant. reliability dimensionless a constant 1 reserve The share of the reservation that is counted to reserves (sometimes reserve sources are not fully trusted). Constant.
